obligations.work: Maintain dependency/security updates, backup restore drills and platform end-of-support policy.
obligations.acceptance: Supported releases receive fixes; users get compatible migration/export routes before a channel is retired.

obligations.work: Refresh roadmap from measured architect outcomes and postmortems.
obligations.acceptance: New work maps to evidence and existing scope owners; roadmap maintenance never reclassifies an unverified capability as shipped.

phases.title: Cloud identity, tenancy and commercial services

obligations.work: Implement the API beyond its current stub with authentication/session recovery, account settings and tenant/project permissions.
obligations.acceptance: Cross-tenant object access, revocation, expired tokens and anonymous routes fail closed; offline local authoring remains useful.

obligations.work: Build object storage, semantic snapshot upload, jobs, rate limits, idempotency and regional/retention controls.
obligations.acceptance: Resumable transfer, retry, deletion and restore tests preserve identity and prevent duplicates or leaked project data.

obligations.work: Add hosted billing/entitlements only if paid cloud is selected.
obligations.acceptance: Signed idempotent webhooks, cancellation, grace periods, refunds and quota boundaries cannot trap local project files.

obligations.work: Qualify backups, disaster recovery, load, abuse/cost controls and on-call ownership.
obligations.acceptance: Restore drills meet approved RPO/RTO; capacity and service-cost measurements precede promises or public SLAs.

obligations.work: Use one staged import/export fidelity report for preserved, approximated, flattened, omitted and opaque-preserved content.
obligations.acceptance: Source file, version, unit/origin transform and losses are inspectable before canonical commit.

obligations.work: Ship the declared DXF linework import/export subset with layer/style, units and coordinate reconciliation.
obligations.acceptance: Representative external corpus files compare with independent readers; unsupported entities never disappear without a report.

obligations.work: Wire IFC viewing, property inspection and bounded coordination over existing adapters.
obligations.acceptance: Large/corrupt/mixed-unit models respect resource limits; IFC viewing is not marketed as full IFC authoring.

obligations.work: Test cancel/retry/memory pressure and all export deliveries from current revision.
obligations.acceptance: Failed import cannot replace the open model; failed download cannot report success; reversible staging and provenance survive supported workflows.

obligations.work: Implement review snapshots/share links with scope, expiry, revocation and viewer permissions.
obligations.acceptance: Server-side enforcement prevents stale links, previews and cache paths from exposing revoked projects.

obligations.work: Anchor comments/issues to explicit project revision and stable semantic references.
obligations.acceptance: Deleted/changed objects and inaccessible snapshots have honest stale/missing states rather than silently moving anchors.

obligations.work: Provide semantic revision comparison and review resolution with accessible navigation.
obligations.acceptance: Differences represent supported model/document changes and distinguish missing data from unchanged data.

obligations.work: Prove offline reconnect, duplicated events, account removal and restore.
obligations.acceptance: Review cannot silently become concurrent authoring; local copies and cloud shared snapshots have clear ownership and durability states.

phases.title: Read-only Agent, proposals and Review Centre

obligations.work: Wire the existing governed MCP host to explicit project/revision context, scoped grants, expiry and revocation.
obligations.acceptance: Read-only explain/query is product-reachable without granting hidden file paths, database queries or mutation tools.

obligations.work: Build proposal objects with intent, assumptions, affected IDs, validation, source provenance, cost and predicted document impact.
obligations.acceptance: Ambiguous requests ask for bounded inputs or produce a clearly marked proposal; uncertainty is not invented geometry.

obligations.work: Integrate Review Centre diff and Plan/3D/document highlights with usable keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
obligations.acceptance: The user can inspect what will change before approval and identify the exact revision being reviewed.

obligations.work: Handle streaming, cancel, timeout, interrupted provider runs and grant loss.
obligations.acceptance: Failures preserve the model, partial output cannot look committed, and private project data stays inside the approved data policy.

phases.title: Approved Agent actions, Skills and adversarial evaluation

obligations.work: Apply approved proposals through the canonical validation/operation/persistence path with revision checks and grouped undo.
obligations.acceptance: Stale, unauthorised or partially invalid plans fail closed; applied changes publish/reopen and undo as a coherent operation group.

obligations.work: Version reusable Skills with capability requirements, input schema, review level and provenance.
obligations.acceptance: Revoked/incompatible Skills are refused; execution remains auditable and no arbitrary script bypasses typed operations.

obligations.work: Build task, regression and red-team evaluations for ambiguous intent, prompt injection, destructive scope and cost exhaustion.
obligations.acceptance: Acceptance measures task success, invalid-action refusal, semantic fidelity and reversibility, not just fluent responses.

obligations.work: Run real supported client sessions and integrate support/kill switches.
obligations.acceptance: An external AI client can complete an approved bounded architectural change under the same grant, review and recovery contract as the native UI.

phases.title: ARQ Connect and first external host

obligations.work: Define Host Adapter SDK with document identity/revision, context, capabilities, typed tools, transactions, undo and result verification.
obligations.acceptance: The host file remains authoritative; generic screen automation cannot claim semantic CAD control.

obligations.work: Run a host bake-off across requested candidate ecosystems using current APIs, licences and user workflows.
obligations.acceptance: Connector 0 is selected from evidence and distribution/support feasibility; no Revit/Rhino/SketchUp/AutoCAD/Blender/Archicad parity promise by assumption.

obligations.work: Implement one useful read and reviewed reversible write workflow with host-native undo.
obligations.acceptance: Wrong-document, stale-document, permission denial, crash and mid-command document switch fail safely.

obligations.work: Package installer/update/uninstall, host-version compatibility, diagnostics and connector conformance tests.
obligations.acceptance: A clean supported machine can install, perform the protected action, roll back and remove the connector without damaging host documents.

phases.title: Advanced documentation and controlled professional exchange

obligations.work: Add door/window/room schedules with stable properties and live revision binding.
obligations.acceptance: Rows reconcile with canonical entities and units; edits, deletes and type changes invalidate schedules predictably.

obligations.work: Qualify bounded sections/elevations with cuts, visibility and annotation rules.
obligations.acceptance: Independent reference drawings verify geometry and dimension consistency; unsupported constructions are reported.

obligations.work: Implement a controlled IFC export subset, classification mappings and loss reports.
obligations.acceptance: External-tool validation and representative round trips show the supported boundary without promising full BIM authoring fidelity.

obligations.work: Expand sheet sets, revision tables, document issue/publish and printing only through accepted scope decisions.
obligations.acceptance: Issued output has immutable revision provenance and reissued documents cannot silently reuse stale render caches.

obligations.work: Create saved camera/view and output provenance for materials, lighting, environment and presentation.
obligations.acceptance: Each result records project revision, camera and settings and becomes stale when the relevant model changes.

obligations.work: Separate strict-geometry visualisation from creative imagery in UI and data.
obligations.acceptance: Geometry-preserving modes pass measured fidelity tests; creative results never become authoritative geometry.

obligations.work: Implement provider/renderer cancellation, privacy, budget limits and failure recovery.
obligations.acceptance: A failed or expensive run cannot mutate the project or leave unexplained charges/cost consumption.

obligations.work: Deliver presentation boards/walkthroughs with export and accessibility requirements.
obligations.acceptance: Outputs are supportable and reproducible enough to diagnose; user studies demonstrate value beyond attractive demo images.

phases.title: Firm standards, libraries and precedent knowledge

obligations.work: Create versioned templates, types/material libraries and firm standards with explicit apply/update operations.
obligations.acceptance: Library changes preview impact and preserve local overrides under a documented policy.

obligations.work: Add explainable rule graphs with source/version, applicability and evidence.
obligations.acceptance: Pass/warn/fail is traceable and does not imply professional approval or universal code compliance.

obligations.work: Build permission-aware precedent search and project knowledge with source revision citations.
obligations.acceptance: Cross-firm/project information cannot leak through embeddings, caches, search snippets or Agent context.

obligations.work: Govern firm Skills with publish/revoke/version lifecycle and offline behaviour.
obligations.acceptance: Revocation and incompatibility are explicit; users retain local project ownership when firm services are unavailable.

phases.title: Site, programme, analysis and generative alternatives

obligations.work: Represent site/lot, orientation, levels, programme and constraints as typed sourced inputs.
obligations.acceptance: Coordinate systems, units, provenance, applicability and missing inputs are visible before any analysis or generation.

obligations.work: Implement bounded layout/furnishing alternatives with deterministic validation and editable semantic output.
obligations.acceptance: Alternatives state assumptions, score constraint satisfaction and never bypass the canonical operation/review path.

obligations.work: Qualify area/quantity/cost and environmental metrics with reference datasets, location/date/rate assumptions and uncertainty.
obligations.acceptance: Quantities reconcile with the model; heuristic cost or simulation output is not presented as a certified estimate.

obligations.work: Add jurisdiction/version-specific checks only with qualified domain review.
obligations.acceptance: Rules record edition, building/use category, exclusions and overrides; English room names or hard-coded thresholds cannot establish compliance.

obligations.work: Define concurrent semantic edit model, authority and conflict classes before enabling shared mutation.
obligations.acceptance: Transport uses versioned operations/snapshots, never raw SQLite pages, and preserves local recovery.

obligations.work: Implement offline queues, ordering, deduplication, retry, safe rebase and permission revalidation.
obligations.acceptance: Partitions and out-of-order events converge for the declared subset or surface explicit conflicts without lost intent.

obligations.work: Provide presence, ownership/conflict resolution, design options and revision history where validated.
obligations.acceptance: Presence is not mistaken for durability; conflict UI shows alternatives and consequences and supports reversible resolution.

obligations.work: Run multi-client chaos/load/restore and mixed-version compatibility campaigns.
obligations.acceptance: Revoked writers, stale clients, server loss and concurrent host deletion never create silent corruption or cross-tenant exposure.

phases.title: Native iPad, Files and spatial capture

obligations.work: Select native architecture with shared-core/FFI and document identity contracts based on measured platform need.
obligations.acceptance: No native-only storage authority makes supported web/native .arq exchange lossy or unreadable.

obligations.work: Implement Files/open-in/share/export, background/foreground, offline editing and interrupted-write recovery.
obligations.acceptance: Real hardware retains portable data under app termination, storage pressure, picker cancellation and OS update.

obligations.work: Add supported Pencil hover/double tap/squeeze/haptic behaviours and keyboard/trackpad/VoiceOver parity.
obligations.acceptance: Exact hardware/OS combinations pass physical tests and unsupported combinations degrade gracefully.

obligations.work: Prototype RoomPlan/LiDAR capture with calibration/accuracy and correction UX, then qualify App Store/TestFlight distribution.
obligations.acceptance: Capture states measurement limitations; install/update/uninstall, privacy/permission disclosures and store review obligations are satisfied before public availability.

phases.title: Desktop downloads and native update lifecycle

obligations.work: Decide whether macOS/Windows and optionally Linux native shells materially improve file/workflow reliability over the browser.
obligations.acceptance: A documented ADR selects platform/toolkit/support versions; this is a proposed extension, not an existing desktop implementation claim.

obligations.work: Build signed/notarised or platform-appropriate packages, file associations, single-instance document opening and native save dialogs.
obligations.acceptance: Clean machines install and launch without developer tools; source files and shared-core invariants remain protected.

obligations.work: Deliver authenticated update metadata, staged rollout, compatible downgrade/rollback and offline update failure handling.
obligations.acceptance: Tampered/interrupted updates refuse safely and never migrate the only good project copy irreversibly.

obligations.work: Test install/update/repair/uninstall, entitlements, antivirus/Gatekeeper behaviour, paths/Unicode and enterprise restrictions.
obligations.acceptance: Public download links, checksums, support matrix and release notes match the tested binary; uninstall clearly distinguishes app removal from user data deletion.

obligations.work: Prioritise curved walls, slabs, stairs/railings, roofs, families, renovation/design options and richer modelling from real unmet demand.
obligations.acceptance: Each selected capability gets an ADR/semantic contract and a separate fixture/evidence campaign; speculative catalogue rows remain gated.

obligations.work: Evaluate BCF, IDS/bSDD, glTF/GLB, STEP, DWG/RVT and structural/MEP interfaces according to actual use and licences.
obligations.acceptance: Exact supported directions/subsets and losses are published; no blanket incumbent compatibility or professional safety claim.

obligations.work: Create a versioned extension SDK with sandboxing, permissions, signing, compatibility discovery and safe-open quarantine.
obligations.acceptance: At least one third-party-style extension works without privileged core access and a malicious/broken extension cannot compromise projects.

obligations.work: Establish marketplace/moderation/licensing/support policies before external extension distribution.
obligations.acceptance: Abuse, revocation, compromised packages, abandoned extensions and migration ownership have rehearsed procedures.

obligations.work: Reconcile the accepted mature scope against every feature, issue, branch, risk, decision and distribution promise.
obligations.acceptance: #367 closes only when required P10 outcomes pass or an explicit owner-approved successor records every deferred obligation.

obligations.work: Run representative end-to-end journeys spanning manual authoring, documents, exchange, Agent, connectors, collaboration and native channels.
obligations.acceptance: No enabled surface bypasses identity, validation, durability, accessibility, privacy or support contracts.

obligations.work: Define long-term format compatibility, old-version readers/exporters, security support and upgrade communication.
obligations.acceptance: Users can retain and open their own data through supported transitions; migration/rollback is demonstrated with historical fixtures.

obligations.work: Plan feature/service retirement, account closure, connector removal and final data export.
obligations.acceptance: Notice, retention/deletion, backup expiry and offline archive access follow approved policies; product shutdown does not strand user projects.

records.title: [PUBLIC SITE V2] Implement ARQ editorial public-site system, starting with shared foundation and PUB-001
records.body:
Parent design-production gap: #205
Related UI/UX programme: #377
Recurring CTO reconciliation: #369
Repository authority: #332

```yaml
programme: arq-public-site-v2
phase: W0-W6
lifecycle: active
risk: standard
blast_radius: public
reversibility: reversible
branch: codex/arq-public-site-editorial-v1
base_head: df04288c182bdfcee91f92e70b0e5d0017fc0628
owner: ChatGPT implementation lane
```

## User outcome
Turn the current static ARQ public site into a distinctive editorial-technical system without weakening its strongest properties: static HTML, no client-side JavaScript, no third-party requests, governed claims, accessibility, dark appearance, 320px support and 200% zoom.

## Current evidence / known gap
The current `apps/marketing` implementation is structurally sound but visually repetitive. It relies on one 68rem measure, a conventional hero scale and a small shared component vocabulary. `design/page-renderings/PAGE-RENDERINGS-MANIFEST.csv` still marks public visual assets as deferred. Marketing CSS also duplicates canonical brand colour values and currently uses a different dark green than `design/tokens/brand.v4.css`. `layout.ts` hardcodes a stale `REV B · 2026-08` footer label.

## First implementation slice
1. Preserve the current integration authority from #332. Do not assume `main`.
2. Add the approved master public-site plan to the repository.
3. Establish a canonical brand-token bridge for marketing without creating a second brand authority.
4. Remove the stale hand-maintained revision month.
5. Add an additive editorial CSS layer rather than destabilising the existing stylesheet in one large rewrite.
6. Add typed shared editorial primitives needed for PUB-001.
7. Recompose PUB-001 using governed current copy and explicit current/limit state pairs.
8. Preserve all public-site route, language, claim, accessibility and no-external-resource invariants.
9. Open a PR and use CI as the executable evidence layer available to this lane.

## Owned files for this slice
Primary ownership:
- `docs/design/ARQ-PUBLIC-WEBSITE-EDITORIAL-SYSTEM-MASTER-PLAN-v1.0.md`
- `apps/marketing/src/layout.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/build.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/editorial.css` (new)
- `apps/marketing/src/components.ts`
- `apps/marketing/src/content/home.ts`
- focused public-site tests only if required by the implementation

Do not overlap another active lane touching these files without reconciliation.

## Non-negotiables
- no framework rewrite;
- no client JS dependency for core content;
- no external resources;
- no fake product screenshots, metrics or capability;
- no weakening ARQ Language System 4.1;
- no second semantic capability vocabulary;
- `.arq opens` must stay adjacent to `does not save back`;
- 3D viewing must not become 3D authoring by implication;
- state cannot rely on colour alone;
- mobile/200% zoom/accessibility outrank exact visual mimicry;
- do not change the public route contract as part of styling work.

## Evidence required before completion
- exact branch head;
- CI/build/type/test status on that head;
- public-site language/claim checks;
- no-external-resource checks;
- responsive/zoom/visual evidence where current tooling can produce it;
- explicit report of any evidence that remains not-inspected rather than treating it as green.

## Completion boundary
This issue is not the entire 17-page rollout. The first closeable checkpoint is a verified shared foundation plus PUB-001 visual proof. PUB-002 onward should proceed only after that system is proven and reviewed.

records.title: [UX-0.6] Reconcile UI/UX issue graph with P1/P2/P3 semantic owners before implementation starts
records.body:
Parent epic: #379
Parent UI/UX programme: #377
Parent universal programme: #367
Coordination authority: #368, #369

```yaml
phase: UX-0
lifecycle: ready
depends_on: []
risk: standard
parallel_safe: yes
ownership: [issue-metadata, docs/product/ARQ-UI-UX-ISSUE-EXECUTION-INDEX.md]
evidence: [live-issue-audit, dependency-graph-validation]
```

## 1. User outcome
Parallel agents receive one bounded implementation responsibility rather than two issues asking different agents to implement the same wall, door, room, sheet or Agent capability.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
While the UI/UX programme was being decomposed, the universal programme was also decomposed into semantic/product issues such as #378 walls, #380 openings, #382 rooms, #385 dimensions, #387 notes, #389 cross-surface coordination, #391 browser/inspector, #393 sheets, #395 PDF, #400 accessibility, #402 performance, #404 help, #406 protected workflow, #415 exchange fidelity, #421/#422/#424 Agent and later supporting issues. These are complementary to the UI/UX slices only if ownership/dependencies are explicit. Without reconciliation, independent agents could duplicate mutation/model work.

## 3. In scope
Read every open UI/UX issue under #377 and every overlapping P1/P2/P3 issue from #367 at the current head. For each overlap, classify one issue as semantic/domain owner and the other as UI integration/polish/evidence slice, or mark a true duplicate for owner review. Update issue bodies/metadata with explicit `depends_on`, `blocked_by`, ownership globs and cross-links. Ensure no two parallel-safe issues claim the same high-conflict files or canonical operation authority without sequencing. Generate/update the UI/UX issue execution index with a dependency graph and safe first work frontier.

At minimum reconcile:
- #431/#433/#435 with #378 and geometry/tolerance #464;
- #437/#439/#441 with #380;
- #443 with #382;
- #445 with #385/#465;
- #447 with #387;
- #449/#456 with #391 and locale/units #452/#88 where relevant;
- #451-#458 with #389 and semantic level/model owners;
- #459-#471 with #371/#355/#356/#410/#415;
- #472-#476 with #393/#395/#406;
- #477-#483 with #419/#421/#422/#424/#428;
- #484-#492 with #400/#402/#404/#408 and platform issues #358-#360.

## 4. Out of scope
No product implementation, no closing an issue as duplicate without reading its actual contract, no redesign of the universal programme.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
This issue is issue/document metadata only and can run before implementation. It must inspect live open PRs as temporary ownership claims.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
None. The purpose is specifically to ensure each canonical mutation/data authority has one implementation owner.

## 7. UI/UX states
Not applicable to runtime; issue-state/lifecycle states must be accurate: ready, blocked, active/claimed, review, integrated/closed.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Explicitly ensure persistence/domain issues own storage semantics and UI issues only integrate/display those results unless the issue says otherwise.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Ensure Agent/import/read-only UI issues do not own security authority that belongs to their domain issues.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Ensure #400 remains accessibility authority while UI slices own only feature-specific implementation/evidence.

## 11. Performance impact
Ensure #402 remains budget authority while feature issues own fixes in their hot paths.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Live GitHub issue/PR inventory; dependency graph has no unclassified semantic-owner collision; high-conflict file ownership map from #396 is incorporated when available; index is deterministic/current-head stamped.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- every known overlap is explicitly classified and cross-linked;
- no semantic capability has two independent implementation authorities;
- machine-readable dependencies reflect actual blockers;
- every `parallel_safe: yes` lane is safe against known ownership conflicts or narrowed accordingly;
- the execution index names the current ready frontier and CTO reconciliation triggers;
- later agents can choose an issue without re-discovering the entire programme.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post exact issue/PR snapshot time/head, overlaps found, bodies/metadata updated, true duplicates needing owner decision, and the next safe parallel lanes.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 must treat this reconciled graph as the UI/UX routing map and refresh it whenever universal programme decomposition adds or materially changes an overlapping domain issue.

records.title: [UX-8.9] Run final UI/UX programme acceptance, human-evidence reconciliation and CTO handoff
records.body:
Parent epic: #394
Parent UI/UX programme: #377
Depends on: #476, #484, #485, #486, #487, #488, #489, #490, #491 and required platform/human gates


## 1. User outcome
ARQ's UI/UX programme ends with one evidence-backed product experience, not a pile of merged redesign PRs whose interactions were never tested together.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#377 defines UX-0 through UX-8 and #369 provides the recurring CTO integrator. This issue is the final UI/UX acceptance checkpoint after all applicable lanes have been integrated and real human/platform evidence is available.

## 3. In scope
At current integration authority: rebuild UI/UX capability/dependency state; run #476 protected workflow; consume accessibility #484, tablet/Pencil #485, motion #486, visual matrix #487, renderer fallback #488, performance #489, lifecycle stress #490 and help/usability #491; reconcile supported browser/device matrix #358-#360; review #211/#408 human findings; inspect open P0/P1 UI defects and unresolved review comments; run #369 reconciliation; fix only bounded integration defects or open owner-scoped issues; update #377 and phase epics with verified state.

## 4. Out of scope
No new feature scope, no waiver of failed mandatory evidence, no issue-count percentage as proof of quality, no closing blocked human/device gates by assumption.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Run after implementation lanes are merged. Do not overwrite active owners. Exact integration head must remain stable for each recorded evidence run or evidence must be rerun after changes.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
No new operation authority. Verify manual, document and Agent UI surfaces all converge on canonical operations/persistence appropriate to their phase.

## 7. UI/UX states
Acceptance covers normal protected workflow plus representative empty/loading/read-only/validation/error/recovery/renderer-failure/Agent-failure states that are active in the tested phase.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Native edit/publish/reopen/recovery truth is mandatory for Core acceptance; later-phase Agent/import/document paths use their applicable durability contracts.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Consume parser/Agent/privacy evidence where active. No private user project data in acceptance fixtures or screenshots.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Mandatory linked evidence from #484/#485 and required human/device checks; missing evidence keeps the corresponding claim red/blocked.

## 11. Performance impact
Mandatory #489/#402 verdict for protected hot paths and no unresolved material regression.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
One structured evidence bundle with integration branch/head, commands/results, browser/device envelope, visual artifacts, benchmark deltas, human evidence references, failure-injection results, known limitations and open blockers.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- #476 protected workflow is green on exact integration head;
- no unresolved release-stop/P1-critical UI defect remains;
- accessibility/performance/renderer/lifecycle gates required for Core are green;
- tablet/physical/human evidence is present for every claim that requires it, or the claim remains explicitly unsupported/blocked;
- save/publish/export/import/Agent wording matches actual capability state;
- #369 reconciliation finds no unresolved cross-lane authority/integration defect;
- #377 can be closed or narrowed only from this evidence and an owner-approved programme decision.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post exact head, evidence bundle location, gate verdicts, human/device debt, regressions fixed/issues opened and final next-safe frontier.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 is required before closure. If later feature phases continue beyond Core, keep #377 open for those phase-specific UX gates or explicitly revise the programme rather than declaring global completion prematurely.

records.title: [UX-8.8] Reconcile first-run, contextual help and shortcut guidance against the final editor
records.body:
Parent epic: #394
Depends on: #404, #420, #427, #476
Related usability evidence: #211, #408
Parent programme: #377

```yaml
phase: UX-8
lifecycle: blocked
blocked_by: [404,420,427,476]
risk: standard
parallel_safe: yes
human_evidence_required: true
ownership: [help/onboarding UI, command-derived references, packages/design-system/**]
evidence: [browser-help, registry-drift-check, usability]
```

## 1. User outcome
A first-time architect can discover the protected workflow and recover from unfamiliar states without forced tours, stale help text or developer coaching, while experienced users can work without interruptions.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#404 owns first-run/contextual help for Core. UI/UX work can change commands, shell layout, panel locations and tool states after help is initially implemented, so a final reconciliation is required.

## 3. In scope
Reconcile #404 against canonical command registry, final shell, active-tool HUD, level navigation, durability/recovery, sheet/export and supported Agent surfaces. Generate shortcut/help references from stable command metadata where possible, verify empty-state guidance and error/recovery links, ensure coach marks never cover precision interactions, and add a drift check preventing references to removed/renamed commands/surfaces.

## 4. Out of scope
No forced onboarding tour, marketing education, hidden telemetry dependency or documentation rewrite unrelated to in-product guidance.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Consume #404 rather than replacing it. Coordinate command/help metadata with #420 and active-tool hints with #427.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
None. Help invokes/navigates to canonical commands; it does not create alternate actions.

## 7. UI/UX states
First run, no project, empty level, active tool, no selection, read-only, recovery/error, no sheet, command unavailable and advanced/Agent feature unavailable.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Help copy must accurately distinguish working-copy persistence, Publish, recovery and external export states.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
No private project content enters generic help/telemetry; error help links expose only safe diagnostic categories.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Help is keyboard/screen-reader accessible, dismissible, reopenable and does not trap focus or obscure active precision work.

## 11. Performance impact
Help content/illustration dependencies remain lightweight/lazy; no first-paint penalty from a large documentation bundle.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Command/help drift validation, browser dismiss/reopen/focus, stale-state links, first-run protected-flow smoke and real usability findings from #211/#408.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- in-product help references only current commands/surfaces;
- first-time protected workflow has no hidden developer-only step;
- guidance is dismissible/non-obstructive for experts;
- save/publish/recovery language is truthful;
- real usability findings become bounded fixes/issues rather than being buried.

## 14. Agent progress updates

## 1. User outcome
ARQ remains stable during a real workday: repeatedly opening/closing projects and moving between heavy surfaces does not accumulate Workers, event listeners, object URLs, GPU resources or UI state until the editor becomes slow or unreliable.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
Native open evidence already asserts one Worker and clean close for a bounded scenario. The UI/UX programme introduces more panels/sheets/deferred surfaces and needs a repeated lifecycle stress proof rather than a single-cycle smoke test.

## 3. In scope
Create deterministic browser stress scenarios for repeated `.arq` open/close, Plan↔3D cycles, panel/drawer open/close, sheet enter/exit, file dialog cancel/reopen, Publish/export attempts and Agent surface/session connect/disconnect when active. Track Worker/session count, event listeners/subscriptions where instrumentable, object/blob URLs, retained project identifiers, renderer/resource disposal signals and browser memory proxies supported by the test environment. Define stable thresholds/trends rather than brittle absolute memory bytes where APIs are noisy.

## 4. Out of scope
No synthetic memory claim on physical devices that test APIs cannot observe, no arbitrary forced GC requirement for product correctness, no rewrite of Worker architecture unless evidence identifies a defect.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Coordinate native-session/Worker, ModelCanvas, file-delivery and Agent lifecycle owners. Prefer test/instrumentation hooks that do not ship sensitive debug state to production.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
No semantic change. Closing one project/session must not affect another project's canonical state or reuse stale identity.

## 7. UI/UX states
Normal close, close during pending UI state, failed open, failed export, renderer surface teardown, Agent disconnect and reopening a different project.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Stress tests must wait/handle pending acknowledged writes according to lifecycle policy; they may not hide leaks by force-closing unsafely.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Instrumentation records counts/IDs only from synthetic fixtures; no private content or secrets.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
No direct scope; lifecycle fixes must preserve focus restoration and accessible status behaviour.

## 11. Performance impact
Primary scope: detect monotonic growth and interaction degradation over repeated cycles; correlate with #402 budgets.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Production-build headless-browser stress loop, Worker/session assertions, project identity isolation, repeated 3D/Sheet/Agent mount-unmount, object URL cleanup, memory trend report and zero unexpected console-error requirement.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- repeated project open/close returns Worker/session counts to expected baseline;
- heavy UI surface churn has no material monotonic resource leak;
- project identities/context do not survive into unrelated sessions;
- object URLs/listeners/subscriptions owned by scoped features are cleaned up;
- any noisy memory metric is reported honestly with the stronger deterministic leak signals.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post exact head/browser, cycle counts, before/after resource metrics, leaks found/fixed and limitations of available memory APIs.

records.title: [UX-8.5] Add honest weak-GPU, renderer-init and 3D failure fallback UX
records.body:
Parent epic: #394
Depends on: #457, #418 and current supported browser/device envelope #358/#360
Parent programme: #377

```yaml
phase: UX-8

parallel_safe: yes
ownership: [apps/web/src/ModelCanvas.tsx, packages/model-renderer/**, packages/design-system/**]
evidence: [failure-injection, browser-matrix, capability-fallback]
```

## 1. User outcome
If 3D cannot initialise, the GPU/context fails, or a browser falls outside the supported renderer envelope, ARQ keeps the project usable and explains what failed instead of showing a black/blank canvas or crashing the whole workspace.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
ARQ's 3D surface is real WebGL2 and browser/platform support is being formalised by #358/#360. The UI/UX programme needs deterministic renderer failure/fallback states comparable in trust to file/persistence failures.

## 3. In scope
Identify renderer initialisation/capability failure classes already detectable; add 3D loading timeout, unsupported-capability, context-lost/runtime render error and recover/retry/reload guidance where technically valid; preserve Plan/browser/inspector usability; allow return to Plan; keep current project/selection safe; provide privacy-safe diagnostics hook. If a lower-quality supported render mode already exists, expose it honestly rather than inventing one here.

## 4. Out of scope
No WebGPU migration, no new renderer backend, no pretending unsupported hardware is supported, no hiding repeated GPU failure behind infinite retries.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Coordinate ModelCanvas/renderer owners and #358/#360 support policy. Do not alter semantic project state to recover renderer errors.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Renderer failure never changes canonical project data. Renderer/cache state remains disposable and rebuildable.

## 7. UI/UX states
Deferred 3D loading, slow init, unsupported WebGL/capability, context lost, runtime renderer error, retrying, recovered, permanent fallback to Plan and browser/device unsupported.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Project durability continues independently. Renderer failure cannot trigger false recovery/save messages or discard edits.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Diagnostics redact GPU/browser details only as required by privacy policy and never include project geometry/content by default.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Failure panel/status is keyboard and screen-reader accessible, returns focus safely to a usable surface and does not rely on canvas-only text.

## 11. Performance impact
Detection/recovery adds negligible hot-path overhead; no high-frequency polling. Retry attempts are bounded.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Capability/init failure injection, context-lost simulation where possible, renderer exception boundary, Plan usability during failure, retry/recovery, browser matrix and zero project mutation/durability regression.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- blank/black 3D failures become explicit actionable states;
- Plan/project browsing remains usable when 3D fails;
- renderer failure cannot corrupt or mutate project data;
- retries are bounded and honest;
- support claims follow #358/#360 evidence rather than optimistic fallback.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post detectable failure classes, recovery path per class, tested browser/GPU environments, diagnostics fields and exact evidence.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 includes renderer failure smoke after 3D changes and treats project-level crashes from 3D failure as a high-priority integration defect.

Define a bounded deterministic matrix for supported desktop/tablet/phone breakpoints, available light/dark/appearance modes, Plan/3D/Sheet surfaces, panel expanded/collapsed states, active tool, selection/multi-selection, no project/loading/read-only/error/recovery, import/export review and Agent/Review Centre when those phases are active. Visual regression checks focus visibility and non-colour state in representative fixtures but do not replace accessibility tests.

Keep CI matrix bounded; shard or run selected impacted baselines via path mapping, with periodic full matrix. Avoid turning every small change into an unbounded browser farm.

Deterministic screenshot generation from production build, pixel-diff thresholds documented per surface, intentional-change review workflow, nondeterminism stability test and CI/path-selected execution.

Depends on: #421, #424, #418, #477
Related evaluation: #428
Parent programme: #377

```yaml
phase: UX-7
lifecycle: blocked
blocked_by: [421,424,418,477]
risk: deep
parallel_safe: yes
ownership: [Agent UI, Review Centre result/error states, packages/design-system/**]
evidence: [failure-injection, Agent-evals, browser-agent-failure]
```

## 1. User outcome
If an Agent request fails, the user never sees unexplained silence. ARQ states what failed, whether anything changed, whether the proposal remains valid, and what retry/recovery action is safe.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
Pascal's open-source implementation illustrates a dangerous trust failure class: a stream may fail while users cannot tell whether earlier tool calls changed anything. ARQ's architecture intends stronger atomic governed mutation through #424, but transport/read-only/proposal stages can still fail and must present exact outcome truth.

## 3. In scope
Define a failure taxonomy mapped from real Agent/transport/apply states: cancelled, offline, timeout, provider/tool error, grant expired/revoked, stale project/revision, proposal generation interrupted, apply refused before commit, atomic apply failure, persistence failure after operation contract reports it, and any explicitly supported partial outcome. Show retry only when semantically safe; bind retry to the right project/revision or require re-review when context changed. Preserve any successful read-only result/proposal data that remains valid.

## 4. Out of scope
No generic `Something went wrong` catch-all as the only UI, no automatic regenerate-and-apply, no claim of partial application when the canonical apply contract is atomic, and no swallowing technical diagnostics needed for support logs.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Consume actual error/result contracts from #421/#424. Coordinate #428 eval taxonomy. Do not infer mutation outcome from visible canvas changes.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Mutation outcome comes only from canonical apply/operation/persistence result. The UI cannot guess that `nothing changed` or `some changes applied` from Agent prose or renderer state.

## 7. UI/UX states
Cancelled, offline, timeout, stream interrupted before proposal, proposal incomplete, stale, permission failure, apply refused/no mutation, apply failed atomically/no mutation, persistence/commit result as defined by canonical contract, safe retry, retry requires new review and terminal failure.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
If a canonical operation was acknowledged but persistence later failed, show the exact durability state from #459/#460 and recovery action. Never collapse mutation and persistence failure into one ambiguous banner.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
User-facing errors redact secrets/provider internals; support diagnostics keep privacy-safe error codes/provenance only. Retry cannot reuse stale grants across project/revision boundaries.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Failure/status announced, retry/cancel keyboard reachable, no colour-only severity, focus moves to the error/result action without trapping the user.

## 11. Performance impact
No aggressive retry loops. Backoff/network logic remains with Agent transport owner; UI avoids duplicate timers/subscriptions.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Inject each real failure class, verify exact mutation/durability outcome, stale retry behaviour, project-switch isolation, accessibility, and integrate relevant #428 red-team/eval fixtures.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- Agent failure never results in silent thread/UI state;
- user can tell whether canonical project state changed;
- retry is offered only when safe and context-valid;
- durability failures use canonical project state model;
- atomic apply failures are never misrepresented as partial mutation;
- diagnostics remain privacy-safe.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post error taxonomy, canonical outcome source for each case, retry policy, injected evidence and any unrepresentable backend ambiguity that needs a contract fix.

## 15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes
#369 checks Agent failure UX against #424 atomicity and #459 durability after each Agent contract change.

## 1. User outcome
After review, the user can approve exactly the proposal they saw, reject it cleanly, understand the resulting project/durability state, and undo an applied Agent action as one meaningful action where the canonical operation group supports it.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#424 owns governed application of the exact reviewed operation group, fresh validation, persistence, provenance and grouped undo. This issue owns the final interaction/result UX around that authority.

## 3. In scope
Wire Approve/Reject through #424; show approval prerequisites, fresh validation in progress, applying, persistence acknowledgement, success with affected-object links, stale/permission/validation refusal, grouped Undo action when available, undo result, and transition back to ordinary selection/project state. Reject clears preview without mutation and records/handles proposal lifecycle according to P3 contract.

## 4. Out of scope
No alternative apply path, no proposal regeneration on Approve, no permission bypass, no hidden automatic retry that changes proposal semantics.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Consume #424 exactly. Coordinate durability state #459 and proposal preview #479. Do not duplicate operation/persistence logic in React components.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Approve applies the exact reviewed typed operation group through #424. Undo uses ordinary canonical grouped history/operation semantics. Reject never changes the project model.

## 7. UI/UX states
Ready to approve, approval blocked, revalidating, applying, persistence pending, applied, apply failed atomically, stale, permission revoked, rejected, undo available, undoing, undone and undo failed.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
Success messaging waits for #424/#459-defined persistence acknowledgement. Apply/undo failure must never falsely show durable success.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Approval requires current grant/permission. Do not expose reusable tokens/grant internals. Actions must remain project/revision scoped.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Approve/Reject are explicitly labelled, destructive/consequential state is not colour-only, confirmation only where policy requires it, progress/status announced, focus lands on result/next action predictably.

## 11. Performance impact
Applying may be longer-running but UI remains responsive. Avoid duplicate project rehydration if canonical operation invalidation already updates views.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
#424 stale/permission/validation/failure fixtures, exact reviewed-vs-applied operation equality, grouped undo/redo, persistence/publish/reopen, keyboard/focus and real browser Agent apply workflow.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- Approve applies exactly the reviewed proposal;
- Reject never mutates project state;
- stale/invalid/unauthorised proposals fail closed;
- result state reflects real persistence status;
- grouped Undo is understandable and operates through canonical history;
- Plan/3D/documents settle through normal invalidation.

## 14. Agent progress updates
Post #424 contract/version consumed, approval state matrix, exact reviewed/applied comparison evidence, persistence/undo results and browser proof.

## 1. User outcome
When reviewing an Agent proposal, the architect can see exactly which existing or proposed objects and documents are affected without confusing preview state with committed project state.

## 2. Current evidence / known gap
#422 identifies affected semantic/document IDs and #389 owns canonical cross-surface invalidation. The Review Centre needs a safe preview/highlight projection that does not write hidden model state.

## 3. In scope
Add proposal-review highlight state keyed to semantic IDs/document references, reveal/focus selected affected item, distinguish existing/modified/created/deleted-preview states where canonical proposal data can represent them, Plan and 3D highlighting, document/sheet affected-state indication, clear preview on reject/close/stale proposal, and handling for hidden/off-level targets with explicit navigation action.

## 4. Out of scope
No canonical mutation, no renderer-only semantic changes, no speculative geometry reconstruction beyond the reviewed proposal/dry-run contract.

## 5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
Coordinate Plan/3D selection/highlight and #389 derived-state owner. Keep proposal-review highlight separate from ordinary selection while allowing controlled reveal/select actions.

## 6. Canonical model / operations impact
Preview/highlight is disposable view state. Any geometry preview must come from canonical dry-run/operation projection APIs, not mutate scene/model stores directly.

## 7. UI/UX states
Existing affected object, proposed create, proposed delete, modified object, hidden/off-level, missing/deleted/stale target, multi-object group, affected sheet/view and cleared review.

## 8. Persistence / recovery impact
No preview/highlight state persists as project content. Closing/reloading cannot make a proposal appear applied.

## 9. Security / privacy impact
Only permitted project objects may be revealed; no cross-project target leakage from stale Agent context.

## 10. Accessibility / input impact
Affected-object list/reveal actions provide non-visual equivalent; highlight state is not colour-only; current reviewed object/status is announced in the Review Centre.

## 11. Performance impact
Large affected sets must use batched/selective highlight and avoid whole-scene material rewrites or expensive per-frame proposal recomputation.

## 12. Tests and exact-head evidence
Proposal fixtures with create/update/delete/hidden/off-level/stale targets, Plan/3D/document reveal parity, clear-preview regression, cross-project isolation and large affected-set performance.

## 13. Acceptance criteria
- preview/highlight never mutates canonical project data;

- hidden/off-level items can be revealed without losing review context;
- stale/missing targets are explicit;
- preview clears deterministically on reject/close/invalidation.

records.title: [P0/P1] Calibrate and enforce the canonical geometry tolerance ladder
records.body:
Parent programme: #367
P0/P1 architecture dependency
Depends on: #88 canonical unit/numeric representation
Related product issues: #378, #382, #385, #389, #411, #413

## User outcome
Geometric operations behave predictably across small details, ordinary buildings, large coordinates, imported files and repeated edits. ARQ must not depend on scattered magic epsilons or provisional tolerance magnitudes that happen to pass today's fixtures.

## Current evidence / known gap
ARQ already has a named tolerance policy and geometry functions that take explicit tolerances, but current repository notes state that the actual magnitudes remain provisional pending the canonical numeric/unit decision and domain calibration. Core authoring, dimensions, room boundaries, import reconciliation and future connectors depend on settling this deliberately.

## In scope
After #88 is resolved:
- inventory every named tolerance and every remaining local epsilon/magic threshold across geometry, snapping, topology, BIM operations, imports/exports and rendering-to-model hit tests;
- define one canonical tolerance ladder with purpose-specific fields rather than one global epsilon;
- distinguish at minimum coordinate coincidence, zero-length/degeneracy, intersection/topology, angle, area, snap/display and import/reconciliation tolerances where the architecture requires separate semantics;
- define how tolerances scale or do not scale with canonical units, world extents and view-space interactions;
- measure behaviour on representative architectural extents and adversarial fixtures, including very small details, large site coordinates, near-parallel segments, nearly coincident endpoints, repeated transforms and import round trips;
- document which tolerances are model-semantic and which are UI/view-space only;
- update all Core geometry/operation consumers to use the accepted named policy;
- add a check for forbidden stray model-space epsilons outside explicitly approved modules;
- define compatibility/migration consequences if tolerance changes affect derived topology or validation in existing projects.

## Out of scope
Do not choose the canonical numeric representation here. Do not hide algorithm instability by simply increasing tolerances until tests pass. Do not make screen-pixel snap tolerance a canonical geometric truth.

## Safety rules
- invalid/ambiguous geometry must fail explicitly rather than being coerced into coincidence;
- tolerance changes must not silently rewrite persisted canonical coordinates;
- imported geometry reconciliation must report any approximation that crosses material fidelity boundaries;
- topology-changing tolerance changes require explicit compatibility review.

## Evidence
Benchmark/fixture matrix across representative scales; property/adversarial tests; import/export round trips; wall join/room boundary/dimension reference regression suite; repeated-edit drift tests; exact-head performance measurement.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] #88 is resolved first or this issue remains blocked.
- [ ] One documented named tolerance ladder is accepted and used by Core model operations.
- [ ] No unapproved model-space magic epsilons remain in the scoped packages.
- [ ] Screen/view tolerances are clearly separated from semantic geometry tolerances.
- [ ] Wall joins, room boundaries, stable references and supported import reconciliation pass calibrated adversarial fixtures.
- [ ] Existing project compatibility effects are measured and documented.
- [ ] Changing a tolerance requires targeted evidence and cannot silently weaken validation globally.

## ZEUS CTO reconciliation
#369 must review this together with #88, wall/room/dimension lanes and import adapters because a tolerance change can produce cross-cutting semantic regressions even when each package's unit tests remain green.

records.title: [EPIC P6] Firm Intelligence: reusable standards, libraries, rules and precedent memory
records.body:
Parent programme: #367
Entry: stable native model, Agent/Skills contracts and permissions.

## Product outcome
A practice can encode and reuse its own trusted architectural standards without turning informal precedent into hidden AI behaviour.

## Capability groups
- **Firm library:** approved wall/opening/component/types, annotation/document standards and reusable project resources with versioning/provenance.
- **Firm rules:** explicit machine-readable constraints/checks with severity, scope, jurisdiction/project applicability and human override policy.
- **Precedent search:** search the firm's authorised prior projects/resources by semantic attributes and bounded embeddings/metadata, preserving access controls and project provenance.
- **Firm Skills:** versioned P3 Skills owned/published by the practice with review/approval lifecycle.

## Principles
Firm knowledge is separate from model-provider memory. A precedent does not automatically become a design rule. Rules/checks are explainable and source-linked. Access control is enforced at retrieval as well as UI. Updating a library/rule version does not rewrite old project provenance.

## Exit gate
- [ ] Versioned firm library can be applied to new/current projects through explicit operations.
- [ ] Rules produce explainable pass/warn/fail results with source/version.
- [ ] Precedent search respects project permissions and identifies source project/revision.
- [ ] Firm Skills have publish/revoke/version lifecycle.
- [ ] Offline/native projects remain usable when firm services are unavailable; unavailable firm features degrade explicitly.
- [ ] Security/privacy/retention policy is approved for firm data.

## Decomposition rule
When P6 activates, #369 creates bounded issues for library storage/versioning, rule engine, precedent index/search, firm Skill governance and permissions after re-reading then-current collaboration/account architecture.

records.body:
Parent: #419
Phase: P3
Depends on: #422 and stable P1 native operation/persistence path

## User outcome
After reviewing a valid current proposal, an authorised architect can approve it and ARQ applies exactly the reviewed operation group through the same canonical model, validation, persistence and undo system as manual editing.

## In scope
- approval action with current permission/grant checks;
- revalidate project/revision/preconditions immediately before commit;
- apply the exact reviewed typed operation group, not regenerate a new one at approval time;
- atomic/grouped commit semantics where required;
- one grouped undo/redo entry with meaningful label;
- native persistence acknowledgement and honest save state;
- provenance linking request -> proposal -> approval -> operations -> resulting revision;
- Review Centre result state and links to affected objects;
- partial failure policy: fail atomically unless an explicitly designed operation group supports safe partial outcomes.

## Safety
No model-provider tool can bypass this path. Stale proposals fail closed. Approval tokens/grants are scoped and cannot be reused across projects/revisions. Invalid operations leave canonical state unchanged.

## Evidence
Eval and deterministic tests for stale revision, permission revocation, validation failure, one operation failing inside a group, Worker/native write failure, undo/redo, publish/reopen and provenance replay.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Approved proposal applies exactly the reviewed operations.
- [ ] Commit is gated by fresh deterministic validation and permission checks.
- [ ] Result is persisted through the canonical native path.
- [ ] User can undo the Agent change as one understandable action where semantically valid.
- [ ] Failed/stale proposal cannot partially mutate hidden state.
- [ ] Resulting plan/3D/documents coordinate through ordinary invalidation paths.
- [ ] Provenance can answer who/what proposed, approved and committed the change.

- committed Agent actions use ordinary native operations/persistence and grouped undo;
- provenance records model/tool/skill/version/request/approval/operation result without exposing secrets;
- AI output never establishes professional/code/structural approval.

- [ ] Read-only explain/query is product-reachable.
- [ ] Proposal UI shows exact affected semantic objects and document impact.
- [ ] Stale/revision-mismatched proposals fail closed.
- [ ] Approved native mutation applies via canonical operations and is undoable/publishable/reopenable.
- [ ] Agent eval suite covers unsafe/destructive/ambiguous requests and regression cases.

records.title: [P1] Handle browser storage quota, low-space and large-project pressure without data-loss ambiguity
records.body:
Parent: #373
Phase: P1
Related: #397

## User outcome
When local browser storage is constrained, ARQ warns early, explains the difference between working-copy risk and published-file safety, and fails writes predictably without pretending work is durable.

## In scope
- measure available storage where the platform permits it, without treating estimates as guarantees;
- define thresholds for warning/critical states using measured project/resource size;
- distinguish canonical working-copy bytes, recoverable journal/metadata and disposable derived caches;
- reclaim derived/cache data before risking canonical data where policy allows;
- explicit write refusal/failure state when quota prevents acknowledgement;
- recovery/export/publish recommendations that are actually available in the current product;
- large underlay/resource pressure and cancellation;
- browser-specific limitations recorded in the support matrix.

## UX
Persistent but non-blocking warning before critical pressure; blocking error only when a required write cannot be acknowledged. Never show `saved` after quota failure. Provide a clear next action and current risk state.

## Safety
Never delete canonical project data automatically to satisfy quota. Do not promise exact free-space values when browser APIs only provide estimates.

## Evidence
Injected quota/error tests, large project/resource fixtures, cache eviction tests, browser capability checks, restart/recovery after failed writes.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Quota/write failures produce honest unsaved state.
- [ ] Disposable caches can be reclaimed without changing semantic project state.
- [ ] Canonical data is never auto-deleted for space.
- [ ] Warnings/actions match platform capabilities.
- [ ] Failure/recovery behaviour integrates with #397 and publication semantics.

records.title: [ZEUS PROGRAMME] Enforce the universal issue contract and machine-readable dependency metadata
records.body:
Parent programme: #367

## Objective

Make every ARQ implementation lane self-contained enough that an agent can safely pick one issue, understand the user outcome, identify dependencies/conflicts, implement it, prove it, update the issue, and hand it back without relying on hidden chat context.

This issue does **not** replace #317/#319. It builds the programme-level issue contract on top of their ownership protocol once available.

## Required issue metadata

Define a stable machine-readable block for programme issues containing at least:

- programme phase;
- parent epic;
- lifecycle state (`blocked`, `ready`, `claimed`, `in_progress`, `review`, `merged`, `verified`, `released`, `human_evidence`, `superseded`);
- dependencies by issue number;
- blocking issues;
- expected ownership surfaces/files/globs if known;
- risk tier;
- required evidence layers;
- user journey / capability IDs;
- release gate impact;
- whether human/external evidence is required;
- whether the issue may be safely worked in parallel;
- next reconciliation checkpoint.

Do not create a second product/evidence authority. This metadata coordinates work and traceability only.

## Agent issue template

Every executable issue must contain these sections:

1. User outcome
2. Current evidence / known gap
3. In scope
4. Out of scope
5. Dependencies and active ownership conflicts
6. Canonical model / operations impact
7. UI/UX states
8. Persistence / recovery impact
9. Security / privacy impact
10. Accessibility / input impact
11. Performance impact
12. Tests and exact-head evidence
13. Acceptance criteria
14. Agent progress updates
15. ZEUS CTO reconciliation notes

## Progress-update protocol

While an issue is active, its agent must update the issue at meaningful checkpoints with:

- branch and head SHA;
- files/interfaces actually touched;
- assumptions changed after reading code;
- evidence run and result;
- blockers discovered;
- follow-up issue required, if any;
- whether the original scope remains valid.

The issue must not be marked complete merely because a PR was opened.

## Dependency rules

- A blocked issue must not be auto-selected by ZEUS.
- An issue whose dependency has changed materially must be re-preflighted before implementation continues.
- Different issue numbers do not imply safe parallelism. Shared semantic contracts, persistence paths and cross-cutting UI surfaces must be serialised when needed.
- Research-only issues reserve no runtime files unless they become implementation lanes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One canonical programme issue metadata schema exists and is documented.
- [ ] A validator can parse programme issues and reject malformed executable issues.
- [ ] ZEUS issue selection can distinguish ready work from blocked/future work.
- [ ] Dependencies and conflicts are surfaced before mutation begins.
- [ ] The schema composes with #317/#319 instead of duplicating their claim state.
- [ ] The master issue #367 and all newly created programme issues can be represented without losing required information.
- [ ] Tests cover malformed metadata, dependency cycles, stale state, duplicate ownership metadata and blocked-issue selection.
- [ ] Documentation states clearly that product truth still comes from code/ADRs/evidence, not issue metadata.

## Handoff

Once this lands, the ZEUS CTO reconciler should use this contract to refresh programme state and to create later-phase atomic issues only when their phase gate is ready.

# ZEUS active agent work board

This issue is the repository-wide visibility board for concurrent ARQ/ZEUS implementation lanes.

## Authority boundary

This board coordinates **repository work ownership only**. It does not override Zeus classification, Engineering OS, Arq Language System, evidence states, canonical project data, persistence/recovery rules, reliability gates, design authority or release authority.

Issue-comment ownership events on implementation issues are the intended canonical work-ownership log once #317/#319 enforcement lands. This board is a derived visibility surface, not product/design/evidence truth.

## Bootstrap state

Deterministic claim enforcement is not installed yet. Issues #317 and #319 own that rollout plan. Until the validated LEAPH `harness-claims/v2` implementation is safely adapted to ZEUS:

- all currently open pre-enforcement PRs remain legacy owners of the files/interfaces they actually change;
- agents must inspect open PRs and target issue history before mutation;
- no agent may treat the absence of a board row as proof that a file/interface is free;
- do not create a second implementation of #317 or #319 merely because this board exists.

## Target protocol

When installed, the ZEUS-local protocol must provide:

- one active mutation owner per implementation issue;
- unique active branch per issue;
- first valid unreleased claim priority;
- file/glob and shared semantic/interface serialisation;
- `research-only` lanes that reserve no files;
- actor-bound claim lifecycle where identity is available;
- append-only edit/delete-safe ownership history;
- explicit generation-bound owner release/reassignment;
- no automatic claim expiry;
- PR metadata + actual diff/rename/base-drift coverage;

- legacy treatment for all pre-enforcement PRs.

_No machine-managed claims are active because the enforcement engine is not installed yet._

Parallel mutation is allowed only across demonstrably independent lanes. Read-only review/research may run in parallel. If there are fewer safe independent lanes than available agents, excess agents should review/research or remain idle rather than duplicate implementation.

## Federation

ZEUS may adopt reviewed generic harness algorithms and failure-mode lessons from LEAPH, RAAS, CLEO and AETHAR. ARQ must remain operational and authoritative when sibling repositories are unavailable. records.title: platform: decide Firefox desktop support envelope by OS and fallback path
records.body:
Parent: #219 (ARQ-189 browser/device validation matrix)

## Problem

Firefox WebGPU availability is not one uniform "desktop" capability. Current primary evidence differs by OS: stable Windows support exists, stable Apple Silicon macOS support exists in newer Firefox, while Linux and Intel macOS remain non-default/experimental. The product support promise must not be inferred from a single Firefox version number.

## Decision required

For each desktop OS in ARQ's intended market, choose one of:
- required with WebGPU
- required with WebGL fallback
- supported with limitations

records.title: ARQFS-003: Add lossless semantic wall operations for reference-format projects
records.body:
## Problem

Reference-format `.arq` projects cannot safely use the workspace's current `WorkspaceOperation` wall edits.

`WorkspaceOperation` carries only drawn wall centreline geometry and ids. A canonical reference wall also requires semantic identity such as `levelId` and `typeId`, and existing walls can own or affect openings, doors, windows, rooms and other dependent model content. The current native save encoder writes only the flat `{ projectName, walls }` shape.

Therefore treating a rich reference project like the flat editable model would either invent missing semantics or silently discard canonical project content.

## Goal

Create a lossless semantic mutation path for walls in reference-format projects so the editor can make real native edits without flattening the model or guessing project semantics.

## Scope

- Define semantic wall create/update/delete operations against the canonical reference model.
- Carry required level and wall-type identity explicitly. Never infer these from unrelated UI labels.
- Define dependency policy for hosted openings, doors/windows, rooms and other affected content on wall delete or geometry change.
- Preserve untouched levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content, services, pathways, views and project metadata byte-semantically where possible and semantically always.
- Add a reference-model encoder/serializer that round-trips the typed canonical model rather than projecting it to the flat wall format.
- Integrate operations with undo/redo and `NativeProjectSession` without duplicating its write queue.
- Reopen published output in an independent worker and prove semantic equivalence for untouched content plus the intended edit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Adding a wall requires explicit valid `levelId` and `typeId` and survives publish/reopen.
2. Moving/updating a wall preserves its semantic identity and all unrelated canonical content.
3. Deleting a wall follows an explicit tested dependency policy for hosted/dependent elements. No orphan references are written.
4. A rich project containing multiple levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content and views retains all untouched content after edit/publish/reopen.
5. Invalid or incomplete semantic edits are refused rather than guessed.
6. The workspace can switch #355's reference-project persistence route from refusal to this semantic mutation path once these guarantees are proven.

## Relationship

Follow-up to #355. #355 must remain non-destructive and may persist only the flat native model until this semantic path exists.

records.title: ARQFS-002: Persist live editor operations through native project sessions
records.body:
## Problem

The native project write path already exists in `NativeProjectSession.save()`, but the workspace editor does not call it.

Today `App.tsx` applies typed plan operations to in-memory walls and records edit/undo/redo activity only through the IndexedDB demo journal (`PLAN_PROJECT_ID = 'demo-project'`). When a writable native `.arq` project is open, the same edits therefore do not advance the native working copy even though publication/checkpoint infrastructure exists.

There is also a critical format boundary: `NativeProjectSession.save()` currently re-encodes the editable model as the flat `{ projectName, walls }` shape. A reference-format project can contain levels, wall types, rooms, openings, doors, windows, placed content and views. Sending a reference project through the flat encoder would silently discard that richer content. This issue must not introduce that data loss.

## Goal

Connect live editor persistence to native project sessions where the current editor model can be round-tripped without loss, while preserving the current demo/recovery journal when no native project is open and explicitly refusing destructive persistence for richer reference projects until semantic edit operations exist.

## Scope

- Add a single workspace persistence bridge for edit, undo and redo operations.
- For a writable flat native project (`snapshot.document === null`), route the resulting wall state plus the exact typed `WorkspaceOperation` through `NativeProjectSession.save()`.
- Use the existing native session queue. Do not invent a second native save queue.
- Keep the existing IndexedDB plan journal for the no-native-project/demo path.
- For reference-format native projects (`snapshot.document !== null`), do not call the flat native save path. Report the project as not safely editable/persistable by the current wall operation model rather than flattening it.
- Respect read-only native projects. Do not silently fall back to the demo journal and imply the project was persisted.
- Do not report `saved` until the selected persistence authority acknowledges the write.
- Surface native write failure as unsaved/failed state without discarding the editor's visible operation or poisoning later saves.
- Ensure undo/redo use the same persistence path as forward edits.
- Make close/publish semantics account for in-flight editor persistence through the session's existing queue.
- Add focused tests for routing, native edit, undo/redo, failure recovery, reference-format refusal and read-only behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Opening a writable flat `.arq`, drawing/removing walls, then publishing produces bytes whose reopened model contains those edits.
2. Undo and redo change both the visible plan state and the flat native working copy.
3. A native write failure leaves the UI in an honest unsaved state; a later successful write is still attempted and can recover the session.
4. A read-only native project cannot be presented as saved after an edit attempt.
5. A reference-format project can never be flattened by an editor persistence attempt. The bridge refuses that route until semantic wall operations can preserve levels/types/dependants.
6. With no native project open, the current IndexedDB recovery behaviour remains intact.
7. Tests cover the persistence bridge without duplicating `NativeProjectSession` queue logic.

## Follow-up boundary

Reference-format wall editing needs a semantic operation that carries at least level and wall-type identity and preserves/cascades hosted/dependent content correctly. That work is tracked separately and is a prerequisite to making rich reference projects natively editable.

This issue is intentionally narrower than file-handle write-back to the original user-selected file. It closes the safe editor-to-native-working-copy bridge first.

records.title: [ZEUS CTO v2] Enforce closed-loop runtime decisions and execution-state blockers
records.body:
## Outcome

Turn #328 / PR #329's adaptive ZEUS budget adviser into a deterministic closed-loop runtime controller without changing Zeus 5.0 core authority, Engineering OS, evidence/gate/plan/state ledgers, repository-intelligence work, or protected approval rules.

Stack this work on the clean #329 head. The runtime must import the v1 adviser rather than fork it.

## Runtime decisions

Every checkpoint or finish emits exactly one next action:
- `stop-success`
- `proceed`
- `re-evaluate-tier-or-evidence-plan`
- `repair`
- `block-external-evidence`

## Semantics

- Executed required verification failure, authority inversion, or unsupported evidence promotion -> `repair`.
- Required proof that did not execute, missing independent review, missing protected owner approval, or unavailable current-head proof -> `block-external-evidence`; do not burn code-repair loops on non-execution.
- Budget ceiling breach or duplicate executed work -> `re-evaluate-tier-or-evidence-plan`.
- `stop-success` requires acceptance plus the full required proof frontier and no duplicate execution waste.

## Receipt

Privacy-safe operational metadata only: schema/phase, tier, caller-supplied repository/source/claim fingerprints, budget ceilings and actual usage, verification execution states, duplicate operations, expansion reason, decision and reason codes. Never store raw prompts, hidden reasoning, secrets, private user data, or fabricated engineering evidence.

## ZEUS protections

- Existing Engineering OS/evidence gates remain authoritative and cannot be lowered by this layer.
- Critical/protected proof remains freshness-sensitive and ordinary cache cannot replace current proof.
- One semantic mutation lane remains mandatory.
- Independent review remains separate from implementation when required.
- More agents cannot manufacture owner/protected approval or current-head evidence.

## Regression coverage

Pin green finish, green checkpoint, budget overrun, duplicate work, executed gate failure, zero-step/non-executed gate, missing independent review, missing protected approval, missing current-head proof, authority inversion, unsupported evidence promotion, protected expansion without reason, protected expansion with reason, and invalid `not-required` state on a required check.

## File scope

Exactly three files on `codex/zeus-cto-runtime-v2`:
- `scripts/zeus-adaptive-runtime.mjs`
- `scripts/zeus-adaptive-runtime.test.mjs`
- `.github/workflows/zeus-adaptive-runtime-v2.yml`

## Done

The exact-head path-scoped workflow executes formatting plus the v2 regression suite successfully, while #329 remains a clean four-file v1 dependency and existing repository gates stay unchanged.

records.title: ARQFS-001: Make `.arq` open a byte-safe compatibility gate
records.body:
## Problem

The file picker must not hand arbitrary or future `.arq` bytes to SQLite or the editor. A reader must distinguish malformed, incompatible and healthy files before authoring begins.

## Scope

- Wire `preflightArqfsBytes` into every file-open path.
- Validate SQLite header fields, page/file limits, ARQ application ID, frozen meta, schema and required feature flags.
- Return stable reason codes and route to editable, read-only, migration or blocked states.

## Acceptance criteria

- Truncated, oversized, wrong-ID, future-major, future-schema and unknown-required-feature fixtures never construct an editable session.
- Older same-major schemas offer copy-on-write migration.
- The UI shows a short actionable message plus a diagnostics affordance.
- No raw SQLite error or empty editor shell leaks to users.

Scenarios: S001–S017.

## Live implementation status (2026-07-24)

The storage-layer half of this issue has landed on `claude/arq-master-agent-execution-ir9re1` (commit `3d808d5`):

- `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-preflight.ts` — raw SQLite header checks for journal mode, reserved bytes, payload fractions, application ID, and declared vs physical page count (truncation detection), each with a stable code (`ARQ_INVALID_JOURNAL_MODE`, `ARQ_INVALID_RESERVED_BYTES`, `ARQ_INVALID_PAYLOAD_FRACTIONS`, `ARQ_FILE_TRUNCATED`, `ARQ_PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).
- `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-open.ts` — refuses future-major and future-schema files, requires numeric version metadata, and treats unreadable feature flags as structural failure rather than "no flags declared".

Evidence: `npx vitest run packages/arqfs --coverage=false` → 23 files / 121 tests pass against a real `better-sqlite3` binding.

### Remaining for this issue

The **UI half is not done**: no file-open path is wired to `preflightArqfsBytes` yet, and no user-facing message or diagnostics affordance exists. That work depends on UI-011 (file open / import UI) and is tracked there.

Dependencies: UI-011, UI-013.
