records.title: reliability: import-export worker cancellation has a race with in-flight conversion
records.body:
Fixed in d19d388.

**Bug (FP-019):** `workers/import-export-worker/src/handler.ts` adapters only check `AbortSignal.aborted` once, at the very start of `convert()`. If a `cancel` request arrived after that check but before `convert()` resolved, the handler would still post a final `'converted'`/`'failed'` message for a request the caller had already been told was `'cancelled'` — a real race, not hypothetical, since today's adapters do all their work inside one synchronous-looking `async` call with no later checkpoint.

**Fix:** added a `cancelledRequestIds: Set<string>` plus a `postFinal()` wrapper that silently drops any late `'converted'`/`'failed'` post for a requestId already reported as `'cancelled'`. Once a request is cancelled its outcome is permanently `'cancelled'`; anything settling afterward is dropped, not posted.

**Regression test:** new test in `handler.test.ts` uses a fake adapter whose `convert()` only resolves when the test explicitly releases it, so the cancel genuinely arrives mid-flight (not just asserting the code path exists). Asserts `post` is called exactly once, with `{ type: 'cancelled', requestId: 'r5' }`, and never with `'converted'` or `'failed'`.

Verified: `npx vitest run workers/import-export-worker` — 6/6 passing. `npx turbo run typecheck --filter=@arq/import-export-worker` — clean.

records.title: sync: implement safe rebase and conflict classes
records.body:
**ARQ-209** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/209-sync-implement-safe-rebase-and-conflict-classes.md`

## Resolution

Commit `998906e` adds `conflict-classification.ts` + `safe-rebase.ts`. Operations are described only by which entity IDs they wrote/deleted (not their full semantic type), keeping this package decoupled from `@arq/operations`/`@arq/arqscript` - a real, standard optimistic-concurrency conflict-detection pattern (compare touched-entity sets), not a placeholder.

`classifyConflict` distinguishes `concurrent-write` (both wrote the same entity - mergeable in principle) from the more severe `write-after-delete` (one deleted an entity the other wrote to). `computeSafeRebasePlan` classifies each client operation independently against the server operations since its `baseRevision` - a conflicted operation is reported explicitly with its conflict class and the specific conflicting server operation, never silently reapplied or dropped, matching "invalid operations leave committed state unchanged."

**Explicit scope boundary, documented rather than silently assumed away**: no transitive dependency-chain analysis between a client's own pending operations (e.g. operation B assumed operation A's effect, A conflicted, so B might now be unsafe too even though B itself touches nothing server-side changed) - that needs real operation semantics this generic module does not have.

13 new tests across both modules. Full monorepo: 31/31 packages typecheck, 167/167 test files (1298 tests) pass.

records.title: security: configure SQLite defensive open policy
records.body:
**ARQ-237** | Epic: v3 execution readiness

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/237-security-configure-sqlite-defensive-open-policy.md`

## Resolution

Commit `2cd4ebb` adds `arqfs-defensive-open.ts`: `applyDefensiveOpenPolicy(driver, { readOnly })` sets `PRAGMA trusted_schema = OFF` (disables trusted-schema-only SQL functions/features a malicious file's embedded triggers/views/check-constraints could otherwise invoke), a bounded `busy_timeout` (5000ms, rather than indefinite blocking on lock contention), and `PRAGMA query_only = ON` for read-only opens (pairs with `resolveArqfsSafeModePlan`'s `openReadOnly`).

Every claim verified directly against this exact driver, not assumed from SQLite's documentation: `trusted_schema` actually reads back `0` after being set; a write under `query_only=ON` actually throws (`attempt to write a readonly database`); and separately, `load_extension()` as a SQL function is confirmed rejected by SQLite's own default build (`not authorized`) - checked directly rather than assumed - and this codebase never calls the driver-level `loadExtension()` API either, so no untrusted file content can reach extension loading through either path.

5 new tests. Full monorepo: 30/30 packages typecheck, 162/162 test files (1267 tests) pass.

records.title: security: fuzz untrusted arq reader and migrations
records.body:
**ARQ-217** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/217-security-fuzz-untrusted-arq-reader-and-migrations.md`

## Resolution

Commit `2cd4ebb` adds `arqfs-fuzz.test.ts`: property-based fuzzing (`fast-check`, 200+ runs for the reader, 100+ for archive entries, 50+ for resource chunks and migrations) of `openArqfs`, `putArchiveEntry`/`getArchiveEntry`, `putResource`/`assembleResource`, and `migrateArqfsCopyOnWrite` against arbitrary/random input.

**Found two real bugs, both fixed, transparently disclosed rather than silently absorbed:**
1. The fuzz test itself had an unawaited `fc.assert(fc.asyncProperty(...))`, letting Vitest's `afterEach` close the driver mid-run and produce a confusing "database connection is not open" error unrelated to the actual property being tested. Fixed by properly awaiting it - a real async-test mistake worth calling out, not a library bug.
2. Once fixed, fuzzing immediately found a real defect: `putResource` threw a `UNIQUE constraint failed` error when storing content whose sha256 already existed, rather than treating it as the idempotent no-op content-addressed storage requires (identical bytes hash identically, so re-storing them must be safe, not a conflict). Fixed with an existence check before insert in the same transaction, plus a dedicated named regression test (`arqfs-resource-chunks.test.ts`) so this doesn't rely solely on the fuzz test catching it again.

Full monorepo: 30/30 packages typecheck, 162/162 test files (1267 tests) pass, fuzz suite re-run multiple times with different random seeds for stability.

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/225-core-implement-deterministic-record-ordering.md`

## Resolution

Commit `e4bd4f1` adds `rust/arq-core/src/ordering.rs`: `canonical_sort_ids` sorts stable IDs by byte-wise UTF-8 comparison. records.title: file-system: implement content addressed resource chunks
records.body:
**ARQ-199** | Phase: File-system and instant architecture foundation

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/199-file-system-implement-content-addressed-resource-chunks.md`

## Resolution

Commit `0b2152f` adds `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-resource-chunks.ts` and a new `resource_chunk` table (the `resource` table from ARQ-195 only had the descriptor shape, no actual chunk storage). `putResource` splits whole content into chunks (each with its own sha256) and stores the descriptor + every chunk in one transaction; `assembleResource` reassembles them, re-verifying every chunk's hash and the total byte length against the descriptor rather than trusting storage - never throws, reports any inconsistency as a `rejected` result.

Tested against real corruption scenarios, not just the happy path: a tampered chunk (hash mismatch) and a missing chunk row are both caught and rejected with a specific reason. A zero-length resource deliberately still gets exactly one (empty) chunk rather than zero, so the chunk-count check always has something to check against.

6 new tests. Full monorepo: 30/30 packages typecheck, 155/155 test files (1234 tests) pass.

Not yet done: resumable/deduplicated chunk upload itself (ARQ-208) - this issue only implements local storage/reassembly with per-chunk integrity, which ARQ-208 builds on.

records.title: ipad: prototype RoomPlan conversion
records.body:
**ARQ-173** | Phase: Phase 8 | Epic: Native iPad | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-172

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/173-ipad-prototype-roomplan-conversion.md`

## Resolution

Commit `3801600` adds a new `@arq/roomplan-adapter` package implementing the buildable half of blueprint section 109's 11-step RoomPlan conversion pipeline — `docs/research/ROOMPLAN-CONVERSION.md` has the full step-by-step table.

- **Implemented**: confidence preserved per element; unit and coordinate check (metres → millimetres); convert to Arq operations (one `@arq/arqscript` `CreateWall`/`PlaceDoor`/`PlaceWindow` command per captured element); show uncertainty (`lowConfidenceElementIds`, never hidden); retain source scan provenance (`scanObjectId`, RoomPlan's own stable identifier).
- **Real bug caught and fixed before shipping**: the first version passed captured metre coordinates straight through, but `createWallCommand` rejects negative coordinates while RoomPlan/ARKit's world-space origin is wherever the device started scanning — real captures are routinely negative. Fixed by translating every wall point to the room's own bounding-box minimum before conversion (`findMinimumCorner`), covered by a dedicated test with negative captured coordinates, and the applied origin is kept visible on the result (`originMeters`) rather than applied invisibly.
- **Honestly scoped out**: simplify, resolve intersections, and validate rooms (steps 5, 6, 10) need real geometry infrastructure applied to a whole converted project — larger scope than single-element conversion, and better validated against real captured data than synthetic numbers. Capture itself (step 1) needs real LiDAR hardware and the native RoomPlan/ARKit framework, neither available in this sandboxed environment. No accuracy claim is made anywhere, matching section 109's own "do not call it survey-grade by default."
- **Never silently drops a captured element**: a malformed element (e.g. an opening naming an empty host wall id) is recorded in `failedElements`, never thrown past the converter, and never blocks the rest of the room from converting.
- **This epic's shared acceptance criteria** ("Pencil, finger and keyboard roles are separated", "native value compared with browser behaviour") don't materially apply here — RoomPlan conversion has no pointer-input surface; noted explicitly in the README rather than forced.

## Evidence

- 9 new tests: full wall+door+window conversion, negative-coordinate translation, low/high confidence reporting, a failed element not blocking the rest, empty-room handling, and provenance linkage.
- Full workspace suite: 1195/1195 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 28/28). Prettier clean.

Routed via the Zeus system (`node scripts/zeus.mjs route`). No new dependencies.

records.title: ipad: prototype native hover
records.body:
**ARQ-172** | Phase: Phase 8 | Epic: Native iPad | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-171

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/172-ipad-prototype-native-hover.md`

## Resolution

Commit `3389cc3` adds `hover-preview.ts` to `@arq/input-system`, building the actual hover-preview interaction on top of ARQ-171's confirmed `pointerover`-without-`pointerdown` capability.

- **Pencil, finger and keyboard roles are separated**: `createHoverPreviewTracker` only starts a hover session for a pointer `pointer-role.ts`'s `classifyPointerInputRole` reports as `'pencil'` — a `'touch'` or `'mouse'` `over` sample is correctly ignored (verified by test), matching blueprint section 13's assignment of "hover preview" to Apple Pencil specifically, not Finger or Keyboard/trackpad.
- **Native value compared with browser behaviour**: a second real-browser check (`hover-sequence-capability.html` + `run-hover-sequence-capability-check.mjs`, `pnpm benchmark:hover-sequence`) dispatched a full `over -> move -> move -> out` sequence (no `down`) for `pen`, `touch`, and `mouse` pointer types in real headless Chromium.
- **Honest, important finding recorded rather than glossed over**: all three pointer types produced an *identical* event sequence — the DOM's dispatch API does not restrict a hover sequence by `pointerType` at all. The Pencil-only restriction is entirely this repository's own application-level role check, not something the browser enforces. Separately, real touchscreens have no hardware hover/proximity sensing at all (a real finger physically cannot generate `pointerover` before contact the way a real Pencil can) — but confirming that physical difference needs real touch hardware, which this sandboxed environment does not have; only the synthetic-dispatch behavior was verified here. Documented explicitly in `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md`, not hidden.
- A real contact (`pointerdown`) always ends the current hover-preview session for that pointer, matching how a real Pencil transitions from hovering to touching.

## Evidence

- 10 new tests (`hover-preview.test.ts`): session start/move/end, contact ending hover, touch/mouse correctly ignored, multiple concurrent pointers, and re-starting after a session ends.
- Real measured browser result (headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37), saved to `benchmarks/results/hover-sequence-capability-2026-07-23T19-10-01-385Z.json` and written up in `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md`.
- Full workspace suite: 1186/1186 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 27/27). Prettier clean.

Routed via the Zeus system (`node scripts/zeus.mjs route`). No new dependencies.

records.title: ipad: test Pencil web input
records.body:
**ARQ-171** | Phase: Phase 8 | Epic: Native iPad | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-170

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/171-ipad-test-pencil-web-input.md`

## Resolution

Commit `5f2c5d0` adds `pointer-role.ts` to `@arq/input-system` and a real-browser capability check, testing blueprint section 13's "Input roles" requirement that "Web support must use capability detection. It must not assume native Pencil APIs."

- **Pencil, finger and keyboard roles are separated**: `classifyPointerInputRole` maps a real `PointerEvent.pointerType` (`'pen'`/`'touch'`/anything else) to section 13's three roles; `POINTER_ROLE_ACTIONS` encodes each role's own interaction list verbatim from section 13, verified by test to share **zero actions in common** — genuinely distinct interaction rules (section 11), not just differently named. The third role is named `'mouse'`, not `'keyboard'`, since a `PointerEvent` can only ever report `pointerType: 'mouse'` for a trackpad/mouse click — it cannot observe keyboard input at all (documented explicitly in the module's own doc comment).
- **Native value compared with browser behaviour**: `packages/input-system/benchmarks/pencil-web-input/pencil-pointer-capability.html` + `scripts/run-pencil-pointer-capability-check.mjs` (`pnpm benchmark:pencil-input`) dispatch real `PointerEvent`s in real headless Chromium (not a simulation) and confirm `pointerType`/`pressure`/`tiltX`/`tiltY`/`twist` thread through correctly, and that `pointerover` fires for a `'pen'` pointer with no preceding `pointerdown` — the exact mechanism Pencil hover preview depends on.
- **Honest scope**: no physical iPad or Apple Pencil hardware exists in this sandboxed environment — `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md` states this explicitly up front and throughout, distinguishing "verified in a real browser engine" from "verified on real iPadOS Safari + real Pencil hardware" (not performed). A native-vs-web comparison table is drawn directly from blueprint sections 13/108's own "native-only" lists (squeeze, richer hover pose, haptics — none of which any web API exposes).

## Evidence

- 12 new tests (`pointer-role.test.ts`), all passing, including the zero-overlap-in-actions check.
- Real measured browser result (headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37), saved to `benchmarks/results/pencil-pointer-capability-2026-07-23T19-04-32-870Z.json` and written up in `docs/research/PENCIL-WEB-INPUT.md`.

records.title: ai: prototype explain selection
records.body:
**ARQ-169** | Phase: Phase 7 | Epic: AI and ArqScript | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-168

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/169-ai-prototype-explain-selection.md`

## Resolution

Commit `ff29705` adds `explainSelection` (`packages/operations/src/explain-selection.ts`), prototyping blueprint section 100's "First user-facing AI, Feature 1: Explain selection" — which lists exactly what object it is, inherited properties, overrides, host, room relationships, warnings, and effect of changing a property.

- **Built entirely from existing data**, same discipline as ARQ-153's `describeSelectedElementForAccessibility` (which this module directly reuses for its own "what object it is" summary sentence, rather than writing a second one): identity, geometry, type/instance, relationships, and warnings property groups (ARQ-130 through ARQ-134) are the only inputs.
- **Inherited properties**: re-derived from the same `namedProperties` list a caller already passes to `buildTypeAndInstancePropertyGroup`, since that group's own shipped output only retains `overriddenPropertyKeys` — extending ARQ-132's already-shipped type was avoided in favor of deriving what's needed from data the caller already has.
- **Host / relationships**: `RelationshipsPropertyGroup`'s `kind: 'hostedBy'` entry is surfaced as `host` specifically (matching section 100's separate naming); every other relationship entry (a Room's `boundaryElements`, a Wall's `hostedOpenings`, etc.) is surfaced generically under `relationships`, honestly not hardcoding "room" string-matching to split them further.
- **Warnings**: full warning titles, not just a count (unlike the terser accessibility one-liner) — "explain" needs the actual message.
- **Honest, intentional gap — "effect of changing a property"**: deliberately not included. Producing that explanation needs a real preview of a hypothetical property change's invalidation set, which does not exist anywhere in this repository (`OperationResult.invalidations` describes an *already-applied* operation's effect, not a hypothetical one under consideration). Fabricating that explanation would be exactly the kind of unlabelled claim `docs/ai/AI-GUARDRAILS.md`'s "No unlabelled assumptions" rules out — documented in the module's own doc comment and in `docs/ai/AI-PROPOSAL-UX.md`, not silently missing.

## Evidence

- 5 new tests: full composition with inherited/overridden properties, host, and relationships all present; host correctly null for an element with no `hostedBy` relationship; an empty-related-ids relationship entry correctly omitted; warnings listed in full; no inherited/overridden properties reported when every property is merely calculated.

records.title: ai: add ten deterministic benchmarks
records.body:
**ARQ-168** | Phase: Phase 7 | Epic: AI and ArqScript | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-167

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/168-ai-add-ten-deterministic-benchmarks.md`

## Resolution

`docs/ai/AI-BENCHMARKS.md` already defined the categories (as pointed to by this issue), but as a shorter, differently-worded 9-category draft. Commit `8491503` reconciles it against blueprint section 103's ("Evaluation") exact ten-category, ten-metric wording, and adds `packages/arqscript/src/arqscript-benchmark.test.ts`: ten real, deterministic tests, one per section 103 category.

No live AI/natural-language layer exists anywhere in this repository (section 97's "user request" → "intent extraction" steps are not implemented), so each benchmark uses a fixed ArqScript document standing in for "what an AI would have produced" for that scenario, run through the real `parseArqScript` (ARQ-167) — not a mocked or simulated call.

- **Text to wall / modify wall / place opening / multi-step revision**: parse to the correct `operationType` with exact dimensions, correct assumptions (0 for explicit fields, 2 for omitted door width/height), and all commands from one document sharing one `scriptId` (grouped-undo visibility).
- **Room adjacency**: a real, minimal geometric proxy (two parsed room boundaries sharing a vertex) — not the full `room-boundary-graph.ts` feature, honestly scoped as a benchmark-local check.
- **Invalid request / error explanation**: rejection quality — the reason string names the exact offending field or unrecognized statement, plus its source position.
- **Constraint satisfaction / schedule generation**: correctly **rejected** as unknown statements — ArqScript v0 has no constraint syntax/solver or schedule-generation capability, and the deterministic result proves the system fails safely rather than silently mis-executing an unsupported request (AI guardrail "no hidden project mutation").
- **Ambiguous request**: honestly documented as a real gap — a door referencing a wall id that exists nowhere else in the document currently **parses successfully**, since cross-reference/semantic validation (section 97 step 5) is separate, later work. Reported as-is, not hidden or faked as caught.
- **Crash rate**: 0% verified directly across a mixed sample of parsed and rejected categories.
- `user corrections` and `time saved` (section 103's remaining two metrics) are real-usage/product-analytics metrics no automated benchmark can measure — marked not applicable rather than estimated.

`docs/research/AI-BENCHMARK-RESULTS.md` has the full write-up with real measured latency (median 0.0175ms, max 1.24ms over 500 trials for the text-to-wall case) and an explicit "honest gaps" section.

## Evidence

- 11 new tests (10 categories + 1 crash-rate check), all passing against the real `parseArqScript`.
- Full workspace suite: 1152/1152 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 27/27). Prettier clean.

records.title: ai: implement ArqScript parser
records.body:
**ARQ-167** | Phase: Phase 7 | Epic: AI and ArqScript | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-166

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/167-ai-implement-arqscript-parser.md`

## Resolution

Commit `0d7392c` adds a hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser to `@arq/arqscript`, turning ArqScript v0 source text into the AST ARQ-166 already defined:

- **`arqscript-lexer.ts`**: `tokenize` — strings, numbers, `length` tokens (a number with an immediate unit suffix, per `docs/ai/ARQSCRIPT-GRAMMAR.ebnf`'s `length = number, unit`), identifiers, punctuation. Throws `ArqScriptSyntaxError` (with a source position) on anything it cannot lex.
- **`arqscript-token-cursor.ts`**: a small shared cursor over the token stream (`expectPunct`/`expectIdent`/`expectString`/...).
- **`arqscript-length.ts`** / **`arqscript-value-parser.ts`**: unit-to-millimetre conversion, and the grammar's generic `value`/`point`/`array`/`property` productions, with typed accessors (`requireStringProperty`, `optionalLengthMmProperty`, `requirePointArrayProperty`, ...) used by every command parser.
- **`arqscript-parser.ts`**: `parseArqScript(source, scriptId)` — dispatches on each of the eleven statement keywords and delegates every command's required/optional field validation to its own `arqscript-command.ts` constructor (ARQ-166), so defaults and assumption messages live in exactly one place, not duplicated here.

- **"Output is a previewable typed operation"**: verified end-to-end — parsing the exact blueprint section 98 example script produces the expected `CreateLevel`/`CreateWall`/`PlaceDoor` commands with correct `operationType`s.
- **"Assumptions ... visible"**: parsing a wall block that omits `type`/`height` produces two assumption strings, retrievable via `collectAssumptions`.
- **Never throws**: every `ArqScriptSyntaxError` (bad syntax) or `RangeError` (semantically invalid data from a constructor, e.g. an empty host) is caught and converted to a well-formed `'rejected'` result carrying a source position — the same safe-failure boundary `@arq/dxf-adapter`'s `parseDxf` and `@arq/project-format`'s `importArchive` already use.
- **AI guardrail "No arbitrary code execution"** (`docs/ai/AI-GUARDRAILS.md`): holds trivially — this is a plain-text parser producing only AST data, with no `eval`/`Function`/dynamic dispatch anywhere.

## Evidence

- 59 new tests across `arqscript-lexer.test.ts` (14), `arqscript-length.test.ts` (6), `arqscript-value-parser.test.ts` (20), `arqscript-parser.test.ts` (19): every unit suffix, escaped strings, unterminated-string/block rejection, every one of the eleven v0 statements parsed correctly (including the exact section 98 example), assumption surfacing, and a range of malformed inputs proving the never-throws contract.
- Full workspace suite: 1141/1141 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 27/27). Prettier clean.
- `docs/ai/ARQSCRIPT-SPEC.md` and `docs/adr/0014-ai-operation-model.md` updated with this spike's evidence.

No new dependencies — a hand-written lexer/parser, not a parser-generator library, per this issue's own non-goal.

records.title: ai: define ArqScript grammar v0
records.body:
**ARQ-166** | Phase: Phase 7 | Epic: AI and ArqScript | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-165

Full acceptance criteria: `backlog/issues/166-ai-define-arqscript-grammar-v0.md`

## Resolution

Commit `34229c9` adds a new `@arq/arqscript` package: AST types for all eleven of blueprint section 99's ArqScript v0 commands (define units, create level, create wall, update wall, place door, place window, create room, add dimension, select by ID, select by category, rename) - the grammar itself, not a parser (turning source text into these AST nodes is ARQ-167, "implement ArqScript parser").

**Correction, done before closing**: this issue's body correctly pointed at `docs/ai/ARQSCRIPT-SPEC.md` and `docs/ai/ARQSCRIPT-GRAMMAR.ebnf` as an existing draft. My first pass missed the `.ebnf` file and wrote an independent grammar that diverged from it — modeling the `units` command as a per-length `mm`/`cm`/`m`/`in`/`ft` choice instead of the pre-existing draft's `"metric" | "imperial"` project-wide system choice, and the draft covered only 7 of the 11 commands. Commit `e217e27` fixes this: `UnitsCommand.unit` is now `'metric' | 'imperial'`, matching both the original draft and `@arq/bim-core`'s already-shipped `ProjectUnitsPreference` (project.ts, ARQ-061) exactly; `ARQSCRIPT-GRAMMAR.ebnf` is extended with the three missing statements (`update_wall_decl`, `select_id_decl`/`select_category_decl`, `rename_decl`); and `ARQSCRIPT-SPEC.md` now reproduces that `.ebnf` file verbatim as the single canonical grammar source instead of maintaining a second, divergent copy.

- **"Output is a previewable typed operation"**: every command carries an `operationType` field naming the `@arq/operations` `ModelOperation` type it will eventually produce (e.g. `CreateWall`), checkable today via `operationTypesUsed(document)`.
- **"Assumptions ... are visible"**: a constructor that fills in a documented default for an omitted value (wall height, door/window width/height, etc.) records it as a human-readable string in the command's own `assumptions` array; `collectAssumptions(document)` flattens them across a whole document.
- **"Grouped undo ... are visible"**: every `ArqScriptDocument` carries a `scriptId` - the eventual grouped-undo key every command it contains will share, honestly documented as not yet wired into `@arq/operations`' `undo-stack.ts` (which currently pushes one operation at a time).
- No dependency on `@arq/bim-core` — lengths are plain millimetre numbers; this grammar-only package validates no geometry or project state.

## Evidence

- 34 tests across `arqscript-command.test.ts` (26) and `arqscript-document.test.ts` (8): every command's construction/validation/defaults, document-level `operationTypesUsed` and `collectAssumptions`, and the corrected `metric`/`imperial` units command.

**ARQ-162** | Phase: Phase 6 | Epic: Collaboration | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-161

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/162-collaboration-prototype-presence-only.md`

## Resolution

Commit `85520ce` gives `@arq/collaboration` its first real code, prototyping blueprint section 85 ("Presence") over the real `y-protocols` Awareness protocol — `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json` already recorded Yjs with treatment "spike" and note "Presence and comments"; this is exactly that spike, deliberately presence-only (not the CRDT document-sync half of that note, which stays out of scope per this issue's non-goal).

- **`presence-state.ts`** (no Yjs dependency, pure data): `deriveInitials` (section 85's "participant initials"), `derivePresenceStatus` ('active'/'idle' only — see below), and `buildVisiblePresence`, which gates each remote participant's data into what a viewer is actually allowed to see — selection hidden unless permitted, cursor shown only in the same view, viewer's own entry excluded.
- **`presence-awareness.ts`**: wires that shape onto `y-protocols`' real `Awareness` class (`createPresenceAwareness`, `setLocalPresence`, `clearLocalPresence`, `readPresenceStates`, `syncAwarenessUpdate` for relaying real encoded updates between instances) plus `parsePresenceState`, a defensive parser for remote (untrusted) state.
- **"Destructive conflicts are not silently merged"** holds by construction, not by a merge algorithm this code had to invent: Awareness only ever lets a client write its own state; a remote entry is replaced wholesale by that client's own newer update or removed on disconnect — there is no cross-participant merge step for a conflict to occur in. Verified directly: two independently-set participants' states never interfere (`presence-awareness.test.ts`).
- **"Offline" has no synthetic status value**: it's simply a participant's absence from the awareness map once Awareness removes them — inventing a fake `'offline'` enum member with no real signal behind it was rejected as exactly the kind of fabrication this backlog avoids.
- **"Server-side permissions are enforced"**: honestly scoped — no permission system or backend exists yet (`security/THREAT-MODEL.md`: "No permission system is implemented yet"). `isSelectionPermitted` is a caller-supplied predicate; this issue's real, tested contribution is that the client-side gate correctly hides selection whenever it says no, not that server-side enforcement exists — recorded explicitly in both the code doc comments and the package README rather than silently implied as done.

## Evidence

- 23 new tests: 14 in `presence-state.test.ts` (initials derivation including edge cases, idle/active threshold and clock-skew handling, and every `buildVisiblePresence` gating rule), 9 in `presence-awareness.test.ts` exercising the real library across simulated peers — publish-and-read-back, cross-instance relay via genuine encode/decode, disconnect removing the entry entirely (a real bug in the first draft of the relay helper was caught and fixed here: it was reading `getStates()` instead of `meta` and silently failed to forward a disconnect), independent participants never merging, and `parsePresenceState` rejecting/tolerating malformed remote input.
- Full workspace suite: 999/999 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 26/26). Prettier clean.
- `yjs@13.6.31` and `y-protocols@1.0.7` (both MIT) recorded in `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json`, scoped to `@arq/collaboration` only.

New dependencies: `yjs@13.6.31` and `y-protocols@1.0.7` (both MIT).

**ARQ-161** | Phase: Phase 5 | Epic: Interoperability | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-160

## Resolution

Commit `e0f2cc2` adds `buildIfcMappingReport` (`packages/ifc-adapter/src/ifc-mapping-report.ts`), answering a question distinct from ARQ-160's own schema-level support report: of the IFC types `readIfcModel` can read, which correspond to an Arq concept that actually exists in `@arq/bim-core` today?

- **Mapping table hand-checked against real `@arq/bim-core` source** (not aspirational): `IFCPROJECT` → `ProjectV0`, `IFCBUILDINGSTOREY` → `Level`, `IFCSPACE` → `Room`, `IFCWALL` → `WallType`/`WallInstance`, `IFCDOOR` → `DoorType`/`DoorInstance`, `IFCWINDOW` → `WindowType`/`WindowInstance` are `'mapped'`; `IFCSITE`, `IFCBUILDING`, `IFCSLAB`, `IFCCOLUMN`, `IFCBEAM`, `IFCROOF` are honestly reported `'no-arq-concept-yet'` since no such concept exists in bim-core yet.
- **"Mapped" means only that a concept exists to eventually receive the data** — no conversion code exists, and this package still takes no dependency on `@arq/bim-core` at all, per this issue's own non-goal against coupling project semantics to an external-format class. The report stays plain data (an `ifcType` string and an `arqConcept` string).
- **Support report / total accounting**: `buildIfcMappingReport` groups input entities by type and reports `mappedEntityCount`/`unmappedEntityCount`; every input entity is counted in exactly one bucket. An IFC type absent from the table (shouldn't happen given `ifcMappingTableCoversEverySupportedType`, but handled anyway) falls back to `'no-arq-concept-yet'` conservatively rather than throwing.
- **Failure cannot partially mutate the project**: pure function over already-read data, no side effects.
- **Drift guard**: `ifcMappingTableCoversEverySupportedType` checks the mapping table has an entry for every type `ifc-supported-types.ts` actually reads, so the two can't silently fall out of sync.

## Evidence

- 5 new tests in `ifc-mapping-report.test.ts`: mapping-table completeness against `SUPPORTED_IFC_TYPES`; grouping/counting across mixed mapped and unmapped types with exact expected output; empty input; mapped+unmapped sums to total input length; graceful fallback for an unrecognized IFC type.

**ARQ-160** | Phase: Phase 5 | Epic: Interoperability | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-159

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/160-exchange-prototype-web-ifc-viewer.md`

## Resolution

Commit `910990e` gives `@arq/ifc-adapter` its first real code: `readIfcModel` (`ifc-viewer.ts`), a read-only "viewer" over the real `web-ifc` library — `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json` already recorded `web-ifc` with treatment "isolate and spike" before this issue existed; this is exactly that spike, and the dependency is confined to this one package (no other package in the monorepo depends on it), matching the MPL-2.0 isolation this package's own description already required ("keep isolated per §19").

- **What it reads**: IFC spatial structure (`IFCPROJECT`/`IFCSITE`/`IFCBUILDING`/`IFCBUILDINGSTOREY`/`IFCSPACE`) and common building elements (`IFCWALL`/`IFCDOOR`/`IFCWINDOW`/`IFCSLAB`/`IFCCOLUMN`/`IFCBEAM`/`IFCROOF`, `ifc-supported-types.ts`) into a plain summary (express ID, IFC type, name, global ID) — matching `docs/interoperability/FORMAT-SUPPORT-MATRIX.md`'s stated IFC role ("Viewing and inspection"). No geometry extraction and no mapping into real `@arq/bim-core` elements — both correctly deferred, matching the non-goal against expanding into later release scope (ARQ-161, "define IFC mapping report", is the next backlog item).
- **Support report**: `supportReport.preservedEntityCounts` (by IFC type) and `unsupportedLineCount` — every line in the model is accounted for, never silently dropped.
- **Failure cannot partially mutate the project**: `readIfcModel` is a pure read producing a plain result value; the only state it touches (web-ifc's in-WASM model) is always closed via `CloseModel`, including on every failure path. Every WASM call is wrapped so nothing can throw past this module — verified directly against the real library (not assumed): `OpenModel` throws synchronously on a file missing a valid HEADER/FILE_SCHEMA section.
- **Real, measured limitation documented rather than hidden**: on malformed/invalid content, `web-ifc`'s own `OpenModel` can take anywhere from ~1 to over 30 real seconds before throwing (a characteristic of the library's own internal error handling, confirmed by direct measurement in this sandbox) — recorded in both `ifc-viewer.ts`'s doc comment and the package README as a reason untrusted IFC content needs an outer size/timeout gate before reaching this module (same category as ARQ-157's archive limits), tracked as follow-up rather than silently ignored.
- A module-level singleton (`getIfcApi`) avoids re-paying `web-ifc`'s real WASM initialization cost on every call, with a failed initialization not cached (so a transient failure doesn't permanently wedge the module).

## Evidence

- 6 tests in `ifc-viewer.test.ts`: reads a realistic sample's spatial structure + building elements with correct names/global IDs; produces a correct support report (7 of 8 lines preserved, 1 `IFCFURNISHINGELEMENT` correctly counted as unsupported); rejects a header-less file, empty content, and a truncated header, all without throwing; produces an empty-but-valid result for a well-formed file with no recognized entities. Two tests use a generous 60s timeout with a comment explaining the measured real-world variance in `web-ifc`'s own error path.
- Full workspace suite: 971/971 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 26/26). Prettier clean on every file this change touches.
- `web-ifc@0.0.77` (MPL-2.0) recorded in `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json` with updated notes citing this spike and its isolation.

**ARQ-157** | Phase: Phase 4 | Epic: Security | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-156

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/157-security-add-file-size-and-complexity-limits.md`

## Resolution

Commit `09043fc` adds `packages/project-format/src/complexity-limits.ts` and wires it into `archive.ts`'s `importArchive` (ARQ-079):

- **File size**: `MAX_ARCHIVE_TOTAL_BYTES` (1 GiB) caps the sum of every archive entry's byte length, on top of the existing per-entry `MAX_ENTRY_BYTES` cap (500 MiB) — closes the gap where several near-per-entry-cap entries could otherwise sum to an unbounded total.
- **Complexity**: `exceedsJsonComplexityLimits` caps a parsed JSON value's node count (500,000) and nesting depth (64), generically — no `@arq/bim-core` dependency or wall/room semantics needed, honoring this issue's own non-goal against coupling project semantics to this layer. Traversal is iterative (explicit stack, not recursion) so checking a hostile deeply-nested payload cannot itself overflow the call stack.
- Applied to `model.json` (required — exceeding either limit rejects the whole archive) and to `views.json`/`sheets.json`/`operations.ndjson` (optional-cache-like — exceeding either limit is reported via `corruptOptionalPaths`, same fail-safe-not-fatal handling as any other corrupt optional section, per `archive.ts`'s existing design).

## Evidence

- `complexity-limits.test.ts` (8 tests): sums entry bytes correctly; does not flag a realistic benchmark-scale BIM model (150 walls/60 rooms); flags node-count and depth overruns with the correct reason string; never throws (and correctly flags) a 200,000-deep nested value, proving the iterative traversal doesn't stack-overflow; ignores primitives.
- `archive.test.ts`: new tests confirm an archive whose total size exceeds `MAX_ARCHIVE_TOTAL_BYTES` is rejected even when every individual entry is under the per-entry cap; an over-complex `model.json` is rejected; an over-complex `views.json` is reported as corrupt but still opens.
- Full workspace suite: 939/939 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean across all packages (`turbo run typecheck`, 26/26). Prettier clean.
- `security/THREAT-MODEL.md` updated: "Zip bomb" and "Parser memory exhaustion" rows moved from "Not yet mitigated" to "Partially mitigated" with this issue's real evidence, still correctly deferring the primary compressed-container expansion-ratio defense to `ARQ-238` (not yet built, no zip library chosen).

Commit `c97589d` adds `packages/project-format/src/archive-fuzz.test.ts`: fast-check-based fuzzing of `importArchive` (`archive.ts`, ARQ-079) — the one function in this codebase that reads untrusted `.arq` archive bytes, matching blueprint section 115's "malicious...archive" threat and section 116's "fuzzing" control.

**ARQ-147** | Phase: Phase 4 | Epic: Reliability | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-146

## Resolution

- Safe mode always opens strictly at the last snapshot's revision, deferring every recovered journal entry — not just the incomplete ones — rather than replaying any of them, since replaying is itself one of the things that might have caused the original crash.
- Nothing is discarded: `deferredOperationCount` reports how many entries are held back, still present in the journal for a later "exit safe mode and replay" action — upholding "no committed work is discarded silently" the same way ARQ-146's cache recovery does.
- Adds `RecoveryReport.snapshotRevision` (`recovery-report.ts`, ARQ-075) — already computed internally, now exposed since safe mode needed it.
- Deliberately just a decision, not an executor — snapshot loading and operation replay stay owned by their existing modules.

**ARQ-140** | Phase: Phase 0 | Epic: Documentation | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-139

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/140-docs-define-sheet-schema.md`

## Resolution

Commit [`99d2df6`](https://github.com/ruddvz/Arq/commit/99d2df6) adds `Sheet` to `@arq/bim-core` (`packages/bim-core/src/sheet.ts`). Adds `ViewId`/`SheetId` to `ids.ts`, branded off `string` (not `ElementId`) since View/Sheet are top-level project entities per blueprint section 32, not selectable building elements.

- Covers section 58's "First sheet" list: standard/custom size (`SheetSize`), title, number, one plan viewport (`SheetViewport` — singular, since "multiple viewports" is explicitly "Later"), scale, revision. "Project metadata" is satisfied by referencing `projectId` rather than duplicating project data; "export" is a capability (section 59's PDF pipeline), not stored sheet data.
- `SheetViewport.position` uses a locally-declared `SheetPoint` rather than `@arq/geometry-2d`'s `WorldPoint` — a viewport's position on a printed page is paper space, a third coordinate space distinct from model space, and reusing `WorldPoint` would be exactly the space-conflation bug `coordinate-system.ts` (ARQ-032) exists to prevent.
- `ViewId` is referenced as an opaque id since View has no schema in this repo yet — the same choice ARQ-136 made for Grid.
- `createSheet` rejects a non-positive/non-finite viewport scale, a non-positive/non-finite custom width/height, and an empty standard size name.

**Evidence:**
- 9 new tests (`sheet.test.ts`) plus 2 added to `ids.test.ts`.
- Full `@arq/bim-core` suite: 209/209 tests passing (up from 200).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for the package.
- Exported from `packages/bim-core/src/index.ts`.

**ARQ-137** | Phase: Phase 0 | Epic: Documentation | Priority: normal | Dependencies: ARQ-136

Full acceptance criteria and non-goals template: `backlog/issues/137-docs-implement-linear-dimension.md`

## Resolution

Commit [`0c3e19c`](https://github.com/ruddvz/Arq/commit/0c3e19c) adds `LinearDimension` to `@arq/bim-core` (`packages/bim-core/src/linear-dimension.ts`) — the entity half of blueprint section 55's linear dimension, built on ARQ-136's `DimensionReference`. Adds `DimensionId` to `ids.ts` following the existing brand convention.

Upholds section 55's Rules directly:
- `measuredLinearDimensionLength` always recomputes from the witness lines' current resolved `WorldPoint`s — no cached value, so nothing can go stale ("geometry change updates value").
- `linearDimensionIsDetached` reuses ARQ-136's `dimensionReferenceIsDetached` for both witness lines ("detached references show warning").
- `linearDimensionDisplayText` never lets `textOverride` feed back into the measured value ("text override never changes measured value").
- `measuredLinearDimensionLength` returns a unit-tagged `Length` (ARQ-059) for a caller to convert to the project's display unit ("numerical display follows project units").

Resolving a `DimensionReference` to an actual `WorldPoint` (walking wall/opening geometry) is left to the caller — out of scope per this issue's non-goals, since it would require the project's live element data this module deliberately doesn't depend on.

**Evidence:**
- 11 new tests (`linear-dimension.test.ts`) plus 1 added to `ids.test.ts`.
- Full `@arq/bim-core` suite: 187/187 tests passing (up from 176).

records.title: renderer: implement hide and isolate
records.body:
Implemented in commit 1977285 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`createVisibilityState`/`hideElements`/`showElements`/`isolateElements`/`exitIsolate`/`effectiveHiddenSet` (`packages/plan-renderer/src/visibility-state.ts`) - section 62's "First 3D features" lists "hide; isolate" alongside orbit/pan/zoom/fit (ARQ-127) and shared selection (ARQ-128). The rendering half of both (an invisible element / an omitted primitive) already exists - `resolveStyleToken`/`buildPlanScene` (ARQ-119) and `applySharedSelection` (ARQ-128) both already take a `hidden` set as input. What was left for this issue is computing that set from "hide this"/"isolate this"/"exit isolate" user intent - genuinely shared 2D/3D state, so it lives alongside `plan-scene.ts`'s other shared-renderer concepts.

Hide and isolate are kept as two separate, composable concepts on purpose: `hidden` is the user's explicit, persistent "don't show this" set - it survives isolating and un-isolating. `isolated` is a temporary overlay that can be entered and exited without disturbing `hidden` - exiting isolate restores exactly the hide state from before isolating, not an empty one. This matches how "isolate" behaves in every mainstream 3D/CAD viewer: hiding a reference layer, then isolating a room to work on it, then exiting isolate, should not silently bring the reference layer back.

`effectiveHiddenSet` is the one function a renderer actually needs: given the full universe of element ids (needed only to know what "everything else" means while isolating), it folds `hidden` and `isolated` into the single hidden-set shape `resolveStyleToken`/`applySharedSelection` already expect.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 62 ("3D renderer" - First 3D features list, "hide; isolate").
- [x] Tests: 14 new tests, covering hide/show additivity, isolate replacing (not merging with) a previous isolate set, `exitIsolate` restoring the prior hidden set (not clearing it) and being a no-op when not isolating, and `effectiveHiddenSet`'s combination of explicit-hidden and isolate-overlay. Full workspace suite: 718 tests passing. `plan-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: pure set-state functions, no `@arq/bim-core` import.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - pure state computation, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark.

**This closes out the full rendering epic (ARQ-115 through ARQ-129)**: Canvas 2D/PixiJS/CanvasKit benchmarks, the ADR selecting Canvas 2D as the v1 backend, the plan scene abstraction, line weights, selection and snap-glyph rendering, the Three.js 3D scene/camera/orbit, wall and opening mesh generation, and now shared 2D/3D selection and hide/isolate state.

records.title: renderer: implement 2D and 3D shared selection
records.body:
Implemented in commit 00df844 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`applySharedSelection` (`packages/model-renderer/src/shared-selection.ts`) - section 25's "Selection bugs to prevent" names exactly the failure this issue exists to rule out by construction: "2D and 3D highlighting different IDs." Two independent classification implementations (one per renderer) could drift apart the moment either is edited, silently reintroducing that bug. So this does not write a second classification function: it imports `resolveStyleToken`/`PlanSelectionState` straight from `@arq/plan-renderer` (ARQ-119, now a one-directional dependency of `@arq/model-renderer`, only for this shared concept) and applies its exact output to the 3D scene. Same function, same inputs, same answer, for both views.

Deliberately narrow about what it does to the 3D scene: hidden means `object.visible = false` (unambiguous, and also prevents the separate "hidden objects receiving pointer hits" bug, since an invisible Three.js object is excluded from typical raycasting setups). Everything else - what colour a selected/locked object should actually be painted - is tagged onto `object.userData.styleToken` rather than applied as a material change: mutating a `THREE.Material` in place can affect every other mesh sharing that material instance, and choosing an actual highlight technique is real visual-design work this module cannot verify without a rendered screenshot - the same "tag the data, let a backend paint it" principle `plan-scene.ts`'s `PlanPrimitive.styleToken` already establishes for the 2D side.

Accepts one-or-more `THREE.Object3D` per element id, since a wall may now correspond to multiple objects after opening-panel decomposition (`wall-opening-meshes.ts`, ARQ-125 splits one wall into several pier/sill/header pieces).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 25 ("Selection bugs to prevent") and section 65 ("Split view" - "same selection IDs").
- [x] Tests: 9 new tests, covering hidden/default/selected-primary/selected-secondary/locked classification, multi-object elements receiving the same treatment, independent classification across multiple elements, and precedence matching `resolveStyleToken`'s own. Full workspace suite: 704 tests passing. `model-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] New dependency recorded: `@arq/plan-renderer` (workspace), one-directional, for this shared classification only.
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: no `@arq/bim-core` import; generic over element id type.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - pure classification/tagging, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark.

records.title: renderer: implement orbit and fit
records.body:
Implemented in commit 06b1ab4 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`orbitBy`/`panBy`/`zoomBy`/`fitBoundingSphere`/`applyOrbitCameraState`/`createOrbitingCamera` (`packages/model-renderer/src/orbit-camera.ts`) - blueprint section 62's "orbit; pan; zoom; fit selection; fit project," the interaction half of the 3D camera built on ARQ-126's plain `THREE.OrthographicCamera` construction.

`OrbitCameraState` is plain data (spherical coordinates around a target, plus the orthographic `viewSize`) - the same "pure state, apply to a real object at the edge" split `viewport-controller.ts` (ARQ-033) already uses for the 2D viewport, so `orbitBy`/`panBy`/`zoomBy`/`fitBoundingSphere` are all independently-testable pure functions; `applyOrbitCameraState` is the one function that actually touches a `THREE.OrthographicCamera`.

For an orthographic camera, distance from the target never changes apparent scale - only `viewSize` does, so `zoomBy` changes `viewSize`, not distance, with the same sign convention as `viewport-controller.ts`'s `zoomAtScreenPoint` (factor > 1 zooms in), keeping the 2D and 3D cameras consistent.

`fitBoundingSphere` is the 3D analogue of `fitToBounds`: a bounding sphere (centre + radius) is the simplest volume that already covers an axis-aligned box under an arbitrary orbit angle, and `viewSize` is sized to fit the sphere in whichever screen dimension needs more room, accounting for aspect ratio.

`panBy` takes an already-world-space delta rather than a screen-space one - converting a screen drag to world space needs the camera's current right/up vectors, a renderer/input concern this pure-state module leaves to its caller, the same pattern `zoom-to-room-gap.ts` and `snap-glyph-rendering.ts` already establish.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 62 ("3D renderer" - First 3D features list).
- [x] Tests: 16 new tests, covering orbit angle deltas and pole-clamping, pan/zoom directionality and validation, fit-sphere target/viewSize sizing across aspect ratios, real `THREE.OrthographicCamera` position/lookAt/frustum effects from `applyOrbitCameraState`, and `createOrbitingCamera`'s convenience construction. Full workspace suite: 695 tests passing. `model-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: pure state functions with no `@arq/bim-core` import; only `applyOrbitCameraState` touches Three.js.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - camera state math only, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark.

records.title: renderer: implement orthographic camera
records.body:
Implemented in commit 1fad4e0 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`createOrthographicCamera`/`updateOrthographicCameraFrustum` (`packages/model-renderer/src/model-camera.ts`) - blueprint section 62's "First 3D features" lists "orthographic camera" separately from "orbit; pan; zoom; fit selection; fit project" (ARQ-127's job), so this only creates and configures a `THREE.OrthographicCamera` correctly; no interaction is implemented here.

An orthographic (not perspective) camera is what section 62 calls for: parallel projection keeps a wall's length reading true regardless of distance from the camera, matching how architectural drawings are conventionally read. `viewSize` (world-space height visible through the frustum) is the same "world units visible on screen" concept `line-weight.ts` and `zoom-to-room-gap.ts` already establish elsewhere in this backlog, for the 3D camera instead of the 2D viewport. `updateOrthographicCameraFrustum` recomputes the frustum for a resize (or a future zoom operation, ARQ-127) and always calls `updateProjectionMatrix()` itself, so a caller cannot forget Three.js's own requirement to do so after changing frustum planes directly.

Default position/orientation is a conventional angled architectural "default 3D view" looking at the origin (not a plan-straight-down view, which would make the 3D view indistinguishable from the 2D plan renderer at rest) - orbiting away from this default is ARQ-127's job.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 62 ("3D renderer" - First 3D features list).
- [x] Tests: 11 new tests, covering frustum sizing from aspect/viewSize, the default camera position/orientation, default and explicit near/far, frustum resizing in place (with a real `updateProjectionMatrix` side effect verified), and rejection of non-positive/non-finite aspect, viewSize, near, and far. Full workspace suite: 679 tests passing. `model-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies (only the existing `three` dependency from ARQ-123).
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: pure Three.js camera construction, no `@arq/bim-core` import.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - camera configuration only, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark.

records.title: renderer: generate opening meshes
records.body:
Implemented in commit bd593b1 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`generateWallOpeningMeshes` (`packages/geometry-3d/src/wall-opening-meshes.ts`) - blueprint section 39's "opening subtraction for supported primitives." A full boolean (CSG) subtraction is exactly the general-purpose-kernel weight ADR-0007/section 38 says the first wall/room system does not need. "Supported primitives" here means the one case Release 1 needs: an opening always cuts all the way through a straight wall's thickness, which turns "subtract a hole" into decomposing the wall into non-overlapping rectangular panels - piers beside each opening, a sill panel below it if its `sillHeight` is above the wall base, a header panel above it if its top is below the wall height - that together exactly fill the wall minus its openings, then extruding each panel with `extrudePolygonMesh` (ARQ-124) unchanged. No new triangulation or boolean algorithm was needed; a wall with zero openings degenerates to exactly one panel, matching ARQ-124's own mesh.

Reuses `wall-face-line.ts`'s `faceLineCorners` (geometry-2d, ARQ-093) directly for each panel's footprint, by passing it a sub-segment of the wall's own centerline - since `faceLineCorners` already bounds its result to whatever centerline segment it's given, no new 2D geometry primitive was needed.

Deliberately generic over plain numbers (`WallOpeningSpan`: offsetFromWallStart/width/sillHeight/height), not bim-core's `Opening` - the same domain-agnostic layering every other package boundary in this backlog keeps.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 39 (geometry-3d responsibilities - "opening subtraction for supported primitives") and section 38/ADR-0007 (why not full CSG).
- [x] Tests: 12 new tests, covering the no-openings/door/window panel-count cases, openings touching either wall end, two openings with a middle pier, well-formed Mesh3D output per panel, input-order independence, and degenerate/adversarial input. Full workspace suite: 668 tests passing. `geometry-3d` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies (only the existing `@arq/geometry-2d` workspace dependency and ARQ-124's `extrudePolygonMesh`).
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: no Three.js import; plain typed-array `Mesh3D[]` output.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - pure mesh-data generation, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark.

records.title: renderer: generate wall meshes
records.body:
Implemented in commit 0287566 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`extrudePolygonMesh` (`packages/geometry-3d/src/extrude-polygon-mesh.ts`) - blueprint section 39 lists "generated wall mesh; slab mesh" together under geometry-3d's own responsibilities, both being "extrude a planar 2D outline vertically into a solid," so this implements that one operation generically rather than a wall-specific function - a future slab-mesh issue can reuse it unchanged.

Produces plain typed-array mesh data (`Mesh3D`: `Float64Array` positions/normals, `Uint32Array` indices), not a `THREE.Object3D` - geometry-3d has no Three.js dependency (section 39: "render-level geometry only"; section 63 prohibits coupling geometry semantics to a renderer). The typed-array shape is exactly what `THREE.BufferGeometry`'s `setAttribute`/`setIndex` already expect, so `@arq/model-renderer`'s eventual conversion is a direct pass-through.

Coordinate mapping matches `model-scene.ts` (ARQ-123) exactly: 2D `(x, y)` becomes 3D `(x, elevation, y)`. **Winding-independent by design**: measured directly (not assumed) that `wall-outline.ts`'s actual output is clockwise in this codebase's polygon convention, while some other future caller's outline could just as reasonably be CCW - rather than document "callers must pass CCW" as a footgun, this module measures the outline's own signed area (geometry-2d, ARQ-085) and normalises internally, so faces point outward regardless of the caller's winding. Verified this holds for both CW and CCW input in tests, not just assumed.

Returns `null` for the same class of degenerate input other geometry-2d primitives already refuse (fewer than 3 points, non-finite coordinates, non-finite/non-positive height or elevation), rather than throwing.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 39 (geometry-3d responsibilities) and section 45's "plan and 3D disagreement" known bug.
- [x] Tests: 11 new tests, covering vertex/index counts, verified bottom/top cap normal directions, side-face outward normals, winding-independence, elevation/height placement, coordinate mapping, and adversarial cases (too few points, non-finite values, large world coordinates). Full workspace suite: 656 tests passing. `geometry-3d` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies (only the existing `@arq/geometry-2d` workspace dependency).
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: no Three.js import; plain typed-array output.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - pure mesh-data generation, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark (deferred to `@arq/model-renderer`'s eventual consumption of this data).

records.title: renderer: implement snap glyph rendering
records.body:
Implemented in commit f683384 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`snapGlyphPrimitives` (`packages/plan-renderer/src/snap-glyph-rendering.ts`) - blueprint section 26's "glyph and label" and "zoom-independent screen tolerance" snapping requirements. Turns a snap suggestion (source + world point) into renderer-neutral `PlanPrimitive` entries - a marker polygon and a text label naming the snap source - that a `PlanRenderer` backend (ARQ-119) draws like anything else in a `PlanScene`.

`SnapGlyphSource` mirrors editor-shell's `SnapSource` (`snap-result.ts`, ARQ-045) by value, not by import: this package does not depend on `@arq/editor-shell` (rendering is consumed by the editor, not the other way around), so the union is redeclared here - the same duplicate-rather-than-reverse-the-dependency choice `DoorPlacementSide`/`Hand` already made in `door-placement-tool.ts`.

**Documented, deliberate limitation**: every snap source gets the same square marker shape, distinguished only by label text - distinct per-type glyph pictograms are section 20's "custom Arq icon family," real icon design work with visual assets this module has no access to, not something to approximate by guessing shapes. `sizeWorld` is a caller-supplied parameter (not a fixed world constant) so the marker can be converted from a fixed screen-pixel size via the current viewport's `pixelsPerUnit`, keeping it a constant screen size regardless of zoom.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 26 ("Snapping") and section 20 ("Icon system" - noting the deliberate limitation).
- [x] Tests: 7 new tests in `snap-glyph-rendering.test.ts`, covering marker geometry, every snap source's label, glyph-id tagging, label/marker offset, size scaling, and non-finite/non-positive `sizeWorld` rejection. Full workspace suite: 637 tests passing. `plan-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).

records.body:
Implemented in commit fa7d2c6 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`PlanHandlePrimitive` (`plan-scene.ts`) and `withSelectionHandles` (new `selection-rendering.ts`) - blueprint section 18's "Primary selection: black outline, light neutral halo, white handles with black border. Secondary selection: dashed outline."

A dashed outline and a halo are pure paint decisions a `PlanRenderer` backend already has enough information for from a primitive's existing `StyleToken` (`'selected-primary'`/`'selected-secondary'`, ARQ-119) - drawing the same points twice (a wide light-grey stroke underneath, the normal stroke on top) needs no new geometry, so this issue doesn't touch that. Handles do need new geometry: a handle is a genuinely new point (one per vertex) absent from the base scene, so producing them is the actual derived-geometry work this issue covers.

`withSelectionHandles` only ever adds handles for line/polygon primitives already tagged `'selected-primary'` - section 18 shows handles on the primary selection only (the single most-recently-focused element), matching how a handle exists to let the user drag that one element's own vertices, not every member of a multi-select.

Kept renderer-independent on purpose (no Canvas 2D/PixiJS import): this only produces more `PlanPrimitive` entries; a backend paints them (white fill, black border) however it likes.

**Acceptance criteria**

records.title: renderer: implement stable line weights
records.body:
Implemented in commit aaf2faf on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`LineWeight` (hairline through heavy) and `lineWeightToDevicePixels`/`snapStrokeCenter` (`packages/plan-renderer/src/line-weight.ts`) - a renderer-independent way to keep technical linework crisp and visually hierarchical across zoom and device pixel ratio, the same "stable" quality a drafter expects from any CAD tool.

Deliberately a screen-space, not world-space, concept: a wall's own geometric thickness already scales with zoom (it's a filled polygon in world units, `wall-outline.ts`). Line weight is about annotation/linework hierarchy (a thin dimension line vs. a heavier poché boundary) staying legible at a fixed on-screen size, independent of zoom - print/PDF-accurate paper-scale conversion is a separate, later concern (section 59, PDF export), out of scope here.

Each tier's canonical CSS-pixel width is chosen so the hierarchy stays visually distinct even at the lowest supported devicePixelRatio (1); `lineWeightToDevicePixels` floors at 1 device pixel only to protect against a devicePixelRatio below 1. `snapStrokeCenter` implements the standard canvas crisp-line technique (odd-device-pixel-width strokes snap to a half-pixel boundary, even widths to a whole-pixel boundary) so a renderer backend can avoid the blur a non-pixel-aligned stroke produces.

Kept renderer-independent on purpose (no Canvas 2D/PixiJS import) - any `PlanRenderer` backend (ARQ-119) calls these while preparing to draw a stroke.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 61 (renderer decision) and the PDF-export line-weight note in section 59 (explicitly deferred, not this issue's scope).
- [x] Tests: 22 new tests total (12 `line-weight.test.ts`), covering the tier hierarchy at multiple device pixel ratios, the sub-1-devicePixelRatio floor, and `snapStrokeCenter`'s half-pixel/whole-pixel behaviour. Full workspace suite: 623 tests passing. `plan-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: no Canvas 2D/PixiJS import; pure functions any backend can call.
- [x] Performance: not applicable - a pure math utility, no rendering pipeline yet to benchmark (deferred to the backend issues that will actually draw with it).

records.title: renderer: implement plan scene abstraction
records.body:
Implemented in commit fd094af on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

The renderer-neutral scene description blueprint section 60 requires: "plan primitives; annotation primitives; ...visibility state; selection state; style tokens. Renderers consume these structures." This is the concrete abstraction ADR-0008 (ARQ-118) names as its own safeguard for changing the renderer backend later.

- `plan-scene.ts`: `PlanLinePrimitive`/`PlanPolygonPrimitive`/`PlanTextPrimitive` (shape + elementId + `StyleToken`, nothing renderer-specific - no colour/stroke width, which is a backend's job reading the design tokens, sections 17/18). `StyleToken` mirrors section 18's "State language" (hover, active-tool, the two selection tiers, locked, warning, error, imported, proposed). Deliberately generic over the element id type (`TId`), not importing `WallId`/`RoomId` from `@arq/bim-core` - the same domain-agnostic layering every editor-shell tool already establishes.
- `resolveStyleToken`/`buildPlanScene` turn a project's visibility/selection/lock state into styled primitives: a hidden element is omitted from the scene entirely (not drawn with a "hidden" style) - section 18's "eye-off icon and reduced-opacity row" describes the model-tree row, not the canvas.
- `plan-renderer.ts`: the `PlanRenderer<TId>` interface - `render(scene, viewport)` - the one seam every backend implements (Canvas 2D per ADR-0008, PixiJS as the documented upgrade path). No backend is implemented here; that starts at ARQ-120 (stable line weights) onward.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in both modules' doc comments.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 60 ("Rendering architecture") and section 18 ("State language").
- [x] Tests: 10 new tests in `plan-scene.test.ts` covering `StyleToken` precedence (hidden overrides everything; selected-primary overrides locked) and `buildPlanScene`'s omission/ordering/marking behaviour. Full workspace suite: 611 tests passing. `plan-renderer` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies (only the existing `@arq/geometry-2d` workspace dependency).
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: no `@arq/bim-core` import; primitives carry only shape/id/style, no paint decisions.

records.title: renderer: select 2D renderer through ADR
records.body:
Implemented in commit 3f3c9f7 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

Filled in ADR-0008 (previously "Status: Spike required" with only placeholder boilerplate) with a real decision grounded in the ARQ-115/116/117 benchmark evidence.

**Decision**: Canvas 2D as the v1 (first production) 2D renderer, behind a renderer abstraction (blueprint section 61's own recommendation). This directly follows section 61's own stated selection procedure ("spike Canvas 2D; PixiJS WebGL; CanvasKit if the first two fail") - Canvas 2D did not fail the protected benchmark (59.3-60.0 fps average across three runs against a 60 fps target), so there is no basis yet to reach for PixiJS or CanvasKit's added integration complexity. CanvasKit is not adopted at this stage: it measured worse than Canvas 2D (39.7-43.0 fps) even setting aside the no-real-GPU caveat, and needs meaningfully more integration work for no demonstrated benefit at this scene size.

**Explicitly stated, and important**: this ADR does not read the PixiJS/CanvasKit numbers as those technologies being inferior in general - this container has no real GPU, so PixiJS's WebGL path could only be measured through full software GPU-pipeline emulation (16.4-17.3 fps), which both spike research docs already flag as unrepresentative. The ADR states plainly what the evidence can and cannot support, and marks itself **"Proposed"** (not "Accepted") pending a real-device validation run on section 121's supported device matrix.

Also updates `docs/product/DECISION-REGISTER.csv`'s D-005 from "WebGL first, WebGPU optional" to reflect this decision and its evidence trail, and adds a short pointer from `packages/plan-renderer`'s README to this ADR and the three research docs (without fabricating an implementation - the renderer-abstraction seam this decision depends on is ARQ-119's job).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the ADR itself.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 61 ("2D renderer decision") and section 121 (supported device matrix).
- [x] Evidence: the ADR cites and summarizes all three spikes' real, reproducible measured results.
- [x] New dependencies and licence effects recorded (already done in ARQ-116/117; this ADR references them, no new dependency introduced here).
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: the decision is explicitly framed around a renderer abstraction (blueprint section 60), keeping project semantics independent of whichever backend is chosen.
- [x] Performance measured on the protected benchmark: the decision table directly compares all three spikes' measured fps against `panZoomFpsTarget`.

records.title: renderer: evaluate CanvasKit fallback
records.body:
Implemented in commit e4e2669 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

Blueprint section 61 recommends evaluating CanvasKit "if the first two [spikes] fail protected tests" (ARQ-115 Canvas 2D, ARQ-116 PixiJS WebGL). Canvas 2D actually met the target in this environment, so that literal condition isn't triggered - completed anyway since this issue's acceptance criteria require it regardless, and since PixiJS's failure was shown to be a no-real-GPU artifact, leaving CanvasKit's comparison genuinely useful context for ARQ-118.

- `canvaskit-wasm` 0.41.1 added as a dev dependency (BSD-3-Clause, recorded in `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json`).
- Reuses ARQ-115/116's scene generator unchanged. The renderer (`packages/plan-renderer/benchmarks/canvaskit/canvaskit-benchmark.html`) uses `CanvasKit.MakeSWCanvasSurface` - Skia's own CPU software rasteriser - rather than a WebGL-backed surface: this container has no real GPU, so a WebGL-backed CanvasKit surface would only remeasure that same limitation. The software surface asks the fair, GPU-agnostic question this environment can actually answer: how Skia's own rasteriser (via WASM) compares to the browser's native Canvas 2D rasteriser.
- `run-canvaskit-benchmark.mjs`: since CanvasKit needs its `.wasm` binary and real font bytes served over http(s), this runs a small static file server for the benchmark's duration, serving the shared scene generator, CanvasKit's prebuilt `bin/` straight from `node_modules` (not vendored), and this container's installed DejaVu Sans font (Bitstream Vera/Arev licence, read at run-time, not vendored).

**Measured results** (three runs, this sandboxed container): CanvasKit/Skia-via-WASM averages 40-43 fps - fails the 60 fps target, but well ahead of ARQ-116's software-WebGL PixiJS result (~16-17 fps) from the same container. The research doc documents the three-way comparison and is explicit about what this environment can and cannot honestly conclude: the relative ordering (native Canvas 2D > WASM-via-Skia > full software-GPU-emulation) is a real signal about binding/sandbox overhead in this environment, but says nothing certain about real-hardware behaviour (section 121's supported device matrix) - that needs an actual GPU.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the research doc and code comments.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 61 ("2D renderer decision").
- [x] Evidence: real, reproducible measured benchmark output (three runs) in `docs/research/RENDERER-BENCHMARK-CANVASKIT.md` and `benchmarks/results/`.
- [x] New dependency recorded: `canvaskit-wasm`, BSD-3-Clause, dev-only, in `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json`.
- [x] Project semantics remain renderer-independent: the benchmark scene/generator has no dependency on `@arq/bim-core` or any project-model type.
- [x] Performance measured on the protected benchmark: object counts match `benchmarks/PERFORMANCE-BUDGETS.json`'s `benchmarkModel` exactly, compared against its `panZoomFpsTarget`.

records.title: renderer: benchmark PixiJS WebGL
records.body:
Implemented in commit 46deb0a on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

Blueprint section 61's 2D renderer decision recommends spiking Canvas 2D (ARQ-115), PixiJS WebGL, and CanvasKit (ARQ-117) before selecting a renderer via ADR (ARQ-118). This is the PixiJS WebGL half.

- `pixi.js` 8.19.0 added as a dev dependency (MIT, already listed as a planned "spike" entry in `open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`/`.json` - now annotated with this benchmark's finding).
- Reuses ARQ-115's scene generator unchanged. The PixiJS renderer (`packages/plan-renderer/benchmarks/pixijs-webgl/pixijs-webgl-benchmark.html`) builds the scene's Graphics/Text objects **once** as retained display objects and only moves the container each frame before calling `render()` - the natural way a retained-mode 2D GPU renderer is used, deliberately different from Canvas 2D's per-frame full redraw (section 61 itself frames this as each technology's own shape).
- `run-pixijs-webgl-benchmark.mjs`: launches headless Chromium with software-WebGL flags (SwiftShader - this container has no real GPU) and injects PixiJS's prebuilt UMD bundle directly from `node_modules` via Playwright's `addScriptTag` rather than vendoring it into the repo.

**Methodology correction applied to both spikes**: the first 30 frames are now rendered but excluded from timing (WebGL context/shader-compile warm-up is a one-time cost, not part of steady-state pan/zoom frame rate - an early PixiJS run without this exclusion measured a 9.7-second first frame). Both benchmarks were re-run/re-recorded for a fair, consistent comparison; the Canvas 2D research doc has a revision note explaining the change.

**Measured results** (three runs, this sandboxed container, post warm-up-fix): Canvas 2D averages ~60 fps (meets target); PixiJS/WebGL averages 16-17 fps (fails it by a wide margin). **Critical caveat, explicit in the research doc**: this gap must NOT be read as "Canvas 2D beats PixiJS" - this container has no GPU, so it cannot exercise WebGL's actual advantage (confirmed via `gl.getParameter(gl.RENDERER)` showing software rasterisation). ARQ-118's ADR needs a real-GPU device run (section 121's supported device matrix) before weighing these numbers. Full methodology, results table, and this caveat are in `docs/research/RENDERER-BENCHMARK-PIXIJS-WEBGL.md`.

**Acceptance criteria**

records.title: editor: implement zoom to room gap
records.body:
Implemented in commit d55675e on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav` (rebased onto an unrelated concurrent push, #222, that landed on this branch mid-session).

**What was built**

- `findNearestRoomBoundaryGap` (geometry-2d's `room-boundary-gap.ts`): blueprint section 49's Room error UX ("nearest gap; distance of gap; suggested wall endpoint"). A "gap" is a dangling wall endpoint (degree 1 after merging vertices within tolerance, the same way `room-boundary-graph.ts` does) and the nearest point - another dangling endpoint, or the nearest point on any wall it isn't already part of - that closing it would connect to. Candidates already directly connected to the dangling vertex are excluded, so the suggestion is never "reconnect to something you're already connected to." Returns `null` when there is no dangling endpoint at all, or for an invalid tolerance (never a hidden fallback epsilon, per ARQ-081).
- `zoomToRoomGap` (editor-shell's `zoom-to-room-gap.ts`): the "'Zoom to gap' action" itself - a thin wrapper around `viewport-controller.ts`'s existing `fitToBounds` (ARQ-033), since a gap's two points already are a bounding box. Uses a larger default margin (120px vs. `fitToBounds`'s own 40px) because a gap's bounding box is frequently near-zero-size and needs generous padding to keep nearby walls in view for context.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in both modules' doc comments.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 49's "Room error UX" list.
- [x] Tests: 13 new tests (8 `room-boundary-gap.test.ts`, 5 `zoom-to-room-gap.test.ts`), including a square missing one wall, two disconnected segments, a stub whose nearest connection is the middle of another wall (not either of its endpoints), a fully-closed loop returning null, invalid tolerance, a near-zero-size gap, and large world coordinates. Full workspace suite: 593 tests passing. Both packages typecheck clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
