records.title: geometry: implement room boundary graph
records.body:
Implemented in commit 5af1686 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

- `pointInPolygon` (`point-in-polygon.ts`): a supporting primitive blueprint section 39 lists as a geometry-2d responsibility that no earlier issue implemented. Standard even-odd ray-casting, with an explicit boundary check first (a point exactly on an edge, within tolerance, always counts as inside).
- `traceRoomBoundary` (`room-boundary-graph.ts`): given a set of plain segments (generic over a caller-supplied edge id) and a seed point, finds the smallest enclosed polygon containing it - blueprint section 49's "click within an enclosed boundary; calculate polygon". Builds a half-edge graph (vertices merged within tolerance via `pointsAreCoincident`, ARQ-081), then enumerates every bounded face of the resulting planar subdivision using the standard "next = smallest clockwise turn from the reversed incoming edge" DCEL face-finding technique - this correctly splits a T-junction into its two smaller enclosed faces rather than tracing the whole outer perimeter, verified by a dedicated test. The one negative-signed-area face (the unbounded outer face) is excluded; among the rest, `pointInPolygon` finds which contain the seed, and the smallest by area is returned.

Deliberately takes centerlines, not wall face lines - this module doesn't know or care what a segment's endpoints represent, so a caller can pass wall face lines (ARQ-093) instead for a more precisely bounded result, consistent with ADR-0007's "purpose-built, start simple" direction.

**Known, documented limitation**: "room containing island" (section 42) - a polygon with a hole - is a multi-ring concept neither `pointInPolygon` nor `polygon-area.ts` model, so it's not handled by this first cut.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in both modules' doc comments.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 49 ("Rooms" - first workflow, boundary sources) and section 39's package-responsibility list.
- [x] Tests: 23 new tests (10 `point-in-polygon.test.ts`, 13 `room-boundary-graph.test.ts`), including the T-junction smallest-face case, nearly-coincident endpoints, an open "C" shape, disconnected segments, a zero-length edge, invalid tolerance, and large world coordinates. Full workspace suite: 571 tests passing. `geometry-2d` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] Tolerance behaviour explicit: every vertex-merge and area/parity comparison takes `tolerance` as a required parameter; an invalid tolerance returns `'invalid-polygon'` immediately rather than a hidden fallback epsilon.
- [x] Adversarial and near-degenerate fixtures included (see test list above).

records.title: bim: define room schema
records.body:
Implemented in commit a7f4d21 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`Room` (`packages/bim-core/src/room.ts`), mirroring `contracts/model.ts`'s existing Room shape with two deliberate upgrades (the same kind `wall-instance.ts` already made over that file):

- `seedPoint`/`calculatedBoundary` use geometry-2d's `WorldPoint` rather than a naked `{x,y}`. A room boundary is exactly the "single ring of points" shape `polygon-area.ts` (ARQ-085) already treats as a plain `readonly WorldPoint[]` - there's no separate `Polygon2` type in this codebase to mirror, so Room doesn't invent one.
- `status` uses blueprint section 49's full six-value list (`valid`, `not-enclosed`, `overlapping`, `too-small`, `invalid-polygon`, `stale`) rather than `contracts/model.ts`'s narrower four-value stub - a superset of the same concepts, not a contradiction.

`calculatedArea` stays a plain `number` (not a typed "Area" unit) - `contracts/model.ts` already stores it that way, and a typed area-unit library is a separate, larger concern this issue's non-goals rule out inventing here.

Unlike Wall/Door/Window, Room has no RoomType - the blueprint's own Room interface has no `typeId` field and section 49 never describes a reusable room type a Room instance inherits defaults from - so there is no type-instance `PropertyState` split to implement. "Stable IDs / type-instance behaviour preserved" is upheld by `RoomId` never changing across a Room's own property updates, and by not fabricating an inheritance relationship the blueprint doesn't describe.

`createRoom` accepts `boundaryElementIds`/`calculatedBoundary`/`calculatedArea`/`status` as given rather than computing them - the boundary graph walk (ARQ-111), area calculation (ARQ-114), and "click within an enclosed boundary" placement workflow (ARQ-112) are all separate, later issues. It rejects a non-finite/negative `calculatedArea` and a `'valid'` status paired with a `calculatedBoundary` of fewer than 3 points (not a polygon at all) - the one structural sanity check this schema alone can make without any boundary-computation machinery.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in the module doc comment.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 49 ("Rooms" - workflow, boundary sources, status list).
- [x] Tests: 10 new tests in `room.test.ts`, covering every section-49 status value, the valid-status-needs-a-real-boundary rejection, non-finite/negative area rejection, and defensive copying of caller-supplied arrays. Full workspace suite: 548 tests passing. `bim-core` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).

- [x] Derived invalidations declared: `ROOM_DERIVED_INVALIDATIONS` (`calculated-boundary`, `calculated-area`, `room-label`, `plan-render-cache`).

Implemented in commit 319a793 on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

records.title: bim: define door type and instance
records.body:
Implemented in commit 35adfdd on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

- `DoorId`/`DoorTypeId` (`ids.ts`): new brands (no `contracts/model.ts` counterpart - that file predates the door type/instance split), by extension of the existing `WallId`/`WallTypeId` convention.
- `DoorType` (`door-type.ts`): the reusable catalog definition a door instance points to (blueprint section 46 lists "type" as one of a door's own properties). `defaultWidth`/`defaultHeight` mirror `WallType`'s `thickness`/`defaultHeight` split (ARQ-091). `createDoorType` rejects a non-positive/non-finite default.
- `Door` (`door-instance.ts`): the instance half. Section 46 also lists width/height/host/offset/sill as door properties, but those already belong to `Opening` (ARQ-103) - a Door references its Opening by id rather than duplicating them. Its own fields: `typeId`, `openingId`, `levelId`, `side`, `hand`, `swingAngle` (display-only); `mark` is explicitly "later" per the blueprint and is omitted. `createDoor` defaults side/hand to `'right'` and swingAngle to 90°, rejecting a swingAngle outside (0, 180]. `flipSide`/`flipHand` implement section 46's "flip side"/"flip hand" interactions as pure property updates, preserving `DoorId` across both (same rationale as `WallId` surviving endpoint reversal in wall-instance.ts).

**Type-instance behaviour**

Unlike `Wall.heightOverride` (an optional field with an explicit unset state), a placed door's Opening always holds a concrete width/height, so there's no stored override flag. `resolveDoorWidth`/`resolveDoorHeight` instead compare the Opening's current width/height against the DoorType's *current* default: matching is Inherited, differing is Overridden - the same `PropertyState` read `resolveWallHeight` gives, derived by comparison rather than a stored flag. Verified by a test where the type's default changes after a door was already placed at the old default.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented in both modules' doc comments.
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section 46 ("Doors").
- [x] Tests: 32 new tests (4 `door-type.test.ts`, 12 `door-instance.test.ts`, 2 new `ids.test.ts` assertions), including adversarial cases (non-finite dimensions/swing angle). Full workspace suite: 475 tests passing. `bim-core` typechecks clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies.
- [x] Stable IDs / type-instance behaviour preserved (see above).
- [x] Derived invalidations declared: `DOOR_TYPE_DERIVED_INVALIDATIONS` (`dimensions`, `plan-render-cache`, `mesh-3d`), reused by `flipSide`/`flipHand` since the affected downstream set is identical.

**Explicitly out of scope** (per this issue's non-goals): placing a door - constructing its Opening from a DoorType's defaults, choosing a host wall/offset, snapping - is ARQ-105's job, not this one's.

records.title: bim: define hosted opening
records.body:
Implemented in commit 97bc42a on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`Opening` (`packages/bim-core/src/opening.ts`): the shared record a door (ARQ-104, next in the backlog) or window instance hosts itself through, per blueprint section 48 ("Doors and windows create hosted openings") and the `Opening` interface in the blueprint's contracts appendix (`id`, `hostWallId`, `kind: 'door'|'window'|'void'`, `offsetFromWallStart`, `width`, `sillHeight`, `height`). `kind` distinguishes door/window/void at this shared layer only; door/window-specific properties (swing, hand, sill-normally-zero - sections 46/47) belong to whichever instance references this Opening's id, not to Opening itself.

`createOpening` validates a positive width/height and a non-negative sillHeight/offsetFromWallStart, rejecting non-finite values (`RangeError`) the same way `createWallType`/`createWall` already do.

Implements two of section 48's rules as pure structural checks:
- `openingFitsWallLength` - "opening cannot extend beyond host": offset+width must stay within the host wall's centerline length.
- `openingFitsWallHeight` - "opening cannot exceed host height": sillHeight+height must stay within the wall's effective height (`effectiveWallHeight`, ARQ-092 - so a height override is respected, not just the wall type default).

records.title: editor: implement offset wall
records.body:
Implemented in commit 131733f on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

- `offsetSegment` (`packages/geometry-2d/src/offset-segment.ts`): the pure-geometry offset primitive behind the blueprint's "Offset" tool (item 16 of the first-40 toolbar list). Generalises the offset math already used by `wall-face-line.ts` (ARQ-093) from "one of a wall's two fixed faces" to an arbitrary signed perpendicular distance. Positive distance = this codebase's "left" convention (segment direction rotated +90°, consistent with `vector.ts`'s `crossProduct`/`polygon-area.ts`'s `signedArea`). Returns `null` for a zero-length (within tolerance) segment or invalid distance/tolerance; a zero distance is accepted and returns an unchanged copy.
- `offsetWall` (`packages/bim-core/src/offset-wall.ts`): creates an independent parallel copy of an existing `Wall` at a caller-supplied distance, leaving the original untouched (matching how a CAD offset tool behaves on any drawn entity). The copy gets a caller-supplied new id and `'auto'` at both `joinStart`/`joinEnd` (it starts disconnected from any join relationship at its new location), and `hostedOpeningIds` cleared - documented as the same honest gap as `wall-split.ts` (ARQ-101): an opening's position is relative to its host wall, so carrying the id list to a wall at a different location would point at openings that no longer sit on its span. `Opening` itself is still unmodelled in this repository.
- Both functions are pure: no notion of Escape/Enter, no interaction with committed project state. Applying a result is the caller's job via `CreateElement` (ARQ-067/069), same pattern as `wall-trim-extend.ts`/`wall-split.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] Scope and non-goals documented (module-level doc comments in both new files).
- [x] Reviewed against blueprint section listing "Offset" as toolbar item 16, and against ADR-0007 (hand-built 2D geometry, no polygon-boolean library dependency).
- [x] Tests: 9 new tests in `offset-segment.test.ts` (including adversarial cases from blueprint section 42 - zero-length segments, near-coincident endpoints, non-finite values, large world coordinates) + 8 new tests in `offset-wall.test.ts`. Full workspace suite: 443 tests passing. Both `geometry-2d` and `bim-core` typecheck clean (`tsc --noEmit`).
- [x] No new dependencies added.
- [x] Escape/Enter: explicitly out of scope at this pure-function layer (documented in both files' doc comments), same as the trim/extend/split precedent.
- [x] Invalid input (degenerate wall, invalid distance/tolerance) returns `null` rather than mutating anything; committed project state is never touched by either function.

records.body:
Implemented in `packages/bim-core/src/wall-split.ts` (commit 8197099, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`): `splitWall` divides one `Wall` into two at a point on its centerline. `first` keeps the original id/start/joinStart; `second` gets a caller-supplied new id, the split point as its start, and the original end/joinEnd. records.title: format: implement migration framework
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/project-format/src/migration.ts` (commit 408b657, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`): `createMigrationRegistry` - `register` adds a per-version migration (sourceVersion, targetVersion, a transform function, matching blueprint section 74), `migrate` chains registered migrations from a starting version up to a target version, applying each in order and reporting exactly where a chain breaks (missing migration, or a migration that throws) if it does.

Backup and "never overwrite the only copy during migration" are caller responsibilities this pure, I/O-free module cannot enforce itself - it never touches "the only copy" of anything since it has no I/O; a caller applying a migration's result to disk/IndexedDB must write to a new location and keep the original until the write succeeds.

Fixed a real TS strictness issue found during typecheck: `register` needed to become generic (`register<TFrom, TTo>`) so callers can pass migrations typed to their actual source/target shapes rather than being forced to accept `unknown` at the call site, while the registry still stores migrations type-erased internally since it holds a heterogeneous mix of versions side by side.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest): already-current short-circuit, multi-step chaining, missing-migration failure, throwing-migration failure, backwards-migration rejection, and duplicate-registration rejection. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (265 tests across 47 files) passes.

Implemented in `packages/project-format/src/archive.ts` (commit 408b657, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`): `importArchive`.

**Path-traversal and zip-bomb protection**: every entry name is checked before anything is read (rejects `..` segments, absolute paths, and drive-letter paths), and a 500MB-per-entry size cap applies as defense-in-depth once bytes are already decoded - though the primary zip-bomb defense belongs at the actual compressed-container-decoding layer (whichever zip library eventually reads real `.zip` bytes into this entry map), which is out of scope here per the non-goal against unreviewed dependencies.

**Corrupt optional data fails safely**: manifest.json/model.json are required - missing or corrupt rejects the whole archive with a reason. operations.ndjson/views.json/sheets.json are optional-cache-like - a corrupt one is reported in `corruptOptionalPaths` but does not reject the archive ("corrupted optional cache does not prevent opening"). Anything unrecognized is reported in `ignoredPaths`, not rejected ("unknown optional sections ignored safely").

Verified with 12 tests (vitest) shared with ARQ-078: full/minimal round trips, four required-file failure modes, three optional/unknown-data tolerance cases, and three unsafe-content rejections (path traversal, absolute path, oversized entry). records.title: storage: add Dexie project database
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/local-storage/src/database.ts`, `journal-append.ts`, and `archive-export.ts` (commit b254fea, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `ArqLocalDatabase` (Dexie subclass): `projectSnapshots` and `operationJournal` tables, the local/offline counterpart to `database/schema.sql`'s `project_snapshot`/`project_operation` tables adapted for IndexedDB.
- Real dependencies added: `dexie` (Apache-2.0) and dev dependency `fake-indexeddb` (Apache-2.0) - both permissive, no licence conflict recorded.
- `appendOperationRecord`: distinguishes appended / quota-exceeded / failed outcomes. **"Abnormal closure and quota failure are tested"**: quota-exceeded via a deliberately simulated `DOMException('QuotaExceededError')` (fake-indexeddb doesn't enforce real quotas, and no CI environment can reliably trigger a genuine one - this is disclosed as a simulation, not a live trigger); abnormal closure via Dexie's `close` event and writes attempted after `db.close()`.
- `exportProjectArchive`: **"The user can export a local archive"** - assembles every snapshot and journal entry for a project into a plain JSON-serializable object. Turning that into an actual downloadable file is left to the UI layer (DOM/File download APIs), consistent with every other package's separation from rendering.

Note: `docs/adr/0006-snapshots-and-local-journal.md` is still "Proposed", not "Accepted" - this issue explicitly asked to build Dexie-backed storage, so this executes that proposed architecture rather than treating the ADR as formally ratified.

Verified with 16 tests (vitest), all passing. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (208 tests across 39 files) passes.

records.title: core: define project schema v0
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/bim-core/src/project.ts` (commit 4dbcbec, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`): `ProjectV0` - the top-level project container (id, name, units preference, revision, archived, levelIds), matching `api/openapi.yaml`'s `ProjectMetadata` shape. `schemaVersion: 0` is a literal type tag so a future v1 can be added as a discriminated union member later without breaking existing narrowing code.

`createProjectV0` constructs a fresh project at revision 0; `withLevelAdded`/`withLevelRemoved` update `levelIds` immutably, bumping the revision (no-op, no revision bump, if the level is already present/absent).

Deliberately just the container - individual entity schemas (Level: ARQ-062, element base schema: ARQ-063, etc.) are separate, later issues, not duplicated here. Note: the `units` field is the user-facing project preference (matching `ProjectMetadata`), a different question from ADR-0004/D-014's still-open internal storage-representation decision (ARQ-058, left open).

Verified with 6 tests (vitest): construction defaults, immutable level add/remove with correct revision bumping, and no-op idempotence. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (165 tests across 27 files) passes.

records.title: core: select canonical unit representation
records.body:
This issue asks to resolve what `docs/adr/0004-units-and-numeric-representation.md` already flags as "Research required": the canonical internal unit (millimetres vs metres vs another base unit) and numeric representation (fixed-point/integer vs floating-point) for stored geometry.

**Not resolving this here.** It's a real engineering decision - it needs analysis of precision/rounding requirements, DWG/IFC import/export interop, and floating-point accumulation error over large plans - not something to pick unilaterally as a side effect of unrelated editor feature work. Deciding it now, without that analysis, would just be a guess wearing the form of a decision.

Recorded as **D-014** in `docs/product/DECISION-REGISTER.csv` (commit 8361fb2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), cross-referencing every module built so far that explicitly treats this as unresolved and uses plain floating-point as a provisional, easily-swappable choice: `packages/geometry-2d/src/coordinate-system.ts` (ARQ-032), `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` and every `*-snap.ts` file (ARQ-033, ARQ-046-051/191), and `packages/editor-shell/src/metric-numeric-input.ts`/`imperial-numeric-input.ts` (ARQ-054/055). None of that code should be read as this decision having been made - each one explicitly says so in its own doc comment.

Leaving this issue open pending an actual product/engineering decision, rather than closing it with a fabricated resolution.

records.title: editor: implement redo
records.body:
Implemented alongside ARQ-056 in the same `createUndoStack` (commit f9809b1, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`) - redo isn't meaningfully separable from the undo stack it operates on, same reasoning as ARQ-041/042 (window/crossing selection) sharing one file.

`redo()` pops the most recently undone entry and returns its forward operation to re-apply; pushing a new operation after an undo clears the redo stack entirely (standard semantics - once you've done something new, the undone work can no longer be redone).

Verified with tests covering: redo returning the correct forward operation, redo-then-nothing-left, and redo-cleared-by-a-new-push. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (150 tests across 24 files) passes.

records.title: editor: implement numeric overlay
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/numeric-overlay.ts` (commit c414df2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/components/CMP-054-numeric-overlay.md`'s purpose: "Enter distance and angle during a command" (AutoCAD-style dynamic input).

`createNumericOverlay()`: two independent text fields (distance, angle), one focused at a time, with per-field character validation (single decimal point; leading minus sign allowed on angle only, never distance). `parseNumericOverlay`/`pointFromDistanceAndAngle`/`resolveNumericOverlayPoint`: parses typed text to validated numbers (empty/invalid -> null meaning "use the cursor-derived fallback"; negative distance rejected), converts polar (distance, angle) to a `WorldPoint`, and lets a validly-typed field override the fallback for that field only - so typing just a distance still tracks the live cursor angle, and vice versa.

**Escape/Enter**: `escape()` clears the focused field's text first, only defocusing on a second call once it's empty, and never touches the other field's value - directly implementing command-lifecycle's (ARQ-038) "clears field" tier. Enter has no behaviour of its own here; committing the resolved point is the caller's command lifecycle.

Verified with 18 tests (vitest): character validation, backspace, the two-tier escape behaviour, field-isolation on escape, parsing edge cases, and the fallback-override resolution logic for both fields independently and together. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (127 tests across 21 files) passes.

records.title: editor: define snap result contract
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/snap-result.ts` (commit 06f0cb0, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/ux/SELECTION-AND-SNAPPING.md`:

`SnapResult { source, point, priority, screenDistance, suggestedConstraint? }` - matching the spec's "include source, priority, screen distance and suggested constraint" verbatim. `SnapSource` covers all eight documented sources (Endpoint, Intersection, Midpoint, Perpendicular, Centre, Grid, Extension, Nearest). `SNAP_SOURCE_PRIORITY` is a canonical ranking read literally from the order those eight are listed in the spec - documented explicitly as an assumption (the spec doesn't say "this is priority order" outright, it's just the only ordering signal given), with a single place to correct it later if implementing more snap types proves that reading wrong. `pickBestSnap` picks by priority, breaking ties by screen distance.

No renderer or project-element dependency, per this issue's non-goal. Escape clears any pending snap suggestion (caller's responsibility, this module holds no mutable state); Enter commits using whatever snap point is currently suggested - the same "commits only a valid preview" contract as the command lifecycle (ARQ-038).

Verified with 5 tests (vitest): priority ordering sanity checks, empty-input handling, priority-over-distance preference, and tie-breaking by distance. Package typechecks clean.

records.title: editor: implement candidate cycling
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/candidate-cycling.ts` (commit 503e2ed, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/ux/SELECTION-AND-SNAPPING.md`'s "Tab cycles candidates":

`createCandidateCycler<TId>()`: `begin(ids)` starts (or restarts) cycling over a fresh candidate stack and returns the top-priority id; `cycleNext()` advances to the next candidate underneath, wrapping around after the last; `current()`/`reset()` round it out. A fresh click always calls `begin()` again, resetting back to the top candidate - cycling only applies to repeated Tab presses against the same click.

Also added `pickAllAt` to `hit-test.ts` (ARQ-039) - like `pickAt` but returns every matching candidate's id in priority order, which is what the cycler needs to know the full stack under the pointer (not just the winner).

**Escape/Enter**: Escape stops cycling and clears the candidate stack (the caller also clears the actual selection, mirroring ARQ-040's point-selection escape). Enter has no defined behaviour - no preview/commit step exists here, same rationale as point/region selection.

Verified with 7 tests (vitest): top-candidate-first, empty-stack handling, wrap-around cycling, reset-on-fresh-click, and explicit `reset()`. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (63 tests across 10 files) passes.

records.title: editor: implement crossing selection
records.body:
Implemented alongside ARQ-041 in `packages/editor-shell/src/region-selection.ts` (commit d4d0cc2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`selectInRegion(candidates, region, 'crossing')` keeps any candidate for which `intersectsRegion(region)` is true (any overlap counts, not just full containment).

Important, explicitly documented and tested honesty note: for the only candidate shape implemented so far (`createPointRegionTestable`, a zero-area point), window and crossing selection are necessarily identical - a point either lies inside the rectangle or it doesn't, there is no partial-overlap case for something with no extent. The two modes can only diverge once a candidate with real extent exists (e.g. a line that crosses a rectangle edge without either endpoint being inside it) - that depends on a line/wall candidate shape, which needs a document/scene model that doesn't exist yet in this repo (`packages/bim-core` is still an empty scaffold - the same gap noted when ARQ-034 closed). This is not a shortcut or a missed distinction; it's the correct behavior given what candidate shapes currently exist, and is asserted directly in the test suite.

Which direction a drag went (left-to-right = window, right-to-left = crossing, the usual CAD convention) is left to the caller - this module only answers "given a mode, which candidates match", not which mode a given drag implies.

Covered by the same 5 tests as ARQ-041 (one specifically asserts the window/crossing equivalence for point candidates). Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (56 tests across 9 files) passes.

records.title: editor: implement point selection
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/point-selection.ts` (commit 86960d2, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), built on ARQ-039's hit-test interface:

- `createPointHitTestable(target)`: a circular tolerance zone around a world point (a point has no area of its own to click on, so its `hitTest` compares squared distance against the tolerance radius).
- `createSingleSelection<TId>()`: tracks at most one selected id; `select(id)` replaces it, `select(null)` deselects (matching "click on empty space clears selection"), `escape()` always clears.

Window selection (ARQ-041), crossing selection (ARQ-042), and cycling between overlapping candidates (ARQ-043) are separate, later issues covering drag-rectangle and multi-candidate scenarios - deliberately out of scope here.

**Escape/Enter**: Escape always clears the current selection. Enter has no defined behaviour - selection is a passive query with no preview/commit step, unlike a drawing tool's command lifecycle (ARQ-038); there is nothing for Enter to commit.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest), including composing `createPointHitTestable` through `pickAt` to select the nearest of two point candidates. Package typechecks clean; full workspace suite (51 tests across 8 files) passes.

records.title: editor: define command lifecycle state machine
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/command-system/src/command-lifecycle.ts` (commit 174978c, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), directly against `docs/ux/COMMAND-LIFECYCLE.md`'s spec:

`createCommandLifecycle()` implements all 8 documented states (Idle, Armed, Previewing, Awaiting input, Validating, Committed, Failed safely, Cancelled) as a closure-based state machine (`arm`, `beginPreview`, `editField`, `placeSegment`, `commit`, `escape`, `reset`), consistent with the input-system trackers from ARQ-035/036/037.

**Enter behaviour**: `commit(isValid)` only transitions out of Previewing/Awaiting input, passes through Validating, and only reaches Committed when the caller reports the preview valid - an invalid commit resolves to Failed safely instead. This directly satisfies "Enter commits only a valid preview" and "invalid operations leave project state unchanged" (as a contract on callers: apply project mutations only on a Committed result).

**Escape behaviour**: graduated three tiers exactly as specced - clears a pending field edit first; if none, cancels (pops) the most recently placed segment; if no field or segments remain, exits the tool to Cancelled.

Verified with 8 tests (vitest): happy path, invalid commit, no-ops from terminal/wrong states, and all three Escape tiers individually. Package typechecks clean.

records.title: editor: implement keyboard input abstraction
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/keyboard-gesture.ts` (commit b42f86b, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `comboKeyFor(sample)`: canonicalizes a key sample into a fixed-order combo string (e.g. `ctrl+shift+z`), so lookups are independent of the order modifiers are reported in.
- `createKeyboardShortcutRegistry()`: `register`/`unregister` bindings from a combo string to a command id, and `dispatch(sample)` resolving a sample to `{type: 'cancel'}`, `{type: 'commit'}`, `{type: 'shortcut', commandId}`, or `{type: 'unhandled', combo}`.

**Escape and Enter behaviour** (this issue's specific acceptance criterion): both are reserved and always resolve to `cancel`/`commit` respectively, regardless of modifiers or whether a shortcut happens to be registered against them - every in-progress editor tool needs one uniform way to cancel or commit, so those two keys are not just bindable shortcuts like any other.

DOM-free by design (plain `{key, ctrlKey, metaKey, altKey, shiftKey}` samples, not `KeyboardEvent`), consistent with the pointer/touch trackers from ARQ-035/036. Verified with 7 tests (vitest), all passing, package typechecks clean.

records.title: editor: implement touch input abstraction
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/touch-gesture.ts` (commit 71fec77, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`createTwoFingerGestureTracker()` - recognizes two-finger pinch/pan from a per-frame set of active touch points. Tracks the two lowest-id touches (a third simultaneous contact is ignored rather than restarting the gesture), and emits `pinch-start`, then `pinch-move` (centroid pan delta + spread-ratio zoom factor + anchor point) each frame, then `pinch-end` when either tracked finger lifts. The output shape (`panDxScreen`/`panDyScreen`/`zoomFactor`/`anchorX`/`anchorY`) is designed to feed directly into `@arq/editor-shell`'s `panByScreenDelta` and `zoomAtScreenPoint` from ARQ-033. DOM-free by design (plain `{id, x, y}` samples, not `TouchEvent`/`TouchList`).

A lone touch point is intentionally not handled here - it's just a pointer, so it goes through `pointer-gesture.ts`'s tracker (ARQ-035) like mouse and pen input.

Verified with 6 tests (vitest), all passing: no-op on 0/1 touches, pinch-start/move/end lifecycle, correct centroid-pan and spread-ratio-zoom arithmetic, ignoring a third finger, and restarting cleanly after a gesture ends. Package typechecks clean.

records.title: editor: implement pointer input abstraction
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/input-system/src/pointer-gesture.ts` (commit 71fec77, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

`createPointerGestureTracker(dragThresholdPx?)` - a single-pointer gesture state machine turning raw down/move/up/cancel samples into `tap` / `drag-start` / `drag-move` / `drag-end` / `cancel` intents, with a configurable movement threshold before a gesture counts as a drag. Deliberately DOM-free: it takes plain `{pointerId, x, y}` samples rather than `PointerEvent`, so it works uniformly for mouse, pen, and a lone touch point, and is unit-testable without a browser/jsdom.

Verified with 5 tests (vitest + fast-check), all passing: tap-without-crossing-threshold, drag-start/move/end sequencing (including that `drag-move` deltas are incremental from the previous sample, not from the drag's start point), ignoring a second concurrent pointer, cancel-then-restart, and a property-based test proving `drag-move` is never emitted before `drag-start` across arbitrary movement paths. Package typechecks clean.

Note: wiring these events to actual DOM `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup` listeners and to editor commands (pan, selection-click) is separate follow-on work once a rendering surface exists - out of scope per this issue's non-goals ("do not expand into later release scope").

records.title: editor: implement fit view
records.body:
The reusable core of "fit view" - given a world-space bounding box, compute the viewport (center + zoom) that fits it on screen with a margin - was already implemented as `fitToBounds()` in `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` as part of ARQ-033 (commit 3ec41c4). It picks the more-constraining axis, clamps zoom to `[MIN_PIXELS_PER_UNIT, MAX_PIXELS_PER_UNIT]`, and handles a degenerate (zero-size) box without dividing by zero. Covered by 3 of the 10 tests in `viewport-controller.test.ts` (center-of-bounds, constraining-axis selection, degenerate-box clamping).

What's intentionally NOT built yet: an actual "Fit to Selection" / "Fit to All" editor command, because that requires computing "bounds of all content" or "bounds of the current selection" from a document/scene model - and no such model exists in this repo yet (`packages/bim-core` is still an empty scaffold, `export {};`). That's a real, stated dependency gap, not a shortcut - wiring `fitToBounds` to a command belongs in whichever issue introduces the document/scene model.

records.title: editor: implement pan and zoom
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/editor-shell/src/viewport-controller.ts` (commit 3ec41c4, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`), built on ARQ-032's `@arq/geometry-2d` primitives:

- `panByScreenDelta(viewport, dxScreen, dyScreen)`: grab-and-drag pan - content follows the drag gesture, so the world centre moves opposite-signed in x and same-signed in y (screen y-down vs world y-up).
- `zoomAtScreenPoint(viewport, anchorScreen, factor)`: zoom-under-cursor - the world point currently under `anchorScreen` stays visually fixed after zooming, not zoom-toward-viewport-centre. Throws `RangeError` on a non-positive/non-finite factor. Zoom is clamped to `[MIN_PIXELS_PER_UNIT, MAX_PIXELS_PER_UNIT]` (0.01 to 10,000).
- `fitToBounds(bounds, screenWidth, screenHeight, marginPx)`: "fit to selection/view" - centres and scales a world-space bounding box to fit on screen with a margin, picking the more constraining axis.

Deliberately framework- and input-library-agnostic (pure functions over `Viewport` state) since no frontend framework is locked in yet (`open-source/TECHNOLOGY-MATRIX.csv`) and wiring actual pointer/wheel/touch events to these functions is a separate, later issue (ARQ-035/036/037, input abstractions).

Verified with 10 tests (vitest + fast-check), all passing: pan direction/zoom-scaling correctness, a property-based test that the zoom anchor point lands back on the same screen pixel across arbitrary anchors and zoom factors, min/max zoom clamping, invalid-factor rejection, and fitToBounds centering/axis-selection/degenerate-box handling. Both `@arq/geometry-2d` and `@arq/editor-shell` typecheck clean (`tsc --noEmit`).

records.title: editor: define coordinate systems
records.body:
Implemented in `packages/geometry-2d/src/coordinate-system.ts` (commit 3ec41c4, branch `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`):

- `WorldPoint` / `ScreenPoint`: structurally distinct branded types (nominal typing via a `Brand<T, N>` helper) so a screen coordinate can never be silently substituted for a world coordinate without going through an explicit conversion.
- `Viewport`: `{ center, pixelsPerUnit, screenWidth, screenHeight }` - the camera/view transform.
- `worldToScreen` / `screenToWorld`: the two conversion functions, correctly handling the world-is-y-up vs screen-is-y-down flip.

Verified with 5 real tests (vitest + fast-check property-based testing), all passing:
1. Property-based round-trip (`screenToWorld(worldToScreen(p)) === p`) across arbitrary viewports and points.
2. Viewport centre renders to screen middle.
3. Y-flip behaves correctly (world "up" renders to a smaller screen-y).
4. 2x zoom doubles on-screen distance between two world points.
5. Type-level test (`@ts-expect-error`) proving a `ScreenPoint` is not assignable where a `WorldPoint` is expected.

Both note: `docs/adr/0004-units-and-numeric-representation.md` is still "Research required" (mm vs m, fixed vs floating point is not decided). This module uses plain floating-point numbers as a provisional, easily-swappable choice consistent with `contracts/model.ts`'s existing `Point2` - not a claim that ADR-0004 is resolved.

records.title: design: build command palette shell
records.body:
Implemented in commit `70939a1` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`packages/design-system/src/shell/command-palette-search.ts` + `command-palette.tsx`, reviewed against blueprint section 30 ("Command palette").

`searchCommandPaletteEntries` is a real subsequence fuzzy matcher (not a stub, not a plain substring filter): query characters must appear in `target` in order but not contiguously (typing "wldr" matches "Wall draw"), scored to rank tighter/earlier matches above looser ones. Covers "synonyms" (an entry's optional `synonyms` are searched identically to its label), "result category" (`category` carried through unchanged), "disabled reason" (`disabledReason` is entry data the search neither computes nor requires).

"Accessible active-descendant handling" (section 30's own explicit requirement) is implemented per the standard combobox/listbox pattern: the text input keeps DOM focus at all times, and the currently-highlighted result is tracked via `aria-activedescendant` pointing at the highlighted `<li>`'s id — never by moving focus onto list items. "Keyboard-first": ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the highlight (wrapping), Enter invokes (and is a no-op on a disabled entry), Escape closes.

**Documented non-goals** (command-palette-search.ts's own doc comment): "recent commands" persistence (a caller passes recently-used entries first for empty-query ordering — this module has no storage), "no-result telemetry" (an analytics concern out of scope for a pure search function), "AI actions later" (literally deferred by the blueprint's own bullet).

**Evidence**: 7 unit tests (`command-palette-search.test.ts`) covering fuzzy subsequence matching, ranking, synonym matches, case-insensitivity, and empty-query ordering. Verified in real headless Chromium: opening the palette, fuzzy-searching "wldr," matching "Wall draw," invoking it via Enter, and the dialog closing correctly — with zero console errors. Full monorepo: 176 test files / 1377 tests passing.

records.title: design: create icon package
records.body:
Implemented in commit `38154a6` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

**What was built**

`scripts/generate-icon-components.mjs` reads all 40 reviewed SVGs in `design/icons/svg/` (ARQ-021/022 already verified these against `docs/design/ICON-DRAWING-CHECKLIST.md`) and generates one React component per icon into `packages/icons/src/generated/*.tsx` plus an aggregating `index.ts` — each component forwards `SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>`, keeps `stroke="currentColor"` (the icons are already themable by CSS `color`, verified by reading the source files directly), and carries the real per-icon `viewBox`/inner markup through unchanged. `packages/icons/src/index.ts` now re-exports the generated barrel instead of the previous `export {};` stub; `package.json` gained a `generate` script (`pnpm --filter @arq/icons generate`) to regenerate after any source SVG change, plus the `react`/`@types/react` deps and `"jsx": "react-jsx"` needed to typecheck the generated `.tsx` files.

This landed as part of the wider Phase 7 app-shell bootstrap (`apps/web` is now a real Vite+React app instead of a stub) so the icon package could be verified as an actual consumer, not just typechecked in isolation: `App.tsx` imports `WallIcon`/`DoorIcon` from `@arq/icons` directly, and a production `vite build` + `vite preview` was driven by real headless Chromium (Playwright) confirming both icons render (`header svg` count = 2) with zero console errors and zero failed network requests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [x] All 40 icons wired into `@arq/icons` as real importable components (not a subset, not a stub).
- [x] Regeneration is scripted and re-runnable, not a one-off hand-edit.
- [x] Consumed by a real app (`apps/web`) and verified rendering in an actual browser, not just type-checked.
- [x] Full monorepo: 31/31 packages typecheck clean, 168 test files / 1307 tests passing.
- [x] No hand-authored duplication of the SVG source of truth — the generator is the only place markup is transformed.

records.title: chore: add SBOM and licence scan
records.body:
Implemented in commit `5df8916` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

`scripts/check-dependency-licences.mjs` runs `pnpm licenses list --json` (already available - pnpm ships it, so no new dependency was added for this) against the allow-list in the new `docs/product/DEPENDENCY-AND-LICENCE-POLICY.md` (ARQ-003), fails non-zero if any package's licence is outside the allow-list or the documented reviewed-exceptions, and writes `dependency-sbom.json` (name/version/licence for every installed package - a minimal software bill of materials) as a build artifact.

Deliberately not a CycloneDX/SPDX-format SBOM generator: that would add a new dependency for a capability this repository's actual need (licence enforcement plus an auditable package/version manifest) doesn't require in that shape - the same "don't pay for headroom you haven't shown you need" reasoning ADR-0008 already applied to the 2D-vs-WebGL renderer choice.

Wired into CI as the new `dependency-licence-scan` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, uploading the SBOM as a workflow artifact on every run.

**Evidence**: ran against the real, current 195-package dependency tree - correctly identified and required handling for both compound-licence forms actually present (`(MIT OR WTFPL)`-style choices and `(MIT AND Zlib)`-style simultaneous licences), passes clean today with zero disallowed licences. `pnpm run check:dependency-licences` reproduces this locally.

records.title: docs: add dependency and licence policy
records.body:
Implemented in commit `5df8916` on `claude/arq-cad-platform-research-ba8rav`.

Found that ADR-0017 ("Dependency and licensing policy") - the only thing in the repo previously addressing this issue - was itself just an unfilled template (`Decision: Require SPDX, SBOM and legal boundaries.`, `Consequences: State technical benefits.` etc. - literal placeholder text, not an actual policy). This issue needed a real document, not a pointer to another stub.

`docs/product/DEPENDENCY-AND-LICENCE-POLICY.md`: a concrete SPDX allow-list (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-2/BSD-3/ISC/0BSD/Unlicense/CC0-1.0/Python-2.0/Zlib), explicit rules for compound licence expressions (an "OR" expression needs one allowed branch; an "AND" expression needs every branch allowed - both actually occur in this repo's real dependency tree), a documented review path for weak-copyleft exceptions (with a "Reviewed exceptions" table recording the two currently in use: `web-ifc`'s MPL-2.0, `caniuse-lite`'s CC-BY-4.0 - verified against the real dependency tree via `pnpm licenses list`, not assumed), and an explicit "never without a dedicated ADR" list for strong-copyleft/field-of-use licences (blueprint section 114, "Licence rules").

Enforced for real by `scripts/check-dependency-licences.mjs` (ARQ-016) in CI - see that issue's closing comment for the tooling evidence. Full monorepo unaffected (no source-code change): 176 test files / 1377 tests still passing, typecheck clean.

records.title: feat(UX): define canvas overlay zones and layer ownership
records.body:
Closes #412 when exact-head evidence is accepted.

## Scope

- define the documented canvas overlay-zone contract for top/bottom corners, center, selection and tool chrome;
- extend the canonical `shell-tokens.css` layer scale with workspace-overlay `95` and accessibility `98` between Context HUD `90` and modal backdrop `100`;
- pin the complete named layer order in the global layer guard;
- migrate `WorkspaceSheet` off raw z5;
- migrate tab and phone More menus off raw z6 to the canonical popover tier;
- move floating workspace panels/tablet drawers onto the workspace-overlay tier without changing panel behavior;
- preserve canvas pointer ownership with pointer-transparent zone hosts and opt-in interactive child bounds;
- add deterministic contract tests and stable overlay-role attributes for browser evidence.

## Exact integration base

`main` @ `4184551be3e75636d7feea93fda13699b00b4b43`.

Current branch is directly ahead of that head with no behind commits.

## Ownership boundary

PR #361 is still open and owns `apps/web/src/App.tsx`. This PR does not mutate `App.tsx`. The known transformed command-palette wrapper there remains an explicit external exception until #361 releases the host path.

No CAD hit testing, snapping, camera semantics, project persistence or broad shell redesign is changed.

## Canonical layer order

- raised shell: 10
- Context HUD / selection/tool chrome: 90
- workspace overlays: 95
- accessibility escape surface: 98
- modal backdrop: 100
- modal surface: 110
- popover: 120
- toast: 200

All named numeric values live in `packages/design-system/src/shell/shell-tokens.css`. Workspace CSS only consumes those names.

This makes a drawer/sheet occlude HUD chrome only where it physically covers the canvas, keeps the skip link above ordinary workspace overlays, and still leaves modal infrastructure authoritative.

## Pointer contract

`CanvasOverlayZone` hosts are always pointer-transparent. Real controls opt back in only at their bounds using `arq-canvas-overlay-control`. Full-canvas transparent hit surfaces are not introduced.

The existing wall Context HUD remains a conforming independent implementation: pointer-transparent HUD host, interactive numeric field, and browser evidence for wheel/canvas ownership.

## Evidence

`packages/design-system/src/workspace/overlay-zone-contract.test.ts` locks zone names, reserved future roles, layer ordering, pointer transparency, canonical token ownership and removal of raw sheet/menu z-index values. `packages/design-system/src/shell/layer-contract.test.ts` pins the complete global layer scale and rejects future raw escalation.

Repository-wide `format:check` has an existing seven-file documentation baseline. #412-owned files must not appear in that warning list. Final exact-head unit, Engineering Gate and Chromium evidence will be recorded on #412 before closure.

records.title: feat(ARQFS): persist live editor operations through native sessions
records.body:
Closes #355

## What changed
- route workspace wall edits, undo and redo through `NativeProjectSession.save()` whenever a native `.arq` project is open
- keep IndexedDB journaling only for the no-project/demo workspace
- refuse reference-format wall persistence rather than flattening its richer canonical model; #356 remains the semantic follow-up
- keep failed native changes visible and report the project as unsaved
- replay failed native changes through the existing session queue so later successful saves recover operation history without resurrecting superseded geometry
- advance the native journal sequence for typed operations
- report native working-copy save state distinctly from the demo journal

## Safety properties
- no native-to-demo persistence fallback
- read-only projects never queue writes
- reference-format projects never enter the flat encoder
- canonical session state still advances only after Worker acknowledgement
- failed writes do not poison the queue
- latest full wall state remains authoritative, including undo/replacement after a failed write

## Validation
Recovery branch was rebuilt from current `main` after #357. Before opening this PR:
- scoped Prettier: pass
- focused `native-project-session` + `workspace-persistence` Vitest suites: pass
- `pnpm --filter @arq/web typecheck`: pass
- repository `pnpm typecheck`: pass

Temporary recovery workflows/scripts were removed before this PR; final diff is limited to the five product/test files for #355.

records.head: c83d761b0e3ccf62936d9a816f65e8268dbe56b6

reviews.body:
Two current-head blockers before I would treat #361 as release-ready.

1. **Unsaved native edits can be lost when switching projects after a write failure.** Repro from the current control flow: a writable flat native project receives an edit; `NativeProjectSession.save()` fails, so `hasUnsavedFailure` is true and the UI reports unsaved. Both desktop `onOpenProject={() => setFileOpenPanelOpen(true)}` and mobile back/open actions still allow another project to open. `adoptNativeProject()` then swaps `nativeSessionRef` and the visible wall state immediately, calls `void previous?.close().catch(() => undefined)`, and `close()` terminates the old Worker before rejecting because `#lastWriteError` is still set. That rejection is swallowed. The failed visible operation is therefore no longer visible and the old session is gone, so acceptance criterion 3's later-save recovery path has been destroyed by an ordinary project switch. Please gate/safely coordinate project replacement while native persistence is in-flight or failed. A safe handoff must retain the old project/session when recovery is still required, or otherwise require an explicit user decision rather than silently discarding it.

2. **The PR diff is no longer the bounded five-file implementation described in its body.** Current head includes `.github/workflows/arq-355-engineering-context-refresh.yml` plus generated product-voice context files while the PR says temporary recovery workflows/scripts were removed. I understand the workflow is being used to repair the stale Engineering Gate context, but it and unrelated generated changes should not remain in the final #355 diff unless they are actually required repository artefacts for this change. Please regenerate the required engineering context, remove the one-off self-writing workflow, and re-check the final changed-file set.

The native routing, reference-format refusal and failed-write replay logic otherwise look directionally sound.

BLOCKING REVIEW. Engineering verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES.

GitHub rejected the requested `REQUEST_CHANGES` review state because the authenticated account owns this pull request (`Review Can not request changes on your own pull request`). This COMMENT is therefore the strongest review state GitHub permits from this account. It must not be interpreted as a non-blocking review.

Exact reviewed SHA: `c83d761b0e3ccf62936d9a816f65e8268dbe56b6`

Current integration base: `main` is `14d333a225d6b606a8693f85246cacadb1c93ce3`. The PR branch is currently diverged from that head, 9 commits behind and 25 commits ahead. The latest CI evidence for this PR checked this exact PR head in merge commit `afda620d2eb95e65a7ed749cfe33b30878010405` against the older base `5f965f7678a09e1fbd9a81d51778236fce682736`, so it is exact-head evidence but not current-base integration evidence.

## Current diff scope

8 files:
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/project/native-project-session.ts`
- `apps/web/src/project/native-project-session.test.ts`
- `apps/web/src/project/workspace-persistence.ts`
- `apps/web/src/project/workspace-persistence.test.ts`
- `docs/product/voice/context/REFRESH-LOG.json`
- `docs/product/voice/generated-repo-context.json`
- `engineering/ops/generated/engineering-context-v5.json`

The PR body still says the final diff is limited to five product/test files, so that description is stale and was not used as validation evidence.

## Blocking finding

### Project replacement can discard a failed native edit and suppress the only close failure that reports it

`apps/web/src/App.tsx:904-910` invalidates the old persistence revision, replaces `nativeSessionRef` with the newly opened session, then starts `previous?.close()` fire-and-forget and consumes any rejection with `.catch(() => undefined)` before the newly opened project is adopted into the visible workspace.

That is unsafe after a native write failure. `apps/web/src/project/native-project-session.ts:425-449` deliberately makes `close()` wait for the write queue, shut down the Worker/lease, and then reject if `#lastWriteError` is still present. The session also retains failed changes in `#pendingChanges` so a later save can replay them. Swallowing this rejection during project replacement destroys that recovery boundary: the old Worker/session is terminated, its pending retry state becomes unreachable, the visible workspace is replaced, and the user gets no blocking decision or preservation path for the failed edit.

This is a correctness/data-loss defect, not merely missing evidence. It violates #355's failed-write recovery and close/open transition requirements and the accepted ADR-0030 adoption/write boundaries. Do not solve it by silently falling back to the demo IndexedDB tier. Replacement must either retain/resolve the old session until it is safe, or require an explicit user decision that accurately describes the unsaved native state.

## Review questions

A. Native project edits: PASS for the core write path. Committed non-note workspace operations route through `persistWorkspaceOperation` to `NativeProjectSession.save()`. `NativeProjectSession` advances its committed snapshot/operation history only after `putArchiveEntries` resolves. I found no native-to-demo persistence fallback in this path.

B. Failure: PARTIAL / BLOCKED by the finding above. Within one live session, a failed write leaves the acknowledged snapshot unchanged, keeps pending changes, keeps the queue usable, and a later full-wall save can recover without resurrecting superseded geometry. The active shell reports an unsaved state on a failed current revision. But switching projects can discard that recovery state.

C. Read-only: PASS at the session boundary. `save()` refuses read-only projects before they enter the queue, and tests cover deterministic refusal.

D. Reference-format safety: PASS. Reference-format projects are refused before the flat wall encoder can flatten richer semantics. This is a conservative fail-closed boundary only. #361 does not steal #356's responsibility for lossless richer-model edit/round-trip semantics.

E. Undo/redo: PASS at source/unit level. Normal operation, undo and redo all use the same persistence entry point; the session queue serialises writes, failed pending changes are replayed in order, full wall state remains authoritative, and operation history advances in queue order. I found no separate native durability path for undo/redo.

F. Project identity: BLOCKED by the finding above. Worker/session identity checks and revision invalidation protect against an old completion updating the new project's save indicator, and writes are bound to the captured session. However close/open transition safety is not satisfied when the previous session has an unsaved failure.

G. Shell truth: PARTIAL. A writable native project reaches `saved` only after the persistence promise returns `persisted`, which occurs after Worker acknowledgement; failed current writes report unsaved. Demo IndexedDB journal/recovery remains separately named in browser evidence. However project replacement suppresses the previous native session's unsaved close failure. Also `App.tsx:948-955` uses the generic `unsaved-changes` save state for an initially read-only/reference project while the adjacent journal label carries the more precise reason. That state-model wording should be tightened, but the project-switch data-loss path is the blocking defect.

H. Regression boundary: PARTIAL. Demo/no-project journal recovery and native open/Worker paths have browser evidence, but current required browser evidence is not green and the product-level native open -> edit -> reopen durability path is not proven by the existing browser harness.

## Exact-head executable evidence

GitHub Actions run `34637354372` for this exact head reports:
- `pnpm format:check` PASS
- `pnpm lint` PASS
- `pnpm typecheck` PASS
- repository `pnpm test` PASS, including the current native-project-session and workspace-persistence tests
- Rust fmt/clippy/test PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:arqfs-opfs` PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:arqfs-writer-lock` PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:arqfs-project-isolation` PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:file-open` PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:journal-recovery` PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:e2e-arq-open` PASS
- `pnpm benchmark:native-open` FAIL

The native-open failure is specific: the harness reports `the panel did not say the chosen file is not written back to`. Its own limitation states that it proves open/level switching/working-copy/Worker teardown but does not prove checkpointing edits. Because that job fails, CI is red and the live #493 handoff gate is not satisfied unless the failure is explicitly reconciled/evidence-exempted by the repository's current authority.

Reviewer-local standalone filtered commands are BLOCKED in this connected review environment because it does not expose a repository execution shell. I therefore did not invent rerun results. The full exact-head `pnpm test` result above is independent Actions evidence. A browser-native `open -> edit -> failure/retry/undo/redo -> reopen` product path is also NOT PROVEN by the current harness and should be added/run before integration.

There are currently no unresolved inline review threads. I revalidated the source defect above from the current exact head rather than inheriting the earlier review comment.

## Non-blocking follow-ups

- Reconcile the three generated context files with the stated PR scope, or update the PR description so the final diff is truthful.
- Give read-only/reference projects an explicit durability state rather than overloading `unsaved-changes` for a clean baseline.
- After fixing the source blocker, update/reconcile onto current `main` and rerun the required checks against the current integration base.

## Boundary and ownership verdicts

**#356 boundary:** correct. Keep richer semantic persistence in #356; #361 should continue to refuse unsafe flattening.

**Integration-ready:** NO. There is a proven project-switch data-loss/authority defect, browser CI is red, native edit/reopen product evidence is incomplete, and the branch is behind current `main`.

**`apps/web/src/App.tsx` ownership:** NOT RELEASED. Review completion or mergeability alone does not release it. Release only after #361 is actually integrated with the blocking defect fixed and current #493/#377 handoff/ownership reconciliation records the transition, or after the PR is explicitly abandoned and ownership is reconciled.

**#369 / root UI lanes:** NOT SAFE YET. #369 may consider the root UI lanes only after #361 is integrated (or explicitly abandoned), current-main reconciliation is complete, required evidence is green/reconciled, and the ownership handoff is recorded. Do not start #407/#414/#416/#418/#420 in `App.tsx` on the basis of this review alone.

Do not merge in the current state.

records.body:
Refs #333. Stacked on review-ready PR #329.

## Scope

Exactly three additive harness files:
- `scripts/zeus-adaptive-runtime.mjs`
- `scripts/zeus-adaptive-runtime.test.mjs`

## Closed-loop behavior

Every checkpoint/finish receipt returns exactly one next action:
- `stop-success`
- `proceed`
- `re-evaluate-tier-or-evidence-plan`
- `repair`
- `block-external-evidence`

Semantics:
- executed required proof failure, authority inversion, or unsupported evidence promotion -> `repair`;
- required proof/review/protected approval/current-head evidence that never executed or is unavailable -> `block-external-evidence`;
- budget overrun or duplicate executed work -> `re-evaluate-tier-or-evidence-plan`;
- acceptance not yet proven but evidence remains valid -> `proceed`;
- acceptance plus complete required proof and no duplicate waste -> `stop-success`.

The first exact-head dedicated run executed but stopped at the repository Prettier gate before the regression suite. The workflow was temporarily allowed to apply the repository's pinned formatter to only the two runtime files, run the full runtime regression suite, and commit exactly those formatter changes. Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

Updates `react-aria-components` from 1.19.0 to 1.21.1
Release notes

Sourced from react-aria-components's releases.

React Aria Components v1.21.0

We're excited to welcome a brand new component to the family! The new NavigationTree component displays a hierarchical set of links, perfect for building sidebars and complex app navigation. It comes fully loaded with keyboard navigation, and support for nested routes.

Menu also gets a big upgrade this release: it now supports async loading and empty states! Load menu items from an API as the user scrolls with the new MenuLoadMoreItem and use renderEmptyState to show an indicator when data is loading or when the menu is empty.

Full Release Notes

React Aria Components v1.20.0

This release includes many new components and features!

  • The new PreviewTrigger component shows a Popover on hover, focus, or long press. Unlike Tooltip, it may include interactive content, useful for hoverable link previews.
  • TokenField (alpha) allows users to enter text with inline tokens. Use it to build AI prompt fields, tag inputs, structured search fields, mention inputs, and multi-select comboboxes.
  • MenuTrigger now supports trigger="contextMenu", enabling accessible context menus via mouse, keyboard, and touch input.
  • A simpler API to implement keyboard shortcuts to useKeyboard.
  • Support for interactive components like textfields inside Table rows.

Finally, the React Aria and React Stately hook documentation has been completely rewritten! The new docs use the same styles as our React Aria Components examples, and show how to use both components and hooks together.

Full Release Notes

records.title: Zeus 5: the reading, the plan loop, the spec compiler, and seven dead scripts wired
records.body:
Five rounds of work on Zeus. Full handoff: `docs/ZEUS-PRIME-INTEGRATION.md`. Phase 0 reading of the repository: `docs/ZEUS-PRIME-INVENTORY.md`.

State: **green, with four disclosed limits.** Not "perfect".

## Problem

Zeus documented a great deal it could not actually do, and could not tell when a claim was a memory.

1. **Nothing Zeus learned reached a later turn.** `.zeus/eval-log.jsonl` was written by one script, read only by a stats printer, had no lesson field, and was empty.
2. **"Verified" was a memory.** Nothing recorded which gate ran, at which round, against which version of the tree.
3. **"Implemented" was a memory too.** Nothing held the work items, so a six-item request reported finished after four left no artifact saying so.
4. **The always-on core had no drift check.** Nothing proved the kernel stayed a faithful subset of the doctrine it compresses.
5. **7 of 39 Zeus scripts could be run by nothing** — no CLI verb, no package script, no hook, no CI step, no importer. Among them the entire delivery pipeline (`zeus-run-state.mjs`), the role planner, the merge guard and the release watcher.
6. **8 of 10 plainly-UI requests routed to no visual module**, so they got no visual requirements, no UI contract and no accessibility reviewer.
7. **Zeus never said what it thought a request meant**, so a misread surfaced only after the work.

## Solution

**The reading, shown before the work.** Every actionable turn opens with how Zeus read the request, what it deliberately did *not* read it as, every inference it made, and the operator's words quoted back unedited — rendered before any classification field, because that is the line that catches a misread. It restates; it never rewrites the request into different words and acts on those. Deterministic and offline: it runs in the hook on every prompt.

**Plan ledger** (`pnpm zeus:plan`). The work items. An item is done only with a command and a zero exit code; `close` refuses while any item is pending, active or blocked, and names each one. That refusal is the loop.

**Spec compiler** (`zeus spec`). A request turned into something precise enough to implement: the routed modules' own requirement prose, the acceptance criteria, the owning role, the checks. It **never invents intent** — everything it cannot derive is a `TODO`, and `spec --check` refuses the file while one remains. For UI work it emits the twelve dimensions `zeus visual-contract` requires as questions, so a generated skeleton cannot satisfy that lint by shape alone.

**Gate ledger** (`pnpm zeus:gate`). Gate results bound to the workspace fingerprint `zeus-fingerprint.mjs` already computed. A failed gate is never skippable; rounds are bounded by the tier's `repairRounds`; `ship` refuses without the repository gate set and, where risk or radius requires review, **a passing review for every reviewer the changed paths call for** — not merely one. Where the paths resolve to no reviewer, a count applies instead: two independent reviews at high risk and above. Derived beats chosen: two reviews by the wrong two specialists satisfy a count and fail this.

**Continual harness** (`pnpm zeus:harness`, proposed by `/zeus-refine`). Supplemental learned state with mandatory evidence, injected into every turn under a character budget, every mutation one rollback away within a 5-refinement window.

**Drift guards** (`pnpm zeus:drift`). The kernel still names every mode, tier, blast radius level, reversibility, evidence state and configured budget; the hook still *runs* the harness; every slash command is skipped; **every Zeus script is reachable**; the published saving is still true.

**Seven dead scripts wired**, plus the org chart: `.zeus/role-registry.json` defined 14 roles and was read by nothing while the engine carried its own copy of the module-to-role map. The registry now owns it and validation enforces it.

**UI routing fixed.** `ui-visual` went from 13 tokens of design-system language to 45 tokens and 16 phrases: 10/10 hit, 0/10 over-match against controls, pinned by 13 regression cases of which 8 fail against the old vocabulary.

## Non-goals

- prime-agent's runtime, daemon, agent-to-agent messaging and bounded autonomous mode. Autonomy is the repository owner's decision, not an agent's.
- A gate runner that executes commands. The ledgers record a claim about a check, not the check.
- Supabase. It is not in this codebase; only `database/` design artifacts exist.

## Tests

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test` | 4075 tests (baseline 3907; +168, zero failures either side) |
| `pnpm typecheck` | 37 of 37 |
| `pnpm lint` | `eslint .`, no output |
| `pnpm format:check` | clean |
| `pnpm build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm zeus:test` | green |
| `node scripts/zeus-drift-guard-test.mjs` | 24 cases, each guard broken on purpose |
| `node scripts/zeus-classification-test.mjs` | 29 cases |
| `pnpm engineering:context:verify` / `:workflows` / `:policy` | green |

`vitest.config.ts` collects `scripts/**/*.test.ts`, and `ci.yml` runs the drift-guard regression suite, `zeus:drift` and `zeus:validate` in `lint-and-typecheck`. The guard test runs first, on the same principle as `check:decision-ids:test`: a verifier that cannot fail would report a clean repository either way.

**Every new guard was broken on purpose.** Weakening `HARNESS_INVOCATION` to a filename match fails 2 of 24 drift cases, which is how the invocation match is proven to be doing the work.

**Thirty tests were run against deliberately un-fixed modules and all failed as they should.** Five tautologies were caught this way and fixed — including one in the probe that runs those checks, whose import rewrite matched nothing so every run had used the fixed module, and one where a comment explaining the trap re-created it by naming the probe file.

## Performance effect

The hook spawns one extra `node` process per actionable prompt. The harness block is bounded at 1,200 characters. `.zeus/FAST-KERNEL.md` grew from 4,871 to 7,994 bytes and is 84.3% smaller than the doctrine set it compresses; the published floor was lowered from 85% to 80% when the drift guard refused the claim at 84.3%. The harness store was measured at 2,385 KB after 80 ordinary refinements carrying 24 KB of state; bounding the snapshot window brought the same load to 254 KB.

## Accessibility effect

None directly — no product surface is touched. Indirectly positive: UI requests now reach `arq-ux-accessibility-reviewer` and carry the twelve-dimension visual contract, which 8 of 10 previously did not.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq` reader, writer, schema version or migration path is touched. New state under `.zeus/`: `harness/state.json` is tracked (learned state is human-committed); `gates/` and `plans/` are gitignored, because a result bound to a fingerprint means nothing in another checkout.

## Dependency and licence effect

No dependency added or changed; `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched. Ideas from `PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent`, MIT, attributed in each module that carries one.

## Security and privacy effect

- Harness entries are scanned for secret shapes and refused; a labelled git object id stays citable, because the evidence rule asks for a commit and the long-hex rule must not then reject one.
- Entry text reaches the hook's output but is only ever carried as a shell variable and printed; bash does not re-scan a variable expansion, so `$(...)` inside an entry stays literal. That property is load-bearing and commented as such.
- `install-zeus.sh` excludes `.zeus/harness/` and `.zeus/gates/`, so installing Zeus elsewhere cannot carry this repository's learned state across.
- The review gate refuses a reviewer name no dispatchable agent could have run, removing the "record `review:me-the-author`, then ship" path at every risk tier.
- `.claude/hooks/**` and `.claude/settings.json` now route to `security` as well as `architecture`.

## Rollback

`git revert` of the merge restores the previous behaviour completely; nothing is compensable or irreversible. The hook degrades safely on its own: every path exits 0, and a corrupt harness store produces a visible warning with 0 bytes on stderr rather than a blocked turn (reproduced with both a malformed and a truncated store). Learned entries roll back individually, including a rollback of a rollback, within the window; beyond it the store is tracked, so git holds the history.

## What is NOT done

1. **No independent reviewer was dispatched.** This session was forbidden from using the Agent tool. Classifying Zeus's own surface changed this diff to **high risk, `production` blast radius**, and `pnpm zeus:gate ship` refuses it by name: `arq-architecture-reviewer`, `arq-release-reviewer` and `arq-security-ai-reviewer` have not passed. That refusal was left standing and red rather than satisfied with a recorded review that never happened. The merge proceeds on the repository owner's explicit instruction, with `engineering-gate` — which `CLAUDE.md` names as the actual merge authority, Zeus being advisory — green on the head commit. **Dispatching those three reviewers against the merged head remains outstanding work.**
2. **Every gate is self-attested.** Recording `typecheck --outcome pass` does not run `tsc`.
3. **`pnpm zeus:test` still does not run in CI**, because it asserts a p95 compile time under 20 ms that would flake on a shared runner. The drift guards, `zeus:validate` and the 147 Zeus tests do run.
4. **The reviewer match is only as good as the impact map.** An uncovered path yields `matched: false` and falls back to a count: fail-closed, but weaker than a match.

## Open questions

1. **Does the agent operating system deserve its own blast radius level?** `.zeus/`, `scripts/zeus-*` and `.claude/` are classified at `product` radius, which closes the fail-open. But `product` means "user-visible product behaviour across packages", and that is not what these files are. A seventh level would describe them honestly and would renumber a scale `zeus-validate.mjs` requires to be contiguous. That is a vocabulary decision.
2. **How much autonomy should the loop have?** The machinery that makes an autonomous loop safe is built — deterministic next-item, mandatory evidence, a refusal to close early. Unbounded self-continuation is deliberately not built.
3. **Should Arq have a Supabase backend at all?** There is none today.

Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41989 [Regression]: tsconfig "extends" bare specifier isn't resolved via node_modules walk-up like tsc (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41998 [Regression]: directory-form tsconfig project references ("path": "../pkg") fail to resolve (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41985 Accessibility snapshot drops button name when text is nested inside spans with aria-hidden SVG
  • #42000 [Regression]: page.evaluate() arg of a branded primitive type (string & { brand }) no longer type-checks since 1.62
  • #42013 [BUG]Image-type actionable elements are not presented in the snapshot.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });
await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.
await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

Dexie v4.4.5

This is a maintenance release that fixes an issue with indexes named after inherited Object properties and improves authentication recovery in dexie-cloud-addon.

Related Package Releases

Bug Fixes

dexie@4.4.5

  • fix: don't crash when an index is named constructor — Tables with a primary key or index named constructor could cause db.open() to fail with TypeError: indexList.push is not a function. The internal index lookup now uses an object without a prototype, avoiding collisions with inherited Object.prototype properties such as constructor, toString, and valueOf. (#2325, fixes #1920). Contributed by @​tarann26.

dexie-cloud-addon@4.4.14

  • fix: recover from failed refresh-token renewal — When a locally unexpired refresh token is rejected by the server, login() now falls back to the regular fetchTokens authentication path instead of propagating the refresh error. This allows custom authentication integrations to silently obtain new tokens when possible, or trigger their normal login flow when required. OAuth redirect errors continue to propagate normally. (#2326). Fixed by @​liz709 and @​dfahlander.
