records.title: Make Zeus echo the real per-prompt contract, not a generic reminder
records.body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #224 (merged). After Zeus was wired in, the `UserPromptSubmit` hook (`scripts/zeus-hook.sh`) printed the exact same static one-line reminder — `[ZEUS 4 INTERNAL] Load FAST-KERNEL only; route modules; ...` — on every single actionable prompt, regardless of what the prompt actually was. It was visible in the transcript, but useless as visibility: it never showed what Zeus actually decided for that specific prompt (classification, routing, acceptance criteria), so there was no way to see "the updated prompt" Zeus produced.

## Solution

The hook now runs the real compiler (`node scripts/zeus-fast-compile.mjs --task "<the prompt>"`) and echoes its actual markdown output back into the conversation for every actionable prompt: mode / risk / tier / delivery stop, owner and reviewers, routed modules, acceptance criteria, and checks. Falls back to the old static line only if the compile step itself fails (e.g. `node` unavailable), so the hook can never go silently broken.

Updated `CLAUDE.md`'s description of the hook to match the real behavior, and updated `test-zeus-hook.sh`'s assertion to check for the new output signature (`Zeus 4 Compact Contract`) instead of the old static string.

## Non-goals

- No change to the classification/routing logic itself (`scripts/lib/zeus-engine.mjs`) — only to what the hook surfaces.
- No change to acknowledgement/`/zeus-*`/webhook silencing — verified those still produce no output.
- No application code changes.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this is a CLI/hook text-output change, not a UI change. Example of new output for an actionable prompt:

```
Zeus 4 routed this prompt:
# Zeus 4 Compact Contract

**Mode / risk / tier / stop:** implement / moderate / standard / local-green
**Owner:** geometry-bim
**Modules:** geometry, arqfs

**Acceptance**
- [ ] authoritative current state inspected
- [ ] requested success and failure paths work
- [ ] applicable Arq invariants remain satisfied
- [ ] local-green has current evidence
- [ ] integrity, recovery and source-preservation evidence passes

**Checks**
- ranked context retrieval
- impact-selected focused checks
- actual output inspection
- affected package quality checks
- independent critique pass
```

## Tests

- `bash scripts/test-zeus-hook.sh` → passes with the updated assertion.
- `bash scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` (from source package) → full suite passes.
- Manually piped fast/standard/deep-tier prompts through the hook and confirmed each produces its own distinct, accurate contract (different owner/modules/checks per tier and risk).
- Manually confirmed `ok`, `/zeus-audit ...`, and webhook/task-notification payloads still produce no output.
- `node scripts/zeus.mjs verify` and `node scripts/zeus.mjs benchmark --root .` still green.

## Performance effect

Adds one `node` process invocation (the compiler) per actionable prompt inside the hook. Measured compile step is sub-millisecond in-process; the dominant cost is Node startup (tens of ms), which is negligible for a once-per-prompt hook.

## Accessibility effect

None.

## Project format and migration effect

None.

## Dependency and licence effect

None.

## Security and privacy effect

None — the compiler only reads the prompt text already available to the hook and repo-local config; no new external calls.

## Rollback

Revert this commit; the hook falls back to the prior static-reminder behavior.

---

records.title: Install Zeus 4.0 prompt operating system
records.body:
## Problem

Arq had no structured prompt-operating layer for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex/AGENTS). Ad hoc prompting risks assumption-driven changes to protected areas: semantic BIM model integrity, `.arq` file/migration safety, renderer independence, geometry correctness, sync, and accessibility.

## Solution

Installs the Zeus 4.0 Instant Execution System, a silent-first prompt operating system built around a small Fast Kernel (`.zeus/FAST-KERNEL.md`):

- Classifies requests into fast/standard/deep execution tiers by risk and scope, routing to at most 1/4/8 domain modules under `.zeus/modules/` (geometry, arqfs, security, ui-visual, rendering, accessibility, ai, architecture, interoperability, github-cicd, incident, release-production).
- Builds an incremental, gitignored project index (`.zeus/cache/`) for ranked context retrieval instead of reading whole files/repo by default.
- Runs an adaptive check ladder (focused → affected package → repository gate → CI → deployment → production) via a unified CLI, `scripts/zeus.mjs` (compile/route/index/context/impact/check/status/release/benchmark/verify).
- Wires into Claude Code (`.claude/`), Cursor (`.cursor/`), Codex/generic agents (`AGENTS.md`), and GitHub Copilot (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
- Ships an installer/uninstaller, hook tests, prompt-compiler self-tests, architecture/security lint fixtures, and an evaluation recorder.

Installed via the package's own `scripts/install-zeus.sh`, which is purely additive here — no existing repository files were overwritten (verified: no filename collisions with existing `docs/`, `scripts/`, or `examples/` content, and `AGENTS.md`/root `README.md` did not previously exist or were not touched).

## Non-goals

- Does not change any Arq application code, build, or runtime behavior.
- Does not perform any GitHub write beyond this PR (merge/deploy tooling is included but reports `blocked` rather than fabricating success, since no `gh` CLI/authorization is available in this environment).
- Does not modify the existing `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, or any pre-existing `docs/`, `scripts/`, or `examples/` files.

## Visual evidence

records.title: Add final ARQ brand assets and wire them into the prototype
records.body:
## Problem

The repo had no finalized logo, favicon, or brand asset files, and the static prototype used a bare, unbranded `<head>`.

## Solution

- Added the final ARQ brand package under `brand/`: vector logos (SVG/PDF), 4K transparent PNGs, web assets (favicons, PWA icons, manifest, Open Graph image), 1024px app icon sources, and CMYK print PDFs, plus the two brand guideline PDFs.
- Wired the web assets into `prototype/index.html`: favicon (SVG + ICO), apple-touch-icon, web manifest, `theme-color` meta (Phthalo Green `#0B6B50`), and Open Graph/Twitter card meta tags pointing at the new OG image.
- Updated `prototype/site.webmanifest` to use paths relative to the prototype directory.
- Documented the new assets and primary colours/minimum sizes in `marketing/BRAND-VOICE.md`, and added `brand/` to the key-directories list in `README.md`.

## Non-goals

No changes to product code, design tokens, or the technical icon set in `design/`.

## Visual evidence

Verified locally by serving `prototype/` and confirming `index.html`, `favicon.svg`, `site.webmanifest`, and the Open Graph image all return HTTP 200.

## Tests

N/A (static assets and markup only).

## Performance effect

None outside the prototype; new binary assets (~2.4 MB total) added to the repository.

## Accessibility effect

None.

## Project format and migration effect

None.

## Dependency and licence effect

None.

## Security and privacy effect

None.

## Rollback

Revert this commit; no other code depends on the new `brand/` directory or the prototype's added asset files.

records.body:
# design: differentiate component doc content per component

**Issue ID:** ARQ-190
**Phase:** Phase 0
**Epic:** Design system
**Priority:** high
**Suggested labels:** type: docs, area: design, priority: high, state: ready
**Dependencies:** ARQ-177

## Problem

All 84 files in `docs/components/` share byte-identical content after the "Purpose"
line (verified programmatically: `CMP-001-button.md` and `CMP-016-checkbox.md`, and
every other pair, are identical from "## Anatomy" onward). The same problem existed
for the 57 page specs in `docs/pages/` and was fixed under ARQ-175 with four
category-specific templates (PUB/AUTH/APP/PROJ). Components need the same treatment,
but per-component rather than per-category, since a Button and a Canvas have almost
nothing in common beyond both being "components."

## Scope

For each of the 84 components in `docs/components/COMPONENT-MAP.csv`, replace the
generic "Anatomy / Required states / Behaviour / Sizing / Keyboard and accessibility
/ Acceptance criteria" boilerplate with content specific to that component - what it
actually is, which states genuinely apply to it (a Toast doesn't have a meaningful
"Selected" state; a Canvas doesn't have "Hover" in the button sense), and its real
keyboard/accessibility contract (a Data table's keyboard model is not a Button's).

`component-harness/components.js` (ARQ-177) already has a `renderer` field per
component classifying ~40 of the 84 as mapping to simple native controls and ~44 as
layout chrome or engine-dependent - that classification is a reasonable starting
point for grouping this work, not a reason to skip it.

## Non-goals

- Do not expand into full visual mockups (that's ARQ-175/176's territory, not this).
- Do not introduce a frontend framework choice while doing this - it's a content fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No two component docs are byte-identical after "Purpose" unless they are
      genuinely the same kind of control with no meaningful difference.
- [ ] Required states reflect what actually applies to each component, not a
      copy-pasted universal list.
- [ ] `component-harness/components.js` states arrays are regenerated from the
      corrected docs and the harness still renders without errors.

## Evidence

Programmatic diff showing all 84 files are byte-identical after "Purpose" (same
method used to verify the ARQ-175 finding for pages).

# editor: implement centre and nearest snap

**Issue ID:** ARQ-191
**Phase:** Phase 1
**Epic:** Editor interaction
**Priority:** high
**Suggested labels:** type: feature, area: editor, priority: high, state: done
**Dependencies:** ARQ-052, ARQ-192

## Problem

`docs/ux/SELECTION-AND-SNAPPING.md` lists eight snap sources. ARQ-046 through ARQ-052
covered Endpoint, Midpoint, Intersection, Perpendicular, Grid, Extension and their
tie-break behaviour. Centre and Nearest remained missing.

## Scope

- Nearest snap returns the closest point on a segment to the cursor, valid within or
  beyond the segment bounds through endpoint clamping.
- Centre snap returns the authored centre of a valid circle or the parent-circle
  centre of a valid arc through `CircularCandidate`.
- Rectangular bounding-box centres remain out of scope.

## Non-goals

- Do not expand into later release scope.
- Do not introduce unreviewed dependencies.
- Do not couple project semantics to renderer or external-format classes.
- Do not introduce canonical circle or arc BIM entities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The scope and non-goals are documented.
- [x] Nearest snap is implemented against `SegmentCandidate` with tests.
- [x] Circular candidate geometry is split into ARQ-192.
- [x] Centre snap is implemented against `CircularCandidate` with tests.
- [x] Escape and Enter behaviour matches the other snap sources.
- [x] Invalid input produces no snap preview and leaves committed state unchanged.

records.body:
# editor: define circular snap candidate

**Issue ID:** ARQ-192
**Phase:** Phase 1
**Epic:** Editor interaction
**Priority:** high
**Suggested labels:** type: feature, area: editor, priority: high, state: done
**Dependencies:** ARQ-045

## Problem

ARQ-191 intentionally left Centre snap incomplete because the editor had no
renderer-independent closed-shape candidate contract. Only open `SegmentCandidate`
and point-like `EndpointCandidate` existed, so Centre snap could not be implemented
without first defining a clean candidate boundary.

## Scope

- Add a minimal `CircularCandidate` contract for circles and arcs.
- Store only shape kind, world-space centre and radius.
- Keep the contract independent of renderer, BIM element and import-format classes.
- Detect invalid non-finite centres and non-positive or non-finite radii.
- Export the contract from `@arq/editor-shell`.

## Non-goals

- Do not introduce canonical circle or arc BIM entities.
- Do not define rectangular bounding-box centres.
- Do not add renderer ownership or stable project IDs to snap candidates.
- Do not resolve the canonical project-unit ADR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `CircularCandidate` supports circle and arc candidates.
- [x] Invalid candidates are detectable without mutating project state.
- [x] The contract is exported by `@arq/editor-shell`.
- [x] Centre snap consumes it without renderer or BIM dependencies.
- [x] Focused type and runtime checks pass.
